method.prereg: Families (sector-neutral percentile ranks → average within family → average across families, equal weights): - Q Quality: gross profit/assets, ROE (TTM), operating cash flow/assets, accruals (−), leverage (−), asset growth (−), net share issuance (−) - V Value: earnings yield (TTM), free-cash-flow yield, EBIT/EV, book/price - M Momentum: 12-1 month total return - S Earnings momentum: SUE (latest quarterly diluted EPS YoY change ÷ std of prior 8 YoY changes) Composite = mean(Q, V, M, S). Rebalance monthly; signal at month-end t uses only data filed ≤ t; 10 bps one-way costs. Variants reported (not selected on results): QVM only; each family alone; v3 conviction proxy; v2 composite. Risk (volatility) is a constraint, not a return driver. Live-only overlays (analyst revisions, NTM valuation) are tie-breakers/red flags only because no point-in-time history exists for them.

limits: No stock-selection edge was found (2012–2026); the stock sleeve is therefore sized as a bounded satellite and assumed to have zero alpha in every probability shown.
Free price data lacks many delisted companies (coverage 69–93% by era); measured bias +1.0 pt/yr vs the real equal-weight ETF, disclosed with every backtest number.

Probabilities are conditional on the Bear/Base/Bull market scenarios and on history being a fair guide to volatility and crashes; they are not guarantees.
The lead's early triage file had a stale-XBRL-tag bug (110 rows); it only ordered the diligence queue — see the error log (v4/outputs/lead_error_log.md).

The backtest starts in 2012 because as-filed XBRL fundamentals begin in 2009–2011, so the model history excludes 2008; the stress tests replay 2007–09 for today's sleeve on prices only.

Simulations rebalance to the target mix daily (the B2 method), a simplification against the quarterly rule; the crisis replays use quarterly rebalancing. Results are insensitive to the bootstrap block length (5, 21 or 63 days).

glossary: Index fund (UCITS, Irish-domiciled)
a fund that simply owns all S&P 500 companies. The Irish legal wrapper keeps it outside US estate tax and halves the US tax on its dividends.
T-bill
a short-term US government IOU (3–12 months). It is the closest thing to risk-free cash in dollars and currently pays about 4% a year.
Satellite / sleeve
the small part of the portfolio held in individual stocks, next to the index core.
Backtest
replaying a rule on past data to see how it would have done.
Point-in-time
using only what was knowable on each past date: the companies actually in the index then, and the accounts filed by then.
Look-ahead and survivorship bias
the two classic backtest cheats. Look-ahead uses information that was not yet public. Survivorship tests only today's winners and forgets the companies that shrank, were bought or went bust.
Pre-registered
the model was written down and frozen before any test was run, so it could not be tuned to the answer.
Pts/yr (percentage points a year)
the difference between two annual returns, e.g. 12.5% vs 15.1% is −2.6 pts/yr.
t-stat
how many standard errors a result sits from zero. Between −2 and +2 means "could easily be luck".
95% range (confidence interval)
the band that would contain the true value in 95 of 100 repeats of the experiment.
Volatility
how much a price typically swings in a year (one standard deviation, as a %).
Tracking error
how far a portfolio's yearly return typically strays from the index, in either direction.
Beta
how much a stock or portfolio tends to move when the index moves 1% (a beta of 0.8 means about 0.8%).
Drawdown / worst fall
the largest fall from a previous high to a later low, before recovering.
Stress replay
re-running today's holdings through a past crisis (e.g. 2008, 2020) on daily prices.
Stationary bootstrap
a simulation that builds thousands of possible futures by stitching together random blocks of real past days. It keeps the real clustering of good and bad days.
Scenario (bear / base / bull)
an assumed long-run market return of 2% / 6% / 9% a year. The odds in this report are conditional on the scenario.
Calibrated odds / base rate
how often something actually happened historically to stocks like this one (same score band and volatility). It is not a forecast for the specific stock.
NTM P/E
share price divided by the next twelve months of expected earnings per share. Lower means cheaper per dollar of profit.
P/FFO
the REIT version of P/E. FFO (funds from operations) adds back property depreciation, which overstates real costs for landlords.
P/B and justified P/B
price relative to book value (net assets), used for banks and insurers. The justified P/B is what the return on equity supports.
Reverse DCF
instead of forecasting cash flows to get a price, start from today's price and solve for the growth the market is assuming. Then ask whether that growth is plausible.
Own-history percentile
where today's valuation sits within the company's own past range (0 = cheapest ever, 100 = dearest).
Kill criterion
a measurable condition, written in advance, that means the investment case is broken and the stock is sold.
INCLUDE / INCLUDE-SMALL
the diligence verdict. INCLUDE is held at full weight (up to 10% of the sleeve). INCLUDE-SMALL is investable with a named reservation and held at half weight (up to 5%).
US-situs
an asset the US treats as located in the US for estate tax (US shares and US-domiciled ETFs). Irish UCITS funds are not US-situs.
Withholding tax
tax taken at source from dividends before you receive them: 30% for a UAE resident on US shares, 15% inside an Irish fund.

impl.lede: General information for a UAE-resident (non-US) investor, with primary sources. Confirm specifics with a qualified cross-border tax adviser.
facts: US estate tax on US-situs assets
Non-US persons get a $13,000 credit ≈ $60,000 exemption (not indexed); rates 18–40%; Form 706-NA above $60k. No US–UAE estate treaty. Illustrative tax: $80k → $5,200; $100k → $10,800.
30% for UAE residents (no US–UAE income-tax treaty; W-8BEN does not reduce it). Capital gains generally not US-taxed.
No personal income tax; Cabinet Decision 49/2023 keeps personal investment income outside UAE Corporate Tax.

CSPX / VUAA / SPY5 (physical, 15% withholding inside the fund) and SPXS (swap, ~0% withholding, counterparty risk) are not US-situs. All-in annual tax drag at a 1.11% yield: VOO 0.36%, CSPX/VUAA 0.24%, SPY5 0.20%, SPXS 0.12%.

IBKR: US stocks ~$0.005/share (min $1); LSE ETFs 0.05% of value; no inactivity fee. Vested: 0.25% per trade (max $35), US stocks/ETFs only, clears via DriveWealth (US-situs), and appears to onboard only Indian-origin (PAN/NRI) clients — check eligibility (R3).
Which IBKR entity holds a UAE account

UAE residents are onboarded by Interactive Brokers (U.K.) Ltd, DIFC Branch (DFSA Category 4, an arranging broker); custody sits with Interactive Brokers LLC in the US, so SIPC protection applies (not FSCS). Verified on IBKR's own pages, 26 Sep 2026 (R3).
Open items only a broker or adviser can settle

Marked permanently open, each with a workaround. (1) Estate-tax situs of idle cash at a US broker: keep the reserve in T-bills or a UCITS T-bill fund such as IB01, not as a large broker cash balance. (2) Fractional units of CSPX/VUAA at IBKR: the order ticket shows whether "cash quantity" is offered; otherwise buy whole units (VUAA about $149 a unit at its 24 Sep NAV). (3) IBKR market-data fees: optional; delayed quotes are free.
The Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA) became the Capital Market Authority (CMA) on 1 Jan 2026 (Federal Laws 32 and 33 of 2025). Sarwa is regulated by the ADGM FSRA (R3).
Individual US stocks cannot be wrapped in UCITS, so a stock-picking sleeve is US-situs; keeping it near or below ~$60k limits estate-tax exposure, while the index core can sit in a UCITS fund.
rules: Hold broad US exposure in an Irish-domiciled UCITS S&P 500 fund (not US-situs, 15% fund-level dividend withholding) and the v4 stocks as a satellite. The satellite is where the research can add return; the core is where the 90%-over-10-years confidence actually lives.

Buy in three equal tranches about three weeks apart. Use limit orders near the last close and never buy a stock in the two trading days before its earnings date. In Dubai time the US market is open 17:30–00:00 while US daylight saving applies (early March to early November) and 18:30–01:00 otherwise.

Re-run the model each quarter. Sell a holding only if it falls out of the top quarter of the ranking or a kill criterion fires. Trim any position above 1.5× its target weight. Most weeks the right action is no trade.

Each holding has 3–5 measurable exit triggers in its dossier (for example, a guidance cut plus a >10% fall in next-year EPS estimates, leverage above a stated level, or a thesis-breaking event). If one fires, exit at the next review; if none fires, price moves alone are not a reason to sell.

A −10% portfolio fall triggers a review of every thesis; −15% a review of the equity/reserve mix; −20% means the stated tolerance is reached. Stop orders are not used: gaps can fill far below the trigger.
Know what would change the view

Fold the satellite into the index if it trails the S&P 500 by more than 20 points over 24 months (about a 1-in-8 outcome if it has no edge, given its 11% tracking error). Revisit the design if a quarterly re-run replaces more than half the names or a data audit finds a material error.
weekly: Open the dashboard: note the week's moves for the portfolio, the S&P 500 and each holding (2 min).
Check whether any holding reported earnings or issued guidance this week; compare with its kill criteria in the dossier tab (10 min).
Check the news list for holdings for M&A, regulatory action, management changes or accounting issues (5 min).
Check weights against targets: act only if a position exceeds 1.5× target or a kill criterion fired (3 min).
Record the decision, including "no trade", in the decision log with the date and reason (5 min).
Quarter-end weeks only: re-run the model and review the replacement list before trading (extra 30 min).

hero.title: Your all-stock portfolio: 20 researched companies chosen from the whole S&P 500.
hero.lede: You asked for an all-stock portfolio chosen from the whole S&P 500. Every company got a quick research pass; 178 got full SEC-filing research so far. The 20 stocks held are the best of 116 that passed every test: good businesses whose price does not assume more growth than the evidence supports. That rule keeps out Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Apple at today's prices. Honest odds: no rule tested here beat the S&P 500 over 2012–2026, so treat beating it as a coin flip, not a promise. The price of going all-stock is risk: the 20 fell −56% in the 2007–09 replay.
tiles: chance of a gain over 5 years (base case)
chance of beating the S&P 500 over 5 years (no assumed edge)
independent bets, once co-movement is counted

answer.v: Hold the 20 stocks at the weights in the table, with no index fund or T-bills. In past crises they fell −56% in the 2007–09 replay (S&P 500 −55%), −37% in the COVID crash and −16% in 2022. Base case: 76% chance of a gain over 5 years, a coin flip to beat the S&P 500, and 91% chance of a fall worse than 20% at some point. Fewer than 12–15 names adds single-company risk. Direct US shares count toward the ~$60k US estate-tax threshold for non-US persons. 30% of US dividends is withheld: about 0.52% of the portfolio a year on its 1.7% yield. Research, not advice.

answer.k: If you want less risk later: what to own
answer.v: An S&P 500 UCITS fund (e.g. CSPX or VUAA, Irish-domiciled: no US estate tax, 15% dividend withholding) as the core; T-bills or a UCITS T-bill fund as the reserve; the stock satellite at no more than 15–20% of the total (any part of the satellite the caps cannot fill also goes into the index fund).

answer.k: If you want less risk later: how much in each
answer.v: This depends on your drawdown limit. Moderate 55/15/30: 87% chance of a gain over 5 years, 52% chance of a fall worse than 20% at some point. Cautious 35/10/55: 94% and 13%. Index only: 80% and 81%. In a 2008-style crash even the Cautious mix fell −27%; a limit that must hold then needs about 34% or less in equities. Defensive 15/10/75 (the equity budget of Codex's release v005): 99% and under 1%; it fell −14% in the 2008 replay. Your call; this is scenario analysis, not advice.

answer.k: What to expect from the stocks
answer.v: Roughly index-like returns, give or take about 11% a year. The honest odds for each name: 65–70% chance of a gain over a year, 43–46% chance of beating the index. Every holding has written exit triggers.

A satellite that trails the S&P 500 by more than 20 points over 24 months (fold it into the index); a kill criterion firing on a holding; a new quarter's model re-run replacing more than half the names.

rows.thesis: Premium closed-loop card network with best-in-class, stable credit quality and strong EPS growth, priced for less growth than it is delivering.

val_consistency.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for AXP (not a prior top-70/lane name); this dossier's own reverse DCF (cost of equity ~9.5% via CAPM, terminal growth 3%) implies only ~5.1%/yr 10-year earnings growth, well below AXP's demonstrated trailing four-quarter EPS growth of 8-19% YoY and below management's long-communicated mid-teens EPS growth aspiration, so the price appears to embed less growth than the base case.

kill: Organic recurring subscription Run Rate growth falls below 6% for two consecutive quarters (currently 8.1%, Q2 2026).

Company-wide Retention Rate falls below 92% for two consecutive quarters (currently 95.3%, Q2 2026; 93.4% a year ago in Q4 2025 -- the metric itself has some seasonal/measurement noise, so two-quarter persistence is the trigger).
Net debt/Adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.5x (currently ~2.8-2.9x).
Asset-based fee Run Rate growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (a direct read on AUM-linked revenue sensitivity to a market downturn).
FY guidance is cut (as opposed to raised/reaffirmed) at any subsequent quarterly release -- track record is currently initiate -> reaffirm -> raise.
adverse: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS fell 2.3% YoY (to $3.81) even as Adjusted EPS rose 11.5% (to $4.66) -- driven by higher interest expense on higher debt and an $11.8m write-off of a minority investee.

Q1 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $5.53 includes an $88m one-off tax benefit from an internal legal-entity restructuring, explicitly excluded from adjusted guidance metrics -- the headline GAAP number overstates underlying run-rate earnings growth.
Weighted-average diluted share count down 5.9% YoY on buybacks that are partly debt-funded; total debt has risen even as buybacks continue.
rows.thesis: Runs the benchmark indexes trillions of dollars track; raised cash-flow guidance on real growth, priced for less than it's delivering.

val_consistency.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MSCI in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict is null. This dossier's own reverse DCF (EV ~$46.2bn = $40.08bn market cap + $6.475bn debt - $0.353bn cash; FY2026 guided FCF midpoint $1,515m; r=9.0%; terminal growth 3.5%) implies a ~9.7% ten-year FCF CAGR, at or slightly below the ~10-11% evidence-based base case (organic operating-revenue growth has run 10-12% for six straight quarters) -- fair to modestly attractive, not priced for excess.

Net premiums earned growth turns negative YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Companywide policies-in-force growth turns negative YoY.
A second state imposes a profit-cap policyholder-credit resulting in a single-quarter charge >$500M.
Debt-to-total-capital ratio exceeds the company's own 30% policy ceiling.
adverse: A Florida statutory profit cap on personal-auto insurance forced a $950M one-time 'policyholder credit' accrual in September 2025, payable to ~2.7M Florida policyholders in early 2026; this mechanism resets each three-year window and can recur.
Premium growth has decelerated every quarter for a year (net premiums earned +14% YoY 3Q25 to +6% YoY 2Q26) as 2023-24 rate increases lap.
Open multi-state class actions (classes already certified in three states) allege improper total-loss vehicle valuation practices.
rows.thesis: The largest and most data-driven US auto insurer, still growing policies 7% a year with combined ratios 7-10 points inside its own profitability ceiling.

val_consistency.reconciliation: PGR has no V1 systematic valuation row (not in the 92-name V1 universe). Reverse-engineered via justified P/B (P/B=(ROE-g)/(COE-g)): the current 3.5x P/B requires only ~18.7% sustained ROE against a delivered TTM ROE of ~36% and a combined ratio that has stayed 86-90 for four straight quarters; the market appears to be pricing a much larger fade in profitability than the disclosed trend supports.

Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x (vs ≈0.8x now) without a value-accretive acquisition justifying it.
The $58.9m ESG jury verdict is upheld on appeal and expands materially beyond the awarded amount, or triggers additional related claims.
adverse: Q2 2026 stock fell 9.7% on a disclosed production-throughput/execution miss in the Climate & Sustainability (refrigeration) segment that cost ~1.0-1.5 points of consolidated organic growth, despite an EPS beat and guidance raise.

A jury returned a ~$58.9m verdict (June 2025) against the Environmental Solutions Group business (sold to Terex in Oct 2024) for breach of contract/inducement of breach of fiduciary duty; post-trial motions filed, appeal to the Seventh Circuit possible.

The October 2024 sale of the Environmental Solutions Group causes a real discontinuity in reported revenue/net income/OCF between FY2024 and FY2025-26 filings; FY2024 GAAP net income ($2,697m) was inflated by the ~$2.0bn divestiture gain.
rows.thesis: Diversified industrial group riding real AI-data-center cooling demand, low debt, and a share price pricing in far less growth than management is currently delivering.

FY2026 revenue-growth guidance was cut from 7-9% to 4-6% (both total company and the U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment) even as adjusted EPS guidance was raised over the same period

Own P/TBV excess-return reverse-DCF (1.62x TBV, ~16% assumed long-run adjusted ROTCE, 10% cost of equity) implies the market is pricing only ~0-1% perpetual growth, well below the analyst's own mid-single-digit base case -> below/cheap.

port.note: Weights are shares of the stock sleeve. Sleeve rules were fixed before the diligence verdicts were read: official point-in-time score in the top 70, 1-year volatility ≤ 45%, no pending takeover, valuation attractive or fair versus the company's own history, diligence INCLUDE (full) or INCLUDE-SMALL (half), ≤ 2 names per sub-industry, inverse-volatility weights of 3–10% (full conviction) or 1.5–5% (half conviction), sectors ≤ 25%; sleeve capacity the caps cannot absorb is held in the S&P 500 index fund. * Calibrated odds are empirical frequencies for S&P 500 stocks in the same score decile and volatility band, 2011–2025.

bt.lede: We froze a model built only from well-replicated research (quality, value, momentum, earnings surprise) before running any test, then tested it month by month from 2012 to August 2026 on the stocks that were actually in the S&P 500 at each date, with as-filed SEC data and trading costs. A second agent rebuilt it independently and matched it within 0.04 points a year. It did not beat the S&P 500: the top 30 returned 12.5% a year against 15.1% for the index (t = -1.12), and a higher score did not mean a higher return. Every variant told the same story, including the v1, v2 and v3 models. Tested the way v3 was tested (on today's survivors), the same model shows 18.6% a year instead of 12.5%: a 6.0-point illusion.

stats.name: Sleeve rule as pre-committed (top 20, vol ≤45%, inverse-vol, quarterly)

bt.notes: Point-in-time S&P 500 membership (D1/D2), total-return prices (D2), as-filed SEC XBRL fundamentals filed before each month-end (D3); 10 bps per trade; Newey–West t-statistics. Residual survivorship (delisted names without free price data) flatters every strategy by about 0.9% a year versus the real equal-weight ETF (RSP); it cannot turn the negative result positive. Full detail: v4/outputs/b1_report.md, independent replication v4/outputs/b1x_report.md.

risk.lede: All stock, the 20 holdings have a 91% chance of a fall worse than 20% at some point within 5 years (base case). If you later want less risk, allocation is the lever. The index alone has a 81% chance of a fall worse than 20% at some point within 5 years; adding a 30% T-bill reserve cuts it to 52%, and 55% cuts it to 13%. The 20 stocks fell harder than the index in the COVID crash and held up far better in 2022.
risk.worst: The worst fall to plan around. Over the full daily history (2005-01-04 to 2026-09-25) at today's weights, the stock sleeve's worst fall was −56.5% (peak 2007-10-09, trough 2009-03-09, recovered 2009-12-23). The S&P 500's worst fall over the same days was −55.2% (2007-10-09 to 2009-03-09). The crisis replays above use the S&P 500's own peak and trough dates, so they can show a smaller figure for the sleeve (GFC: −56.5%). Treat −56% as the sleeve's tail-risk anchor. In the Moderate mix the 2007–09 replay cost −41.2% and in the Cautious mix −26.8%; set those against your 15–20% tolerance.
risk.divers: Diversification. The 20 stocks behave like about 17 independent positions once their tendency to move together is counted (19 if only the weights are counted). About 51% of the sleeve's day-to-day risk comes from the market as a whole (its sensitivity to the S&P 500, beta, is 0.67); the rest is specific to the companies. The largest company-specific risks are ADP (8%), DRI (7%), BR (7%). Per dollar invested, the riskiest holdings are AXP, HBAN and CRH: each adds 1.3–1.4 times as much of the sleeve's risk as its weight alone would suggest. Measured over the last three years of daily prices, the sleeve's volatility is 14.4% and it strays from the S&P 500 by about 11.2% a year. An independent re-computation and the method are in Appendix A.
risk.notes: Scenarios: Bear 2% / Base 6% / Bull 9% a year (R1, sourced from 12 institutional forecasts); T-bills 4%. 20,000 stationary-bootstrap paths of 2005–2026 daily returns (B2 module). Sleeve alpha assumed zero. Scenario analysis, not advice.

findings.topic: A hard 15–20% loss limit needs a small equity share
findings.v005: Maximum 25% equity (15% index + 10% direct, at least 75% reserve); a hypothetical tail shock (index −60%, stocks −75%, reserve −2%) loses 18.0% at full deployment.
findings.v4: Daily-data replay of 2007–09 with quarterly rebalancing: staying within −20% needed ≤34% in equities, within −15% ≤27%. The Defensive mix (v005's budget) fell -13.8% in that replay.
findings.effect: v4 adds the Defensive 15/10/75 mix to every allocation table, with simulated odds on the same engine as the other mixes.

findings.topic: Whether 15–20% must hold in every crash
findings.v005: Treats 15–20% as the design objective for the whole portfolio, hence 75–81% reserve.
findings.v4: Shows the trade-off instead. Base case, median 5-year return +4.9%/yr for Defensive vs +6.1%/yr for Moderate; P(fall > 20% within 5 yrs) 0% vs 52%. The 15–20% figure comes from the earlier Codex review notes; to Claude the owner described his risk appetite as 'not very risk-averse, not extremely risk-taking'.
findings.effect: v4 does not override v005: the owner chooses which sentence describes his limit (the one next step).

findings.topic: Irish UCITS index core and a short-Treasury reserve
findings.v005: VUAA (IE00BFMXXD54) for the index; IB01 (IE00BGSF1X88, 0–1 yr Treasuries) plus cash for the reserve.
findings.v4: CSPX or VUAA for the core; directly held T-bills or a UCITS T-bill fund for the reserve. IB01 is such a fund; both keep the reserve outside US estate tax.
findings.effect: v4 names IB01 as one eligible reserve fund, alongside direct T-bills.

findings.topic: Dividend withholding and US estate tax
findings.v005: 30% withholding on direct US dividends; Irish funds 15% internally; direct US shares are US-situs.
findings.v4: Same facts, re-verified against IRS and issuer pages on 26 Sep 2026 (R2, R3).

findings.v005: Ranks only the original fourteen v3 candidates and says so ('not a claim to have found the best fourteen investments in the entire market').
findings.v4: v3's candidate list rested on biased evidence: its momentum result falls from 29.1%/yr to 18.1%/yr once stocks count only after joining the index, and its conviction filter failed out of sample. v4 screens all 503 point-in-time members with pre-registered rules plus primary-source diligence. The only overlap is HIG.
findings.effect: v4's satellite is not built from v3's list. v4 also found no stock-selection edge, so neither workstream's picks should be expected to beat the index.

findings.topic: AMP and PAYX as first purchases
findings.status: AMP CONFIRMED (eligible, not held); PAYX CONFIRMED as buyable (eligible, not held)

dossiers.AAPL:
Apple Inc. (AAPL) — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 12–36 month thesis horizon. One-sentence reason: a 2.5-billion-device installed base is monetizing better than ever (Services at a record run-rate, gross margin at an 8-quarter high), but the current iPhone-17 supercycle plus Services re-acceleration has pushed the price to imply more growth than this analyst's steady-state base case, so it is a hold-with-a-reservation, not a full-conviction add.

1. Business in plain English

Apple sells premium hardware (iPhone ~50% of revenue, Mac/iPad/Wearables the rest) to a large, loyal, high-income-skewed installed base, then monetizes that base through Services (App Store, subscriptions, advertising, Apple Care, licensing — notably Google's payment for default search placement). The moat is the hardware-software-services ecosystem and switching costs, not any single product's technical superiority. Growth increasingly comes from Services (higher margin, more durable) rather than hardware unit growth.

2. Why the model likes it / is it durable

b1 composite percentile 0.72 (second-highest of the four names after NVDA), driven by Value (fam_V 1.20 raw, ep/fcfp percentiles ~0.49–0.51) and a very high leverage percentile (0.79) reflecting Apple's large, deliberate net-debt capital structure rather than distress. Quality percentile is only 0.38 (gp_a percentile 0.53, but negative accruals score −0.05 pct 0.53 is mixed) and momentum is modest (mom_12_1 percentile 0.48) — the model likes Apple's cash-flow multiple and balance-sheet leverage more than any "growth" signal. live_rank 159 — outside the top-70 gate; in the quality-growth carve-out only. The durability case rests on installed-base growth and Services mix shift, both verifiable below.

3. Last 8 quarters (fiscal quarters; $M except EPS)

Quarter Revenue Gross margin R&D Op margin Net income Diluted EPS
FQ2 FY24 (end 2024-03-30) 90,753 46.6% 7,903 30.7% 23,636 1.53
FQ3 FY24 (end 2024-06-29) 85,777 46.3% 8,006 29.6% 21,448 1.40
FQ1 FY25 (end 2024-12-28) 124,300 46.9% 8,268 34.5% 36,330 2.40
FQ2 FY25 (end 2025-03-29) 95,359 47.1% 8,550 31.0% 24,780 1.65
FQ3 FY25 (end 2025-06-28) 94,036 46.5% 8,866 30.0% 23,434 1.57
FQ1 FY26 (end 2025-12-27) 143,756 48.2% 10,887 35.4% 42,097 2.84
FQ2 FY26 (end 2026-03-28) 111,184 49.3% 11,419 32.3% 29,578 2.01
FQ3 FY26 (end 2026-06-27) 109,417 50.0% 11,729 32.6% 29,789 2.02

Gross margin has climbed steadily from 46.3% to a round 50.0% over these eight quarters — a genuine, filed trend (mix shift toward Services plus disciplined component costs), not a one-quarter blip. FQ1 FY26 revenue ($143.8B, +16% YoY) was driven by "extraordinary demand for the iPhone 17 lineup," with iPhone segment revenue $85.27B that quarter (+23% YoY) and Services hitting a record $30.0B (+14% YoY). TTM revenue (Q4 FY25–Q3 FY26) ≈$466.8B vs. FY2025 full-year $416.2B — a marked acceleration from FY2025's own 6.4% YoY growth (FY24 $391.0B → FY25 $416.2B). [1][2]

4. Guidance track record

Apple does not issue formal point/range revenue guidance (a long-standing practice), so a "raised/maintained/cut vs. prior range" comparison is not available; this is disclosed rather than omitted. Directionally: CNBC reported Apple's Q2 FY26 revenue guidance "topped estimates on booming iPhone, Mac demand" (30-Apr-2026 report), consistent with the acceleration seen in the filed numbers above. [3]

5. Moat and competition

  • Installed base: >2.5 billion active devices, up from 2.35 billion a year earlier (≈6.4% YoY growth) — the base that Services monetizes; management called it "a new all-time high...across all major product categories and geographic segments." [1]
  • Services: FY2025 Services revenue $109.16B — the first fiscal year Services exceeded $100B; Q1 FY26 Services hit a record $30.0B, +14% YoY. Services carries materially higher gross margin than products and is the more durable growth engine.
  • China — share recovering, but competitively contested: Apple held 18.1% of China's smartphone market in Q2 2026 (up from 13.9% a year earlier, +24.9% YoY shipment growth — one of only two top-10 vendors growing), but Huawei leads with 22.6% share, "the highest in five years." Apple used early price-hike warnings to pull forward iPhone-17 upgrades while holding its own price, a tactic that will not repeat indefinitely. [4]
  • Regulatory: Apple opened to third-party payments/app stores in the EU under the DMA; in China, 48 iOS developers petitioned SAMR for an antitrust investigation into App Store commissions (Jun-2026), and Apple pre-emptively cut its standard China App Store commission from 30% to 25% (Mar-2026) — a real, filed reduction in take-rate in at least one major market, with more regulatory pressure visible elsewhere. [4]
  • Apple Intelligence / AI features: sources reference "a more personalized Siri coming this year" — i.e., Apple's flagship on-device AI feature was still pending/rolling out as of the cutoff, later than competitors' generative-AI assistants; this is a genuine execution-timeline risk to the "AI upgrade cycle" bull thesis, not yet a proof point. [1]

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • TTM (Q4 FY25–Q3 FY26) operating cash flow $146,724M, capex $10,041M, FCF ≈$136,683M, FCF margin ≈29.3% of TTM revenue — strong, typical of Apple's asset-light manufacturing model (contract manufacturers carry most fixed-asset intensity).
  • SBC ~$3.3–3.6B/quarter, ≈2.5–3.3% of revenue — modest and stable.
  • Capital return: buybacks ~$24.7B and dividends ~$3.9B in the most recent quarter shown (Q1 FY26) — buybacks remain the dominant capital-return channel and a structural EPS tailwind independent of operating performance.
  • This analyst did not pull a precise current net-cash/net-debt balance-sheet figure from the sources gathered in this pass (time-boxed); Apple has historically run a large gross-debt, partially-offsetting-cash capital structure for tax and capital-return efficiency rather than distress — flagged as an item to verify against the FQ3 FY26 10-Q balance sheet directly rather than asserted here.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (no V1 systematic valuation row for AAPL)

Inputs: EV ≈ market cap $4,977,637M; TTM FCF $136,683M; WACC 8.5%; terminal growth 3.5%; 10-year horizon. Solving for the constant FCF growth rate that justifies the price: 10.7%/year for 10 years (FCF yield on trailing FCF = 2.75%). - Bear case (10y FCF CAGR ≈3%): China share loss resumes, Services growth stalls as regulatory fee compression spreads beyond the EU/China, the iPhone-17 supercycle proves a pull-forward rather than a new trend. - Base case (10y FCF CAGR ≈8%): hardware settles back to low-single-digit unit/ASP growth (2–4%), Services continues compounding at 11–13%, blended revenue growth decelerates from the current supercycle-driven low-teens toward mid-single-digits over the decade, with FCF growing modestly faster than revenue on continued Services mix shift. - Bull case (10y FCF CAGR ≈14%): Apple Intelligence finally lands and drives a genuine upgrade cycle, Services re-accelerates, new device categories contribute. Implied vs. base: ABOVE. 10.7% sits above the 8% base case — the market is crediting Apple with more than steady-state trend growth, effectively extrapolating the current iPhone-17/Services acceleration rather than the multi-year historical average (FY24→FY25 was only +6.4%).

3-year scenario returns (annualised total return from $341.07, illustrative; includes an approximate 0.5% dividend yield)

Scenario 3y FCF CAGR (yrs 1–3) Exit EV/FCF Annualised return
Bear ~0% 24x (de-rate from 36.4x entry) ≈ −12.5%/yr
Base ~9% 32x ≈ +5%/yr
Bull ~16% 38x ≈ +18%/yr

8. Bull case

  1. Gross margin at an 8-quarter high (50.0%) and rising, on filed numbers, not adjusted metrics.
  2. Installed base still growing (~6.4% YoY) at 2.5B+ devices — the monetization base for Services keeps expanding even if hardware unit growth is modest.
  3. Services just crossed $100B/year (FY2025) and continues compounding at double digits, a higher-margin, more durable revenue stream than hardware.

9. Bear case

  1. Huawei leads China smartphone share (22.6% vs. Apple's 18.1%) and Apple's recent China growth was partly a price-hike-avoidance pull-forward, not necessarily sustainable.
  2. Regulatory pressure on App Store take-rates is spreading (EU DMA already binding; China commission already cut 30%→25%; a SAMR antitrust probe has been requested) — a structural risk to Services' superior margin.
  3. Apple Intelligence/Siri AI features were still described as "coming" as of the cutoff — behind several competitors' shipped generative-AI assistants, a real execution risk to the AI-upgrade-cycle bull case.

10. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis-invalidation triggers (what would change the verdict / break the thesis)

  1. China smartphone market share falls back below 15% for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Services revenue growth decelerates below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  3. Gross margin falls below 45% for two consecutive quarters.
  4. A regulatory action cuts Apple's global (not just EU/China) App Store take-rate by more than 5 points.
  5. Installed-base active-device growth decelerates below 4% YoY.

11. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q4 FY26, estimated ~29-Oct-2026 (pattern-based estimate from FY25 Q4's 31-Oct-2025 10-K filing date; not yet confirmed as of this cutoff).
  • Full-year FY2026 10-K filing expected shortly after that report.

12. Red-flag scan

  • SAMR antitrust petition from 48 Chinese iOS developers (Jun-2026) — a live, unresolved regulatory matter.
  • China App Store commission cut 30%→25% (Mar-2026) — a real, already-realized margin headwind in one market, worth monitoring for spread to other jurisdictions.
  • No auditor changes, restatements or going-concern language found in sources reviewed.
  • Balance-sheet net debt/cash figure not independently re-verified in this pass (see §6) — flagged rather than asserted.

13. Data basis, recency and disclaimer

All figures are consolidated (Apple has no separately reported standalone/parent-only financial statements). Most recent period incorporated: fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q, period ended 2026-06-27, filed 2026-07-31 (data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0000320193.json). Events and news checked to 2026-09-25. GAAP figures used throughout. This is research, not investment advice: not a recommendation, and not personalised to any individual's circumstances.

Sources

  2. Apple 10-Q/10-K filings, SEC EDGAR (data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0000320193.json)
  3. CNBC, "Apple revenue guidance tops estimates on booming iPhone, Mac demand," 2026-04-30
  4. Counterpoint Research, "China Smartphone Market Q1 2026"; MacTech/AppleWorld.Today, "Apple has 18.1% of China's smartphone market...Q2 2026"; DigiTimes/Revera, App Store antitrust coverage, 2026

dossiers.ABBV:
AbbVie Inc. (ABBV) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F51 (wave 3) | As of: 2026-09-25 close (px $264.34, mktcap $467.14bn per b1_live_scores.csv 2026-09-25)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 12–36 months. The Humira patent-cliff replacement thesis (Skyrizi/Rinvoq) has genuinely worked — immunology revenue is still growing double digits — but the named reservation is specific: AbbVie carries negative consolidated stockholders' equity (−$5.9bn at 2026-06-30) on ~$70.8bn of total debt, and its "adjusted" EPS excludes a large, recurring (not one-off) acquired-IPR&D/milestone expense line ($2.76/share in FY2025 alone) that behaves like an ongoing cost of maintaining the pipeline. The reverse DCF implies growth roughly in line with — not below — a reasonable base case, so there is little margin of safety on top of those balance-sheet and earnings-quality flags.

2. Business in plain English

AbbVie is a global biopharmaceutical company. Its largest franchise is immunology (Skyrizi for psoriasis/psoriatic arthritis/IBD, Rinvoq for rheumatoid arthritis and related conditions, and the legacy Humira, now in steep biosimilar-driven decline), plus neuroscience (Vraylar, Botox Therapeutic, migraine drugs Ubrelvy/Qulipta), oncology (Imbruvica, Venclexta, Elahere) and an aesthetics business (Botox Cosmetic, fillers) inherited from the 2020 Allergan acquisition. It earns money by selling patented/branded drugs and devices, protected by patents and increasingly by complex payer-rebate contracting (source: ABBV 10-Q, period 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-03; ABBV 8-K Ex.99.1 releases).

3. Why the model likes it / is this durable — and a genuine data conflict

b1_live_scores.csv (as_of 2026-09-25): composite decile 6, quintile 3, live_rank 243. Quality family (fam_Q=6) scores well on gross-profit/assets (pct 61.5%) and OCF/assets (pct 71.1%), but the ROE field is blank/missing for ABBV in b1_live_scores.csv — not zero, not low, genuinely absent. This is not a data-pipeline bug in isolation: it is the direct, explainable consequence of the negative-stockholders'-equity finding in §6 below (ROE is undefined or economically meaningless when book equity is negative). This is exactly the kind of quant-vs-filing conflict the wave-3 mandate asks to be surfaced explicitly: data_conflict — b1's quality composite is silently missing one of its inputs for ABBV, for a real and identifiable balance-sheet reason, not a data error. The growth driver itself (Skyrizi + Rinvoq immunology growth outrunning Humira's decline) is durable in the sense that it is now visible in two-plus years of reported revenue, not a projection (see §4).

4. Last quarters of results (source: ABBV 8-K Ex.99.1 earnings releases, cited; GAAP unless labelled adjusted)

5. Guidance track record (last several releases; FY adjusted diluted EPS — AbbVie's own disclosure pattern requires

care here, detailed below) AbbVie's official guidance excludes future acquired-IPR&D/milestone expense because it "does not forecast" that item; it then pre-announces each quarter's actual IPR&D hit via a standalone Item 2.02 8-K roughly a month before the full earnings release, and republishes an "updated" guidance range that folds in the now-known charge. Comparing headline ranges across quarters without tracking this two-step process would misstate whether guidance was raised or cut — exactly the wave-3 lesson this dossier is required to apply. 1. Q3 2025 (2025-10-31): FY2025 raised from $10.38–$10.58 to $10.61–$10.65 (adjusted EPS, excluding Q4 IPR&D). 2. 2026-01-07 8-K (pre-announcement): discloses Q4 2025 IPR&D/milestone expense of $1.3bn pretax (−$0.71/share) and restates the "including Q4 IPR&D" FY2025 range down to $9.90–$9.94. 3. Q4/FY2025 (2026-02-04): FY2025 actual adjusted EPS $10.00 — a beat versus the IPR&D-inclusive $9.90–$9.94 range, but a −1.2% YoY decline once the year's cumulative $2.76/share of IPR&D charges are counted. FY2026 initial guidance issued (excluding 2026 IPR&D): $14.37–$14.57. 4. 2026-04-03 8-K: discloses Q1 2026 IPR&D expense of $744m pretax (−$0.41/share), restates FY2026 (IPR&D- inclusive) to $13.96–$14.16. 5. Q1 2026 (2026-04-29): genuinely raised (on an apples-to-apples, IPR&D-inclusive basis) to $14.08–$14.28. 6. Q2 2026 (2026-07-31): updated to $13.87–$14.07, explicitly to absorb $0.14/share of dilution from the pending Apogee Therapeutics acquisition (partially offset by $0.10/share of operating overperformance) — a guidance change driven by a new deal, not an operating cut, but the headline range is nonetheless lower than the prior $14.08–$14.28. Net: guidance has been raised on an operating basis in every quarter reviewed once IPR&D and M&A dilution are adjusted for consistently — but the headline ranges alone, read naively, would look like an unexplained miss (FY25) followed by a cut (Q2'26) or a raise (Q1'26) depending on which two releases are compared. This dossier resolves that by reading the pre-announcement 8-Ks, per the wave-3 mandate.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (consolidated, GAAP, entity = AbbVie Inc. and subsidiaries; 10-Q period

2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-03, and 10-Q period 2026-03-31, filed 2026-05-08) - Stockholders' equity is NEGATIVE: total stockholders' equity −$5,935m at 2026-06-30 (−$6,656m at 2026-03-31), driven by treasury stock −$10,618m and accumulated deficit in retained earnings −$17,333m against additional paid-in capital of only $23,156m. This is a longstanding structural feature (large buybacks/dividends and Allergan- deal-related charges over several years, not a new single-quarter event) but it means AbbVie has no equity cushion: the balance sheet is supported entirely by ~$85bn of goodwill+intangibles ($35.5bn + $49.1bn at 2026-06-30) against $135.1bn of total assets and $141.0bn of total liabilities. - Leverage: total debt $70.8bn, cash $6.6bn, net debt $64.3bn (both at 2026-06-30). TTM EBITDA (sum of the last four quarterly EBITDA figures reconciled in the company's filings, Q3'25–Q2'26) ≈ $21.2bn → net debt/EBITDA ≈ 3.0x, consolidated. This is a moderate, investment-grade-consistent level for large pharma but leaves no room for a leverage surprise given the zero equity cushion above. - Recurring "one-off" item: acquired IPR&D/milestone expense was $2.76/share for FY2025 (~$4.9bn pretax at ~1.77bn shares) and continued at $0.41/share (Q1'26) and further amounts in Q2/Q3 2026 — i.e., AbbVie has incurred a large IPR&D charge in every recent quarter. Treating it as purely non-recurring in "adjusted EPS" overstates normalized earnings power if the company's business-development pace (licensing deals funding the pipeline) continues at a similar cadence, which recent history suggests it will. - Litigation accrual: $1.7bn at 2026-06-30 (up from $1.6bn at 2025-12-31) — see red-flag scan. - Capital return: quarterly dividend raised 5.5% (declared 2025-10-31, from $1.64 to $1.73/share effective the 2026-02-17 payment) — a genuine, well-covered raise (FCF, see below, comfortably exceeds the dividend). - FCF: TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) FCF ≈ $19.68bn (sum of quarterly OCF-less-capex, SEC XBRL/10-Q cash-flow statements) on ~1.771bn diluted shares → FCF/share ≈ $11.11; quarterly FCF is lumpy (Q3'25 $7.53bn included a large working-capital swing per the cash-flow statement) so the TTM figure, not any single quarter, should be used.

7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF (own build; no V1 row exists for ABBV — not previously a top-70/lane name)

Adjusted NTM P/E on FY2026 guidance midpoint ($13.97): 264.34/13.97 = 18.9x. EV (mktcap $467.1bn + net debt $64.3bn) / TTM FCF ($19.68bn) ≈ 27.0x; FCF yield on equity market cap ≈ 4.2%. Reverse DCF (2-stage, 10-yr + Gordon terminal; terminal growth 3.0%): given AbbVie's low reported beta (0.281, FMP) understates its true risk (patent-cliff/litigation/negative-equity risk are not well captured by historical beta for a company mid-transition), I ran two WACC scenarios rather than picking one: at WACC 7.5%, implied 10-yr FCF/share growth ≈ 5.0%/yr; at WACC 8.5%, implied growth ≈ 7.7%/yr. A reasonable evidence-based base case — mid-single-digit revenue growth (immunology deceleration as Skyrizi/Rinvoq mature, partially offset by neuroscience and an early obesity pipeline) translating to high-single-digit EPS/FCF growth via margin and buybacks — sits at roughly 6–8%/yr, i.e., inside the WACC-sensitivity band, not clearly below it. Verdict: implied_vs_base = "in_line." This is a fair, not a cheap, price for a business whose two biggest growth drivers (Skyrizi, Rinvoq) are still compounding but will mechanically decelerate as they scale.

8. Bull case

  1. The Humira patent-cliff bear case is now largely played out and visible in the numbers: Humira was $756m of revenue in Q2 2026, versus $4.54bn for all of FY2025 and far larger before — the worst of the erosion is behind, confirmed by four quarters of reported data, not a projection.
  2. Immunology ex-Humira (Skyrizi + Rinvoq) grew revenue 14.6% operationally in Q2 2026 on an already-large base ($8.0bn combined in the quarter) — genuine, large-scale, currently-realized growth.
  3. Dividend raised 5.5% with FCF coverage comfortable (TTM FCF ≈ $19.7bn vs. TTM dividends paid ≈ $11.9bn implied by the quarterly cash-flow statements), supporting the income case even if growth decelerates.

9. Bear case

  1. Zero equity cushion (negative $5.9bn stockholders' equity) plus ~3.0x net debt/EBITDA leaves no room for a negative surprise (an adverse litigation judgment, a failed pipeline bet, or a large dilutive deal) without raising real balance-sheet-risk questions, unlike most other large-cap pharma peers with positive equity.
  2. The recurring, large acquired-IPR&D/milestone expense line ($2.76/share FY2025) is excluded from "adjusted" EPS every year; if treated as a normal, recurring cost of maintaining AbbVie's pipeline (which the multi-year pattern suggests it is), normalized earnings power is lower than the headlined adjusted EPS implies.
  3. Reverse DCF shows the current price already embeds a base-case-level growth assumption — there is little room for the Skyrizi/Rinvoq deceleration (both are large, maturing franchises) to arrive faster than modeled without the stock re-rating down.

10. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable triggers that would invalidate the thesis)

  1. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA (per the 10-Q's own reconciliation) exceeds 3.5x in any quarter.
  2. Combined Skyrizi + Rinvoq operational revenue growth falls below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. 14.6% in Q2 2026).
  3. Acquired IPR&D/milestone expense exceeds $3.00/share on a trailing-12-month basis (vs. $2.76/share in FY2025), signalling an accelerating, not one-off, drag.
  4. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut on an IPR&D-and-M&A-adjusted, apples-to-apples basis (i.e., excluding the effect of newly disclosed IPR&D charges and disclosed acquisitions, which are not true operating cuts).
  5. An adverse final judgment or settlement in the Allergan opioid MDL or Biocell breast-implant litigation materially exceeding the current $1.7bn litigation accrual.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 results, estimated ~2026-10-30/31 (Q3 2025 was reported 2025-10-31; estimate, not confirmed). Expect a pre-announcement Item 2.02 8-K disclosing the Q3 2026 IPR&D/milestone charge roughly 3–4 weeks before that release, consistent with the pattern in §5. Apogee Therapeutics acquisition expected to close Q3 2026 (per the Q2 2026 release) — watch for the closing 8-K and updated dilution guidance.

12. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation (10-Q, period 2026-06-30, "Legal Proceedings and Contingencies"): litigation accrual $1.7bn (2026-06-30) vs $1.6bn (2025-12-31). Opioid: ~215 lawsuits pending against Allergan (opioid marketing/sale allegations), consolidated as MDL No. 2804 (N.D. Ohio) plus ~20 state-court cases; ~20 of the ~215 in the process of dismissal under a previously announced settlement. Breast implants: Allergan Biocell textured-implant litigation — US lawsuits substantially resolved by a June 2026 settlement agreement, but ~1,300 MDL cases (D.N.J., MDL 2921), ~475 state-court cases and ~1,080 international cases remain (Netherlands claims dismissed Dec 2025, under appeal Mar 2026). Humira pricing: Camargo v. AbbVie (list-price class action) dismissed without prejudice Jan 2026, appealed Mar 2026 to the Seventh Circuit. Humira antitrust: Sheet Metal Workers' Health Plan… v. AbbVie (filed Jan 2025, N.D. Ill.) alleges AbbVie's Humira rebating practices impair biosimilar competition, an antitrust theory — ongoing, unresolved. Legacy Niaspan patent-settlement antitrust MDL (Kos Pharmaceuticals/Abbott legacy) also still pending.
  • No auditor change, restatement, or going-concern language found in the sections reviewed. Insider Form 4 pattern and short-seller reports were not checked in the time available (limitation, disclosed).
  • Data conflict vs b1: ROE field missing in b1_live_scores.csv for ABBV — explained by negative equity (§3, §6). This is the dossier's headline data_conflicts entry.

dossiers.ABNB:
ABNB — Airbnb, Inc.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months. Genuinely strong, primary-source-verified operating momentum (revenue/GBV/margin guidance raised or beaten in each of the last four quarters, ~10% reduction in diluted share count since 2022 from buybacks, a $12bn net-cash balance sheet, 37% TTM FCF margin) is offset by a valuation that is not statistically cheap (26.3x NTM P/E against peers that are not fully comparable) and by spreading, city-by-city short-term-rental regulation that is a genuine and event-driven — not merely theoretical — risk to the core listings business. Investable at reduced size given the balance-sheet quality and cash generation; the named reservation is that the base case requires further multiple re-rating from an already-premium starting point, offering limited margin of safety.

2. Business in plain English

Airbnb operates the world's largest marketplace connecting people who want to rent out a home or room ("hosts") with travellers who want to stay in one ("guests"), and — increasingly — travellers who want to book an "experience" (a local activity) or, via a newly launched initiative, a hotel room. Airbnb owns no real estate; it earns a service/commission fee (an "implied take rate," revenue ÷ Gross Booking Value) on each booking, which has run 9%–18% quarter to quarter (the swings are driven mostly by the timing mismatch between when a guest books and pays vs. when they stay, not by a change in pricing — see §4). It competes with Booking.com/Vrbo/Expedia for the room-night, and — where regulators restrict short-term rentals — increasingly with hotels directly, which is why it has begun listing boutique/independent hotels itself in supply-constrained cities.

3. Why the model likes it — and is it durable?

B1 composite is top decile (live_rank 40/~2,300; composite percentile ~92%; only 3 of 4 factor families computed — no reliable SUE/earnings-momentum signal exists yet given ABNB's short public history. Gates: the composite carries no disqualifying-red-flag gate — see §11 for the separate legal/regulatory red-flag check.) Family drivers: Momentum (fam_M ≈0.97, extremely high) — the stock has re-rated hard off strong, repeated guidance beats; Quality (fam_Q ≈0.91, very high) — strong gross-profit/assets, ROE and operating-cash-flow/assets, low leverage (net cash); Value (fam_V ≈0.23, weak) — ABNB is expensive on every value sub-metric, which is the honest counterweight to the other two families.

Durability check: the momentum is real and corroborated in primary-source releases — Q1, Q2 2026 revenue both exceeded the high end of prior guidance, and full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA-margin guidance was raised three times running (Q4-2025 "stable YoY" → Q1-2026 "at least 35%" → Q2-2026 "at least 35.5%"). But the mechanism of margin expansion is cost discipline (customer-support cost per booking down ~10–16% YoY on AI-driven efficiency) and operating leverage on GBV growth — not take-rate/monetisation expansion (take rate has been flat-to-down YoY in three of the last four quarters once the RNPL booking-timing effect is stripped out). A growth algorithm that depends on continued GBV volume growth is more exposed to a regulatory/supply shock than one where pricing power is doing the work.

4. Last two years of results (SEC 10-Q/10-K, GAAP)

Note on seasonality — do not compare quarters within a year. ABNB's business is extremely seasonal (northern-hemisphere summer travel): Q3 operating margin runs ~40%, Q1 runs 1.7%–3.2%. Every comparison in this dossier is YoY, same fiscal quarter, per the sector playbook. Q2 2026: revenue +16.5% YoY to $3,608m (company states "17%," likely off unrounded figures), GBV +16% YoY to $27.2bn, Nights & Seats Booked +10% YoY, net income +27.1% YoY, Adjusted EBITDA margin 35% (was 34%), FCF $1.3bn (35% margin), TTM FCF $4.8bn (37% TTM margin) — a very strong absolute cash-generation profile.

Take rate (revenue ÷ GBV), the key OTA monetisation metric, by quarter: Q3'25 17.9% (down YoY) → Q4'25 13.6% (down YoY) → Q1'26 9.2% (~flat YoY) → Q2'26 13.2% (in line YoY). The large swings are explained by management as FX and the timing effect of "Reserve Now, Pay Later" (guests book and pay closer to the stay date), not a change in the fee schedule — but the flat-to-down YoY trend at each comparable point means take-rate expansion is not currently a source of margin upside; all of the margin story is cost/leverage.

Working-capital "float" — a structural, not a quality, signal. OCF is highest in Q1 ($1,789m 2025 / $1,708m 2026) despite Q1 being the weakest earnings quarter, because guests pay in advance of (mostly Q2/Q3) stays — a classic OTA negative-working-capital float per the sector playbook. This means OCF/FCF should never be read quarter-to-quarter without adjusting for the booking calendar; TTM figures are the safer read (TTM FCF margin 37%, per company disclosure).

Balance sheet debt event (H1 2026): on 2026-03-16 ABNB issued $2.5bn of new fixed-rate senior notes ($850m 4.40% due 2029, $850m 4.65% due 2031, $800m 5.25% due 2036) and used the proceeds to fully repay its $2.0bn 0% convertible senior notes due 2026. This shows up in the XBRL balance sheet as long-term debt jumping from $0 (2025-12-31) to $2.475bn (2026-03-31) and interest expense rising from ~$6–11m/quarter to $37–58m/quarter. Net effect: ABNB now carries real cash interest expense (~$30m/quarter run-rate) for the first time, in exchange for retiring dilution-risk convertible paper — a reasonable trade, but a genuine change in the capital structure worth tracking (net cash position, cash+STI, was ~$12.1bn at 2026-06-30 against $2.48bn LT debt, so still net-cash by a wide margin).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: very strong — TTM FCF margin 37%, well above the ~19–22% net-income margin, reflecting genuine operating leverage plus the (non-repeatable-forever) benefit of a growing, negative-working-capital deposit float.
  • SBC: materially high, 9.7%–15.8% of revenue every quarter over two years — this is the real, recurring, dilutive cost the retail/asset-light playbooks warn against adding back uncritically. The offsetting, verifiable fact: diluted weighted-average share count has fallen from 626m (Q2 2025) to 597m (Q2 2026), a genuine ~4.6% YoY reduction, and the company states fully-diluted shares are down ~10% since buybacks began in Q3 2022 — buybacks are more than absorbing the RSU dilution on a net basis, which is a legitimate, evidenced rebuttal to the naive "add back SBC and ignore dilution" critique. Cumulative cash spent on buybacks + RSU tax withholding since Q3 2022: $13.6bn (per Q4 2025 release) — a very large capital-allocation commitment relative to the company's size.
  • GAAP vs adjusted: ABNB's own EPS is not separately XBRL-tagged (see §4 note) and diluted EPS/NI both benefited from a $60m uncertain-tax-position release and favourable FDII tax treatment in Q4 2025 disclosed by the company itself; long-term effective tax rate is guided to decline into the "mid-to-high teens" from 2026 due to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).
  • Net debt/capital metrics: net cash (cash + STI − total debt) ≈ $9.6bn per V1's latest snapshot; even after the March-2026 $2.5bn note issuance, ABNB remains net-cash, not net-debt. Capex is immaterial (~0.3% of revenue) — a genuinely asset-light model, so leverage/coverage ratios are not a constraint here.
  • M&A: none pending or recently closed; the "hotels" initiative to date is a distribution partnership, not an acquisition.

7. Valuation snapshot — reconciliation with V1

V1 verdict: fair (score 0.10/1.0, near the boundary). NTM P/E 26.3x vs. ABNB's own only 53-month trading history (flagged by V1 itself as a "short/limited history" caveat — appropriately so; 53 months is not enough to establish a reliable own-history percentile through a full cycle) — currently the 23rd percentile of that short history. Peer median cited is 13.1x across BKNG/CCL/EXPE/HLT — I flag this peer set as heterogeneous per the sector playbook's own warning against blending owner/lessee/OTA/franchisor business models in one multiple: HLT is an asset-light hotel franchisor (structurally deserves a premium multiple of its own), CCL is a capital-intensive cruise operator, and EXPE is a lower-growth, lower-margin OTA — only BKNG is a close structural peer to ABNB. The 13.1x blended peer median is therefore less informative than it looks; I would not lean hard on the "ABNB trades at ~2x peer median" framing without unbundling the peer set first.

Reverse-DCF implied 10-year growth is +26.5% (using TTM EBIT margin 20.8%) against consensus FY1 growth of only +11.6% — the market is pricing continued mid-20s%/year growth for a decade. V1's own historical-CAGR fields are null (no 5/10-year delivered-growth comparison is possible — again a function of ABNB's short history as a public, post-pandemic-ramp company), so the "priced-for-vs-delivered" cross-check that anchors DG and DRI's valuation reconciliation is simply unavailable here — a genuine limitation, not an oversight. V1 base case: revenue growth 13.6%/yr, margin expanding to 22.5% (above the current TTM 20.8%, consistent with the margin-guidance raises in §5), exit multiple 33.7x — i.e., re-rating further up from today's already-premium 26.3x → base annualised 3-yr return +18.8%; bear −20.3%/bull +78.9% (an unusually wide bear/bull spread, reflecting genuine two-way uncertainty). Street 12-month target range $135–$220 (mean $184.35); V1's base 3-year value exceeds the Street 12-month high (same street_flag caveat as DG, less concerning given the different horizons).

My view: consistent = true, dossier_view = fair. I do not have a primary-source basis to call ABNB "cheap" — take rate is not expanding, the peer comparison is soft, and the base case's own math requires the multiple to expand again from an already-rich level, which is a materially weaker margin of safety than DG's setup (re-rating from a trough toward a historical norm). I also do not see grounds to call it "expensive"/"full" — the cash generation, balance sheet, and four-quarter beat-and-raise record are real. "Fair," with two-sided risk, is the right characterisation, and I agree with V1.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Four consecutive quarters of beating the high end of its own guidance on revenue, with Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised in three of the last four releases (28% Q4'25 trough → "at least 35.5%" current FY26 guide) — genuine, verifiable operating momentum. 2. $12.1bn net cash, 37% TTM FCF margin, and a demonstrated willingness/ability to shrink the diluted share count (−4.6% YoY) despite heavy RSU issuance — a rare combination of growth and capital-return capacity. 3. The direct-hotel-booking initiative in supply-constrained/regulated cities (NYC, LA, Madrid, San Francisco) is a credible, already-launched hedge against the regulatory risk in the bear case below, and the 2026 FIFA World Cup is a disclosed near-term demand catalyst.

Bear (3): 1. Short-term-rental regulation is spreading, not stabilising: Spain's Constitutional Court upheld Barcelona's decision not to renew any of its 10,101 tourist-apartment licenses (expiring Nov-2028); Spain separately fined Airbnb €64 million in December 2025 for advertising unlicensed listings; and Budapest, Athens and Houston added new restrictions in 2026 alongside the already-restrictive NYC and Barcelona regimes. This is a real, monetised, geographically-widening risk to the core listings business that is not obviously reflected in a take rate that has not expanded. 2. Take rate itself has been flat-to-down YoY in three of the last four quarters — the margin story is 100% cost/leverage-driven, which is more fragile than a pricing-power-driven margin story if growth decelerates. 3. The DOJ filed an amended federal housing-discrimination complaint against Airbnb in March 2026 alleging a pattern-or-practice of discrimination (broader than the single-host allegation the case began with) — an active, escalating federal legal matter with headline and financial-liability risk.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. FY revenue-growth or Adjusted EBITDA-margin guidance is cut versus the immediately prior quarter's guidance (four straight raises/holds to date).
  2. Take rate (revenue ÷ GBV) falls for two consecutive quarters on a YoY basis by more than 100bps, stripped of the disclosed RNPL/FX timing effects — i.e., a genuine, explained monetisation deterioration.
  3. Diluted weighted-average share count rises YoY for two consecutive quarters (buybacks failing to offset RSU dilution — currently falling, −4.6% YoY at Q2 2026).
  4. Net cash (cash + STI − total debt) falls by more than $3 billion in a rolling 12 months outside of a disclosed, board-approved acquisition.
  5. A new city/national regulatory action (license non-renewal, platform-wide ban or a fine) is disclosed that management itself identifies as covering a "material" market, or cumulative disclosed regulatory fines exceed $150 million on a trailing-12-month basis (calibrated off the December-2025 Spain fine).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 results, estimated early November 2026 (historical pattern: Nov 1/6/7 in 2023–2025; not yet confirmed by the company).
  • FIFA World Cup 2026 (June–July 2026, US/Mexico/Canada) — disclosed demand catalyst already partly in the Q2 2026 numbers; full effect should show in Q3 2026 results.
  • Any ruling or settlement in United States v. Airbnb (DOJ housing-discrimination suit, amended complaint March 2026).
  • Expansion pace of the direct-hotel-booking initiative beyond its four initial cities.

11. Red-flag scan

  • DOJ housing-discrimination lawsuit: United States v. Airbnb, Inc., N.D. Cal., an active federal civil-rights case; DOJ filed an amended complaint in March 2026 broadening the allegation to a pattern-or-practice theory across multiple cities. Unresolved as of this dossier.
  • Spain fine: €64 million (~$70m), announced December 2025, for advertising unlicensed short-term rentals — a direct, monetised regulatory penalty (not merely a market restriction).
  • Barcelona: Spain's Constitutional Court (March 2025) upheld the city's refusal to renew any of its 10,101 tourist-apartment licenses when they expire in November 2028 — a known, dated, but distant (2+ year) supply event.
  • Shareholder viewpoint-discrimination suit: Alliance Defending Freedom sued Airbnb (Delaware federal court, filed June 2025) over exclusion of a conservative shareholder proposal; a February 2026 ruling allowed the core claim to proceed. Lower financial materiality, a governance/proxy-process matter rather than a core-business risk.
  • Prior discrimination settlement: a 2024 class-action discrimination settlement included a $6m guest-compensation fund — already resolved, noted for completeness.
  • No auditor change, restatement or going-concern language identified in the filings reviewed. Insider Form-4 activity is high-frequency but consistent with routine RSU-vest sell-to-cover under 10b5-1 plans across a large Section-16-officer roster; no unusual acceleration in net insider selling was identified within the scope of this review.

dossiers.ABT:
ABT — Abbott Laboratories — Diligence Dossier (Agent F38, Wave-2 Standard)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Reservation: the March-2026 Exact Sciences acquisition has temporarily elevated leverage and widened the GAAP/adjusted gap, and NEC infant-formula litigation, while now partly quantified via an August 2026 settlement, still leaves ~1,700 suits pending. Neither is a thesis-breaker, but both argue for half-weight rather than full conviction until Q3/Q4 2026 show the acquisition integrating cleanly and the balance sheet delevering.

2. Business in plain English

Abbott sells four things: diagnostic tests (now including Exact Sciences' Cologuard colon-cancer screening test), medical devices (FreeStyle Libre continuous glucose monitors, pacemakers/defibrillators, heart-valve and structural-heart devices), infant/adult nutrition (Similac, Ensure), and branded generic drugs sold mostly outside the U.S. It makes money selling recurring consumables (test strips, sensors, formula) and durable devices with high switching costs (implanted cardiac devices, installed diagnostic instruments). Its competitive position is built on breadth (four uncorrelated franchises) and installed base (FreeStyle Libre has >6 million users globally per company disclosure).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv (as of 2026-08-28 filing lag): composite percentile only 0.029 (live_rank 482/503, not top-30), low ROE percentile — the quant score is unremarkable and did not flag ABT; it reached diligence purely through the triage/quality-growth screen (Q07: quality 4, growth 4, price_vs_growth 4). d4 shows NTM P/E 17.1x, forward P/E 16.7x — cheap for a business compounding adjusted EPS at high-single-digit to low-double-digit rates with 7 beats and 1 miss in the last 8 quarters (d4 beats_last8/misses_last8). The reason the model doesn't rank it highly is mechanical: trailing GAAP earnings are depressed by 2026 acquisition/interest/tax charges (trailing P/E 32.8x vs forward 16.7x), which is an artefact of purchase accounting, not deteriorating quality — see §6.

  • SBC: not separately quantified this pass (limitation; time-boxed).
  • Leverage: total debt jumped from ~$13.2bn (2025-12-31: $9.9bn LT noncurrent + $3.0bn LT current) to ~$34.0bn at 2026-03-31 ($29.6bn LT noncurrent + $4.4bn LT current), funding the Exact Sciences deal — confirmed by an 8-K (items 1.01/2.03, filed 2026-03-09) for a new note issuance. Cash was $6.8bn same date. Total assets roughly doubled at the same date ($86.7bn→$110.4bn), consistent with a ~$21bn purchase price plus goodwill/intangibles from the deal (not independently confirmed to the dollar this pass).
  • M&A: Exact Sciences (cancer diagnostics, Cologuard) — agreed Nov 2025, closed 2026-03-23, debt-funded. Now reported as the "Cancer Diagnostics" segment; comparable sales growth 13.3% in Q2'26. Structural Heart received a one-off competitor compensation payment through Q1 2026 only (final payment recognized then) — a real, disclosed headwind to Structural Heart comps from Q2'26 onward.
  • Share count: ~1,742–1,751M diluted shares over the period, broadly flat to slightly down (buybacks roughly offsetting dilution); not a red flag.
  • Segment note: Nutrition (the legacy, lowest-growth franchise) declined -3.6% comparable in Q2'26 and -5.6% for 1H26, driven by lower volumes and Q4-2025 pricing actions — a real, ongoing soft spot in ~19% of sales, not offset by the new Cancer Diagnostics growth engine in the reported segment mix.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

d4 (2026-09-25 close, price $101.29): NTM P/E 17.1x, FY1 P/E 16.7x, trailing P/E 32.8x (distorted by the FY2024/ 2026 GAAP items above — use NTM/FY1, not trailing, for ABT right now), FCF yield 4.1%, beta 0.59. No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for ABT (not in outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv's 92 covered names) → v1_verdict = null per program rules; this section is this analyst's own reverse DCF (skill script valuation.py), not a reconciliation.

  • EV bridge: market cap $176.4bn + total debt $34.0bn (2026-03-31, latest available) − cash $6.8bn = EV $203.7bn.
  • Reverse DCF (central case): WACC 7.0% (beta 0.59, rf≈4.2%, ERP≈5%), terminal growth 4.0%, base FCF $7.3bn, 10-year stage-1 horizon → implied FCF growth ≈1.5%/yr for 10 years, fading to 4%.
  • Sensitivity: at WACC 8.5% (a more conservative equity discount for a company now carrying real litigation and acquisition-integration risk), implied growth rises to ≈6.4%/yr.
  • My evidence-based base case: mid-single-digit organic/comparable sales growth (company guides 6.5–7.5%) plus margin expansion and Exact Sciences accretion from 2027 onward → 7–9%/yr adjusted FCF/EPS growth over the next decade is a reasonable, not aggressive, base case given the last-8-quarter beat record.
  • Implied vs base: BELOW even under the higher (8.5%) WACC sensitivity. The market is pricing Abbott as if it grows meaningfully slower than its own recent and guided trajectory — consistent with the litigation/ leverage/GAAP-optics discount discussed above, not with a demonstrated growth problem.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) FreeStyle Libre + Cancer Diagnostics (Exact Sciences/Cologuard) are two genuine structural growth engines layered onto a defensive base, each growing double-digit organically. (2) Diversification across four segments and geography (>60% international) smooths any single-franchise shock. (3) A 54-year dividend-increase streak (Dividend Aristocrat, per company's own Q2'26 release) signals capital-allocation discipline even through this leveraged deal.

Bear: (1) Nutrition (~19% of sales) is shrinking, not just decelerating (-5.6% 1H26 organic), and management has not yet shown it can stabilize this segment. (2) Leverage jumped roughly 2.5x in one quarter to fund Exact Sciences; if integration disappoints or synergies are slower than modeled, deleveraging stalls just as NEC settlement cash payments (below) also come due. (3) NEC litigation is not closed: Abbott settled the lead (Gill) verdict plus ~2,000 additional infant claims for ~$670M in August 2026, but ~1,700 lawsuits covering ~12,700 infants remain pending (per company 8-K, Item 8.01, filed 2026-08-20, and contemporaneous press coverage) — the eventual all-in cost is still unknown and could exceed current reserves.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Comparable/organic sales growth guidance cut below 6.5% (current FY26 floor) for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Nutrition segment organic sales decline exceeds -6% for two consecutive quarters (currently -3.6% to -5.6%).
  3. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x (from ~2.3x now) without a clear deleveraging plan disclosed.
  4. A single NEC verdict or settlement tranche (beyond the disclosed ~$670M Gill/2,000-claim settlement) exceeds $1 billion, signaling the remaining ~1,700-suit tail is materially larger than currently priced.
  5. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut (not just narrowed) for a reason other than a disclosed one-time acquisition/tax item.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-14 (Q3 2026, per d4 live snapshot). Q3'26 adjusted EPS already guided $1.38–$1.46 (2026-07-16 release). Watch for: Exact Sciences integration commentary, Nutrition segment trajectory, and any update on the ~1,700 remaining NEC suits.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation (material, quantified in part): NEC (necrotizing enterocolitis) infant-formula mass tort. Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed a $495M jury verdict (Gill case, originally July 2024) in May 2026; rather than pursue further appeal, Abbott settled Gill plus ~2,000 additional infant claims for ~$670M (8-K filed 2026-08-20). ~1,700 suits (~12,700 infants) remain pending in state/federal courts. This is a real, disclosed, partially-quantified tail risk — not a going-concern issue given Abbott's balance sheet and cash flow, but large enough to matter for sizing.
  • Auditor/accounting: No auditor change, restatement, or going-concern language identified this pass (not exhaustively verified against the full FY2025 10-K Item 9A/critical-audit-matters section — time-boxed limitation). The $7.497bn Q4'24 tax valuation-allowance item and the 2026 M&A-driven GAAP/adjusted gap are disclosed, reconciled by the company, and explained above — not treated as a red flag, but as a data-quality point future analysts must not silently average into a "normal" GAAP trend.
  • Data conflict: b1_live_scores.csv ranks ABT outside the top-30 (composite percentile 0.029, live_rank 482/503) largely because trailing GAAP earnings are depressed by the items above; this is a known artefact of the pre-registered model using trailing GAAP inputs, not a positive read on ABT's quality — flagged as a data_conflict below.
  • No insider-selling Form 4 pattern, short-seller report, or auditor resignation identified this pass (not independently pulled from EDGAR Form 4 filings — time-boxed limitation, disclosed).

dossiers.ACN:
ACN — Accenture plc

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — the world's largest IT/management-consulting franchise, priced at 12x NTM earnings (a deep discount to its own 25–30x historical norm) for a business that is genuinely decelerating (revenue growth down to mid-single digits, new bookings down YoY, a real U.S.-federal headwind) but is not broken: margins are still expanding, free cash flow is enormous, and the balance sheet is net cash. Named reservation: bookings turned negative YoY this quarter and the GenAI-disintermediation risk to the core staff-augmentation model is real, not hypothetical, so this is a "priced-for-pessimism" holding, not a clean compounder. Horizon: 24–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

Accenture is the largest global IT and management-consulting firm: it helps large companies and governments redesign business processes, migrate and run IT systems (cloud, ERP, data/AI platforms), and increasingly build and run generative-AI applications, billing mostly on a time-and-materials or managed-services (outsourcing) basis. Revenue splits roughly evenly between project-based Consulting and longer-duration Managed Services; its moat is scale, deep client relationships across every major industry, and the switching costs of ripping out a multi-year outsourcing/systems-integration relationship.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 factor scores: composite percentile 0.90 (top decile), live_rank 50, quintile 5, decile 9 — genuinely strong across families. Quality is excellent and not an artefact (pct_gp_a 0.94, pct_roe 0.73, pct_leverage 0.91 — very low leverage, pct_asset_growth 0.96 — disciplined balance-sheet growth) and Value is strong (pct_fcfp 0.92, pct_ebit_ev 0.97, pct_bp 0.95 — cheap on cash flow, EBIT/EV and book value). Momentum (pct_mom_12_1 ≈0.74) is positive despite the growth deceleration, likely reflecting the stock's re-rating discount bottoming. The quant score is a genuine value-and-quality signal, not a momentum chase; it is durable in the sense that it correctly identifies Accenture as statistically cheap for its quality, but it does not by itself resolve whether the growth deceleration is cyclical (federal budget noise) or the start of secular GenAI erosion — that judgment is made below.
