5. Guidance track record (last 3 releases; Accenture guides full fiscal year at each quarter)

  • Initial FY26 guide (given 2025-09-25, Q4/FY25 release): revenue growth "2% to 5%" in local currency (ex-federal impact "3% to 6%"); GAAP diluted EPS "$13.19 to $13.57."
  • Guide given 2026-03-19 (Q2 FY26 release): revenue growth raised at the low end to "3% to 5%" LC (ex-federal "4% to 6%"); GAAP EPS narrowed to "$13.25 to $13.50" (low end up $0.06, high end down $0.07 vs. initial). "Revenues at the top of the company's guided range" for Q2 itself, per the release headline.
  • Guide given 2026-06-18 (Q3 FY26 release): revenue growth narrowed at the top end to "3% to 4%" LC (ex-federal "4% to 5%") — i.e., the high end of the range was cut from 5% to 4% even as the low end held at 3%; GAAP EPS raised further to "$13.38 to $13.50" (low end up another $0.13). Q3 revenue itself came in "slightly above the midpoint" of the prior quarter's implied range. Net effect over three releases: full-year local-currency revenue-growth guidance has been progressively narrowed from "2–5%" to "3–4%" — the low end was raised early (Q2) and the high end was cut later (Q3); this is a mixed signal (a de-risked, not simply "raised," guide), and I read it as the company converging on ~3.5% LC growth for FY26, at the low end of Accenture's historical range. EPS guidance, by contrast, has been raised at every release. Pending; next report (Q4/FY26 and full-year) ~2026-10-01 per d4 snapshot — imminent.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (Accenture plc — single consolidated reporting entity; no bank/insurer-style

subsidiary capital metrics apply) - FCF conversion: OCF for the nine months ended 2026-05-31 was $9,267.9M against GAAP net income of $6,375.8M for the same period (10-Q XBRL) — FCF/NI (after $492.5M of nine-month capex) is comfortably >1x, i.e. cash earnings exceed accounting earnings, a genuine quality signal (deferred-revenue growth from Managed Services contracts is a contributor). - GAAP vs. adjusted gap: Accenture's own "adjusted" EPS excludes discrete FY25 business-optimization (restructuring) costs; FY26 guide is now GAAP $13.38–13.50 vs. adjusted $13.78–13.90 — the two have converged versus FY25 (which had a larger one-off drag), consistent with the FY25 restructuring program winding down. - Balance sheet (consolidated, 10-Q, 2026-05-31): cash and short-term investments ≈$10,171.6M; total long-term debt (senior notes) $5,029.4M plus $112.8M current portion (commercial paper + other) ≈$5,142M total debt → net cash ≈$5,029M, i.e. Accenture could retire all its debt with cash on hand roughly twice over. Buybacks are large and continuing ($5,193.3M repurchased in the nine months ended 2026-05-31 vs. $4,145.6M in the prior-year period) alongside a $6.52/share annualized dividend (3.7% yield per d4). - M&A: Accenture announced (Q3 FY26 release, 2026-06-18) an agreement to acquire a majority stake in Dragos and all of runZero and NetRise (OT/industrial-cybersecurity firms) — deal value was not disclosed in the press release reviewed; this is a bolt-on capability acquisition consistent with Accenture's steady tuck-in M&A pattern, funded from a large net-cash position, not flagged as a leverage risk. - Litigation: the 10-Q (2026-05-31) states legal proceedings are covered by the Commitments and Contingencies note and that "there have been no material changes to the risk factors disclosed in our Annual Report" (FY25 10-K). No restatement, going-concern, or investigation language found.

7. Valuation snapshot and V1 reconciliation

V1 systematic valuation (v1_valuation_table.csv): verdict "attractive," score 0.98. NTM P/E 12.01x (own-history percentile 56.5th — mid-range, i.e. not at a historic low multiple despite the "cheap" label, because Accenture's own multiple has structurally compressed over the cycle); peer median 11.93x (essentially in line with peers); V1's P/E-implied growth is -5.5% (the price implies the market expects revenue/earnings to shrink); V1's bear/base/bull 3-year annualized returns are 11.6% / 30.2% / 49.7%. V1 also flags its own base case as internally suspect: street_flag = "base 3y value exceeds Street 12m high target" — V1's base-case re-rating (to ~30%/yr for 3 years, implying the price roughly doubles) would put Accenture above even the highest analyst 12-month price target ($275 vs. current $176.11), which V1 itself surfaces as a red flag. I do not fully agree with V1's base case: a full re-rating back to Accenture's mid-2010s–2020 25–30x multiple looks too aggressive given the bookings deceleration and negative YoY bookings this quarter; I use a more conservative reverse-DCF: NTM EPS ≈$14.66, ~5–7%/yr EPS growth (in line with the FY26 EPS guide's 10–11% this year, decelerating toward mid-single-digit consulting/managed-services growth longer term) with a modest re-rating to 14–15x (still below history, reflecting partial resolution of the federal/GenAI overhang) implies roughly base case ~11–13%/yr total return (including the 3.7% dividend and continued buybacks) — well below V1's 30.2%/yr but still comfortably positive and, crucially, below what I believe Accenture can deliver on a normalized basis if the deceleration stabilizes rather than compounds. Bear case: LC growth stays near 2–3%, no re-rating (multiple stays ~12x), federal drag persists longer than guided → roughly 3–5%/yr (mostly the dividend). Bull case: bookings reaccelerate as GenAI transformation work becomes a net new-demand driver rather than a cannibalization risk, multiple re-rates to 17–18x → roughly 20–23%/yr. valuation_view_vs_v1: dossier view cheap, consistent: true in direction (both V1 and I see the stock as statistically cheap) but inconsistent on magnitude — V1's base case is more optimistic than mine (reconciliation: V1's base-case re-rating assumption is not supported by the current bookings trend, and V1 itself flags this via street_flag).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) 12x NTM P/E against an 11.2% FCF yield and a net-cash balance sheet is priced for far more pessimism than a still-growing, margin-expanding franchise (GAAP operating margin +20bps YoY in Q3) usually receives; (2) generative-AI transformation bookings and large ($100M+) client deals are still growing (104 such bookings YTD, up 13%, per the Q3 release) — GenAI may be a net tailwind for large-scale reinvention work, not only a threat to staff-augmentation revenue; (3) $8.2B already returned to shareholders YTD (buybacks + dividends) provides a floor-like capital-return yield even absent a re-rating. Bear: (1) new bookings fell YoY in Q3 FY26 (-2% USD/-3% LC) for the first time in this two-year window — a leading indicator for future revenue, not yet a lagging one; (2) the U.S. federal segment is an acknowledged, guided-for drag (≈1% of FY26 growth) tied to government contract reviews/terminations, and could worsen with further budget actions; (3) the long-run risk that GenAI compresses demand and pricing for traditional staff-augmentation consulting is structural and not yet resolved one way or the other by the data in hand.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Local-currency revenue growth below 3% (the bottom of the FY26 guide) for two consecutive quarters.
  2. New bookings YoY decline (USD) continuing for two more consecutive quarters (one quarter, Q3 FY26, already negative).
  3. U.S. federal segment drag exceeding the guided ~1% impact on full-year local-currency growth (i.e., realized federal drag disclosed at >1.5% in a future quarterly release).
  4. GAAP operating margin expansion stalling or reversing YoY (currently guided to 50–70bps of full-year FY26 expansion; any quarter of YoY margin contraction would break this).
  5. Consolidated net cash position (cash and short-term investments minus total debt, from the 10-Q balance sheet) falling below $2 billion, e.g. from debt-funded M&A (such as Dragos) rather than cash-funded.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-10-01 (Q4/FY26 and full fiscal-year 2026 results) — imminent, only days after this dossier; will show whether the Q3 bookings decline was a one-off or the start of a trend, and will set the initial FY27 guide.
  • Dragos/runZero/NetRise acquisition close (terms/timing not disclosed in the reviewed release) is a near-term item to confirm in the FY26 10-K or a subsequent 8-K.

11. Red-flag scan

No restatement, auditor-change, going-concern, or SEC/DOJ-investigation language found in the reviewed 10-Q (2026-05-31); the filing explicitly states no material change to the FY25 10-K risk factors. No material named litigation beyond the routine Commitments and Contingencies reference. Two disclosed, real (not fabricated) adverse facts carried into this dossier from the triage/lead audit: U.S. federal government segment revenue pressure from 2025 federal budget/efficiency-driven contract reviews, and the long-run GenAI staff-augmentation risk. Insider Form-4 pattern was not independently checked this pass (limitation).

dossiers.ADBE:
ADBE — Adobe Inc. (Application Software, Information Technology)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 12–36 month horizon. Adobe is priced by the market as if genAI will structurally erode Creative Cloud, but the reverse DCF shows the stock needs 10 years of shrinking free cash flow to justify today's price, while the company is actually growing revenue and FCF double-digits and buying back ~5–7% of its share count a year. Sized small, not full weight, because the core bear case (AI-native tools substituting for paid seats) is genuinely unresolved and the company just lost both its CEO and CFO within six months.

2. Business in plain English

Adobe sells subscription software: Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, and the Firefly generative-AI tools bundled into it) to designers, marketers, photographers and students; Document Cloud (Acrobat/PDF, e-signature) to every knowledge worker; and Experience Cloud (marketing/analytics platforms) to enterprises. Revenue is ~97% subscription, billed annually or monthly, so it is recurring and priced with high switching costs (file formats, muscle memory, team workflows). It makes money the way most SaaS companies do: high (~89%) gross margin, low incremental cost per seat, most of the cost base is R&D, sales/marketing and content-delivery infrastructure. Its competitive position is entrenchment in professional creative and document workflows against a wave of new AI-native point tools (Midjourney, Sora, Figma, Canva) that can each do a slice of what Adobe does, for less.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Adobe screens at the very top of the v4 quant model's composite (composite_qvm 0.885, decile 8/10, rank 118): quality (fam_Q 0.99 — gross-profit/assets 98th pct, ROE 84th pct) and value (fam_V 0.92 — FCF/price 93rd pct, earnings yield 92nd pct) are both exceptional, while momentum is in the bottom quintile (fam_M 0.166, 12-month momentum 17th pct) and the earnings-surprise/sentiment factor is also weak (fam_S 0.326, SUE 33rd pct). This is a classic contrarian value-versus-momentum split, not an artefact: quality and value are computed straight from filed financials that are, in fact, still growing (revenue +13% y/y, non-GAAP EPS +15% y/y in the most recent quarter); the weak momentum/sentiment factors are the market's real-time verdict on the AI-disruption narrative and the Q4 revenue guide landing a hair below consensus. Both readings are correct simultaneously: the business is executing, and the market is discounting it hard for a risk that has not yet shown up in the numbers.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: TTM operating cash flow ≈ $10.81B (Q4 FY25 implied $3.16B + 9-mo FY26 $7.65B), TTM capex only ≈ $214M (asset-light) → TTM FCF ≈ $10.6B, FCF/NI ≈ 1.5x (net income is held down by SBC and tax vs. cash generation) — high-quality cash conversion.

  • GAAP vs. adjusted gap: non-GAAP EPS excludes SBC and a small amortization/restructuring layer; FY26 guide shows GAAP EPS ($18.12–18.17) vs. non-GAAP ($24.45–24.50), a ~35% gap — normal for Adobe's history, not widening.

  • M&A: none pending of note.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

NTM P/E (non-GAAP consensus basis, per v1_valuation_table.csv) = 8.7x — the 0th percentile of Adobe's own 5–10-year history (all-time cheapest), vs. a peer median of ~15.4x (Autodesk, Salesforce-type application-software comps). FCF yield ≈ 10.6–11.3% (TTM FCF / market cap of $93.6B).

V1's systematic model: verdict attractive, implied_growth_or_roe −2.3% (i.e., its NTM-multiple-based method also reads the stock as priced for shrinkage), but its bear/base/bull 3-year annualized returns of 19.1% / 72.4% / 114.6% are not credible at face value — a 72%/year base-case return for three years running would be one of the great trades in history from a mega-cap, and the same table flags itself with street_flag: "base 3y value exceeds Street 12m high target". I agree with V1's direction (cheap, growth priced in is below a reasonable base case) and disagree with the magnitude of its return output — logged as a data conflict below.

My own 10-year reverse DCF (EV ≈ $94.0B; TTM FCF $10.6B; WACC 8.5–10%, terminal growth 3–4%): the market is pricing in a −4% to −8% per-year FCF decline for 10 years, robust across the assumption grid. My evidence-based base case is Adobe growing FCF at a high-single to low-double-digit rate (revenue growth ~9–13%, plus buyback-driven share shrink, minus modest AI-infrastructure cost drag) — well above what's priced in. - Bear case (AI-native tools genuinely erode seat growth and pricing power over 2–3 years): FCF growth slows to ~2%/yr, multiple stays at trough (~8–9x EV/FCF) → ~+10%/yr 3-year annualized return (still modestly positive because the entry multiple is so depressed). - Base case (growth continues near current pace, AI-disruption fear only partially resolves): FCF growth ~12%/yr, multiple re-rates modestly to ~11.5x → ~+22%/yr. - Bull case (Firefly/AI-first ARR scales and the disruption thesis is discredited): FCF growth ~16%/yr, multiple re-rates to the ~15x peer median → ~+38%/yr.

valuation_view_vs_v1: dossier view = cheap, consistent = true on direction (both models say priced below base case), inconsistent on V1's specific 3-yr return magnitude (see data conflicts).

8. Bull case

  1. Firefly/AI-first ARR is real and compounding fast (+150% y/y, >$650M ARR, Firefly ARR +40% q/q) — Adobe is monetizing generative AI as an add-on to, not a replacement for, its core seats.
  2. The stock is at the cheapest multiple in its history (0th percentile) while revenue growth has not decelerated for eight straight quarters (10–13% every quarter since FY24).
  3. Balance sheet is nearly debt-free, buybacks are shrinking share count ~5–6%/year, and management has a $25B authorization still to deploy.

9. Bear case

  1. Generative AI tools (OpenAI/Sora, Midjourney, and Figma/Canva at the workflow layer) are a genuine, still-developing threat to Creative Cloud seat growth; the Q4 guide (in line to slightly light) is the first data point the market has read as early evidence, even though Adobe itself denies deceleration.
  2. Two C-suite departures within six months (CEO Narayen → Chakravarthy effective 1 Dec 2026; CFO Dan Durn's exit disclosed with Q2 FY26 results) create real execution and continuity risk exactly when the AI strategy needs steady-handed defense.
  3. A $150M DOJ/FTC "dark pattern" settlement (below) signals a company that let growth-at-all-costs subscription tactics get ahead of compliance — a governance yellow flag, not just a fine.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Digital Media (Creative + Document Cloud) segment ARR growth falls below 8% y/y for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Firefly/AI-first ending ARR quarter-over-quarter growth falls below 15% for two consecutive quarters (the AI-monetization bridge stalling).
  3. A second senior-leadership departure (CEO, CFO, or a business-unit president) is announced within 12 months of the Dec-2026 CEO handover.
  4. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.0x (i.e., debt-funded buybacks beyond organic FCF + the $25B authorization).
  5. A quarterly revenue guide is cut (not just merely in-line) versus the prior quarter's stated range.

11. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: ~10 Dec 2026 (Q4/FY26 results; date is management-confirmed, not an estimate).
  • CEO transition effective 1 Dec 2026 (Anil Chakravarthy becomes President & CEO; Narayen becomes Executive Chair) — first earnings call under new CEO will be the Q4 print days later.
  • CFO search: unresolved as of this writing; a permanent CFO announcement is a catalyst to watch.
  • $25B buyback authorization: pace of execution each quarter is disclosed in the 10-Q cash-flow statement.

12. Red-flag scan

Adobe denies wrongdoing but must now prominently disclose termination fees and simplify cancellation.
  • Insider selling: CEO Shantanu Narayen sold ~125,000 shares (≈34% of his direct/indirect position) for $31.3M on 16–17 Sep 2026 at $246–$254/share, stated as tax/estate planning — notable timing (one week after the new-CEO announcement, ahead of the December handover), disclosed via Form 4, not obviously alarming but worth tracking for a pattern.

dossiers.ADI:
ADI — Analog Devices, Inc. (Semiconductors, Information Technology)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 12–36 month horizon. Analog Devices is executing exceptionally (three straight quarters of beat-and-raise, a genuinely new secular AI-data-center leg alongside a normal industrial/auto cyclical recovery) and its balance sheet is sound. Sized small, not full weight, because the reverse DCF shows the market has already priced in 10-year FCF growth (~9–14% depending on discount-rate assumption) that is at the upper edge of — and by some readings modestly above — a prudent through-cycle base case for an analog semiconductor company, and the stock is trading near its highest-ever revenue run-rate, which the sector's own playbook flags as exactly the point multiples look least trustworthy.

2. Business in plain English

Analog Devices designs and sells analog, mixed-signal and DSP chips — the components that convert real-world signals (voltage, temperature, motion, radio-frequency) into digital data and back — into industrial automation, automotive (EV powertrain, ADAS, in-cabin), communications infrastructure (including AI data-center power and connectivity) and consumer electronics. It sells through direct enterprise relationships and distributors, with long (5–10+ year) product design cycles once a chip is "designed in" to a customer's product, which makes revenue sticky but also slow to re-accelerate after a design loss. It earns money on high gross margins (~65–67%) typical of analog IP with long product lifecycles and low process-node intensity relative to logic/memory chips.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

ADI's composite_qvm score (0.503, decile 7, rank 173) is unremarkable overall, but the composition matters: momentum (fam_M 0.683, 69th pct) and earnings-surprise/sentiment (fam_S 0.723, 72nd pct) are doing the work, while quality (fam_Q 0.399 — gross-profit/assets only 29th pct, ROE 25th pct) and value (fam_V 0.419, FCF/price 40th pct) are middling. This is the mirror image of ADBE: ADI is being re-rated on execution momentum during a cyclical recovery, not because it screens as statistically cheap or exceptionally profitable on trailing numbers. That is a durable but cycle-dependent reason — real (three consecutive quarters of guide-and-beat, an AI-data-center growth leg that did not exist at the prior cycle peak), but it will fade automatically once the base effect from the FY24 trough laps, so the momentum score should not be read as a standing quality signal.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: per the company's own Q3 FY26 release, TTM operating cash flow ≈ $5.5B and TTM free cash flow ≈ $4.9B — a strong ~90% OCF-to-FCF conversion (capex 9-mo FY26 $392.7M, ≈2.8% of TTM revenue, modest for a semiconductor IDM but rising from $318.4M in the year-ago period as the company invests into demand).

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

No V1 systematic-model row exists for ADI in v1_valuation_table.csv — v1_verdict set to null, this section is my own work. Vendor NTM P/E ≈ 24.4–24.6x (forward PE 24.1x per d4 snapshot), against a semiconductor/analog peer set (Texas Instruments typically 30x+, Microchip, NXP, ON Semiconductor in the high teens to low 20s) — roughly in line with, to a modest discount versus, its highest-quality direct peer (TI), and above the broader analog/industrial peer group, consistent with its recent execution premium.

10-year reverse DCF (EV ≈ $196.7B [$190.7B market cap + $5.95B net debt]; TTM FCF $4.9B): solving for the uniform 10-year FCF growth rate that justifies the current EV, holding terminal growth at 3–4%: - At WACC 7.5%: implied growth 7.6–10.0%/yr. - At WACC 8.0–8.5% (my central estimate given ADI's low beta and investment-grade balance sheet): implied growth 9.3–12.8%/yr. - At WACC 9.0%: implied growth 12.4–14.1%/yr.

My evidence-based base case is company-level FCF compounding at ~9–11%/yr through a full cycle — built from ADI's own 15-year organic-plus-M&A revenue CAGR (~9–10%, 2010–2025), a few points of structural upside from the new AI-data-center leg (Communications +84% y/y this quarter did not exist as a growth driver at the FY23 peak), offset by the industry's well-documented capex/inventory cyclicality (the FY24 trough is only two years behind us). The market-implied range (9–14%) straddles this base case rather than sitting clearly below it — this is the honest, sensitivity-tested conclusion, not a forced one. I classify this as implied_vs_base = "in_line".

  • Bear case: AI-data-center demand normalizes and the industrial/auto recovery stalls; FCF growth ~2%/yr for 3 years, multiple compresses from ~40x EV/FCF to ~30x → ~ −6%/yr 3-year annualized return net of dividend.
  • Base case: FCF growth ~11%/yr, multiple roughly flat (already fair) → ~+12%/yr including dividend.
  • Bull case: the AI-data-center leg proves structural and industrial/auto keep compounding; FCF growth ~18%/yr, multiple re-rates modestly toward TI's premium (~45x) → ~+23–24%/yr.

8. Bull case

  1. Three consecutive quarters of beat-and-raise with broad-based growth (industrial, comms, auto all up double-digits) — this is not a single-end-market or single-customer story.
  2. A genuinely new, structural AI-data-center demand leg (Communications segment +84% y/y) layered on top of the normal cyclical recovery, which the market has not fully distinguished from ordinary cyclicality.
  3. Investment-grade balance sheet with net debt/EBITDA ≈ 0.86x and falling as Maxim-era debt is retired, leaving capacity for further buybacks or M&A.

9. Bear case

  1. Revenue is at a fresh all-time-high run-rate (TTM ~13% above the FY23 cyclical peak); the sector's own playbook explicitly warns that record-quarter P/E multiples are the classic way to buy an analog/semis cycle top, and my reverse DCF shows growth priced in is at the upper edge of (not clearly below) a fair base case.
  2. Two disclosed 2026 cybersecurity incidents (data exfiltration confirmed 23 Jun 2026; a second, unrelated matter under assessment as of 26 Jul 2026) carry unquantified financial/reputational/litigation tail risk (a class-action solicitation was already reported).
  3. The Q3 FY25 tax-rate swing and the general reliance on adjusted (ex-Maxim-amortization) EPS mean the GAAP-to-adjusted bridge needs to be re-checked every quarter rather than assumed stable.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Sequential revenue turns negative for two consecutive quarters after the current record run.
  2. Communications (AI data-center) segment growth decelerates to below 20% y/y for two consecutive quarters.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x (from M&A or leveraged buybacks).
  4. Either 2026 cybersecurity incident is confirmed to have caused a quantified customer, contractual, or regulatory financial impact.
  5. Adjusted operating margin falls below 48% for two consecutive quarters (a utilisation/pricing-driven margin-compression signal that the cycle has turned).

  • Q4 FY26 guide (revenue $4.3B ±$100M) is the next test of the beat-and-raise streak.
  • Ongoing disclosure obligations on the two 2026 cybersecurity incidents (any material update would be 8-K-reportable).

A second, unrelated cybersecurity matter was flagged 26 Jul 2026 and was still being assessed for validity as of the search window. A plaintiffs'-side site (classaction.org) was already soliciting potential breach litigants as of this review — a class action is possible but not yet filed as far as this search found.

1. Verdict

Mission-critical, high-switching-cost payroll/HR platform delivering above-guidance growth every quarter this fiscal year; the reverse DCF shows the market pricing in less growth (≈4.2%/yr, 10y) than management's own guided FY27 trajectory (revenue +5–6%, adjusted EPS +9–11%). 2. Business in plain English

ADP processes payroll, tax filing, benefits administration and HR compliance for ~1.1 million clients (Employer Services) and acts as a co-employer / PEO for small and mid-size businesses (Workforce Now / TotalSource). It earns per-employee/per-transaction fees plus a secondary but material stream from investing client payroll funds it briefly holds before remittance ("client funds interest," roughly 15–20% of pretax earnings and directly geared to short-term interest rates). The moat is switching costs (payroll is high-stakes, low-visibility infrastructure that employers rarely re-platform) plus scale in compliance content (tax tables, benefits rules across every US jurisdiction).

Sector routing note: GICS labels ADP "Human Resource & Employment Services" → the stock-analysis skill router maps this to people-businesses.md. 8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Client-funds interest income is a structural tailwind as long as short rates stay above zero — a multi-year annuity ADP does not have to "earn" through sales effort. 2. New-business bookings and retention have both been resilient through a soft small-business hiring cycle, suggesting share gains against smaller competitors (Paychex, Gusto, Rippling) rather than market softness. 3. Margin expansion (+140bps in Q4 alone) shows real operating leverage still available in a business the market already treats as mature.

Bear (3): 1. Client-funds interest income falls mechanically if the Fed cuts rates faster than the curve currently implies — a real, quantifiable headwind to adjusted EBIT that is macro, not company-specific. 2. Well-funded, product-led challengers (Gusto, Rippling, Deel) are taking share in the smallest-employer segment where switching costs are lowest; ADP's own growth is concentrated in larger, stickier accounts. 3. At 23.7x trailing earnings for high-single-digit growth, there is little room for a guidance miss without multiple compression on top of any earnings miss.

  2. Adjusted EBIT margin guidance cut (vs. the +70–90bps FY27 guide) at any quarterly release.

  • EV bridge: market cap $43.8bn + total debt $3.5bn (2026-07-31, pre-MaintainX-close) − cash $4.1bn = EV $43.2bn (net cash position of ~$0.6bn at this date — will flip to a net debt position once MaintainX's ~$2bn of new financing and cash use are reflected).
  • Reverse DCF (central case): WACC 10.5% (beta 1.31, rf≈4.2%, ERP≈5.5%), terminal growth 4.0%, base FCF $2.9bn, 10-year stage-1 horizon → implied FCF growth ≈3.0%/yr for 10 years, fading to 4%.
  • Sensitivity: at WACC 12% (reflecting integration/leverage risk from MaintainX), implied growth rises to ≈5.9%/yr.
  • My evidence-based base case: 14–18% revenue growth has held for eight straight quarters even through a restructuring year; with MaintainX cross-sell and continued operating leverage (non-GAAP operating margin already ~41%), 11–14%/yr FCF/EPS growth over the next decade is a reasonable base case (below recent revenue growth to allow for deceleration as the base scales and integration costs).
  • Implied vs base: BELOW, even under the higher (12%) WACC sensitivity. The market is pricing Autodesk for materially slower compounding than its demonstrated run-rate, which is consistent with the stock still carrying some discount from the 2024–25 SEC/DOJ overhang and now the MaintainX integration-risk discount.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) 8-for-8 revenue beats over the trailing two years (d4 beats_last8=8, misses_last8=0) with accelerating non-GAAP margins (41% in Q2 FY27 vs 39% a year earlier). (2) MaintainX extends Autodesk from "design/build" software into recurring "operate" software for the same industrial customer base — a genuine adjacency, not a diversification into an unrelated market. (3) The Starboard Value activist situation resolved constructively in 2025 (two new independent directors, no ongoing proxy fight), removing a governance overhang while its cost-discipline pressure likely contributed to the margin gains now showing up.

Bear: (1) MaintainX is Autodesk's largest-ever deal, all-cash, funded partly with new debt, closing right at the point this dossier's balance-sheet data runs out — integration risk is real and unpriced in the numbers shown here. (2) The 2024 Audit Committee investigation into free-cash-flow and non-GAAP operating-margin practices (closed without restatement in August 2025) revealed that Autodesk had historically "engaged in programs designed to incentivize customers to accept multiyear upfront billing, renew early, and/or pay before the end of the fiscal year" to hit FCF targets — a genuine historical earnings-quality flag on how FCF/billings were managed, even though no restatement resulted; worth discounting FCF-based valuation multiples slightly until a few more clean quarters build a track record post-investigation. (3) RPO/unbilled deferred revenue growth (+2% YoY) is running well below revenue growth (+16%), partly explained by the multi-year-discount wind-down (§6) but still a metric to watch for any real demand deceleration hiding behind that explanation.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Quarterly revenue growth decelerates below 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from the current 16-18% run-rate).
  2. Non-GAAP operating margin contracts more than 200bps YoY for two consecutive quarters (from ~41% now), signaling MaintainX integration costs are structural rather than one-time.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA (post-MaintainX-close) exceeds 2.0x with no disclosed deleveraging plan.
  4. Total RPO growth stays below 5% YoY for three consecutive quarters after the multi-year-discount wind-down should have annualized out of the comparison (i.e., the explanation in §6 stops holding).
  5. A new SEC/DOJ inquiry or restatement is announced (the 2024–25 investigation closed clean, but the underlying billing-incentive practices it examined warrant continued vigilance).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-11-27 (Q3 FY27, per d4 live snapshot) — first quarter to show a full period of MaintainX consolidation and the post-close balance sheet. Q3 FY27 revenue already guided $2,125–$2,140M, GAAP EPS $1.57–$1.87, non-GAAP EPS $3.04–$3.09 (2026-08-27 release).

  • Regulatory (resolved): In March 2024, Autodesk's Audit Committee opened an internal investigation into free-cash-flow and non-GAAP operating-margin practices and voluntarily notified the SEC; the SEC and USAO closed their respective matters in August 2025 with no restatement or adjustment of any GAAP or non-GAAP financial statements (per company disclosure, cross-checked via web search of SEC filing summaries).   • Governance (resolved constructively): Starboard Value built a ~$500M stake and pushed for a proxy fight ahead of the 2025 annual meeting; Autodesk settled by adding two new independent directors (Jeff Epstein, Christie Simons), who became full voting board members after the 2025-06-18 annual meeting. Not an ongoing governance red flag.
  • M&A/leverage (emerging, not yet in the filed numbers): MaintainX closing (2026-08-03) and its financing are the single largest near-term swing factor for this name and are not reflected in any balance sheet sourced in this dossier — explicitly flagged as the reservation behind the INCLUDE-SMALL verdict rather than folded silently into the numbers.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — A genuinely improving specialty-insurance franchise (Connected Living volume growth, disciplined Global Housing underwriting, shrinking share count, rising holding-company liquidity) trading at a full-but-not-extreme valuation, with a real, company-disclosed EPS deceleration mechanism baked into H2 2026 that the market may not fully be pricing given persistent price-target raises. Thesis horizon: 12–24 months.

2. The Business

Assurant is a specialty insurance holding company operating two segments. Global Lifestyle (77.5% of FY2025 net earned premiums, fees and other income of $9,582.5M [FY2025 10-K, Global Lifestyle segment table, filed 2026-02-19]) sells mobile device protection/trade-in, extended service contracts, and credit/financial-services insurance through mobile carriers and retailers ("Connected Living," $5,378.7M FY2025, +11.9% YoY), plus vehicle and commercial-equipment protection ("Global Automotive," $4,203.8M FY2025, +1.1% YoY) [FY2025 10-K, filed 2026-02-19]. Global Housing (22.5% of segment revenue, $2,768.8M FY2025 [FY2025 10-K]) underwrites lender-placed homeowners/flood/manufactured-home insurance plus renters and specialty products — genuine catastrophe-exposed underwriting risk. Global Lifestyle is best analyzed as a capital-light, fee/administration-heavy business with a real but secondary loss-ratio component (its own Adjusted EBITDA margin is only ~8% of revenue [FY2025 10-K] because commissions to carrier/retail partners and cost of trade-in inventory dominate the cost base); Global Housing is the true underwriting business where combined-ratio-style economics and catastrophe exposure matter most. Assurant simplified its portfolio further in FY2025-26: a legacy run-off subsidiary holding fully-reinsured individual life, annuity and long-term-care blocks (reinsured to John Hancock) was classified held-for-sale in Q4 2025 and sold in March 2026 for an $11.2M cumulative loss on sale [FY2025 10-K Note 3; Q2 2026 10-Q Note 4, filed 2026-08-06] — following the larger 2021 Global Preneed divestiture to CUNA Mutual ($1.35B) [company press release, 2021-08-02, pre-dating this dossier's window but relevant context].

3. Why the Model Likes It

The 0.80 composite is driven by Quality (0.859) and Momentum (0.834) percentiles, with Value (0.711) more modest [lead_prelim_rank.csv]. Momentum is evidenced, not manufactured: revenue grew every quarter for the last six at +6.7% to +11.3% YoY [derived from 10-K/10-Q XBRL, see §4], adjusted EPS ex-catastrophes grew double-digits, and guidance has been raised three times in the last four releases with the raises subsequently validated by actuals (§5) — this looks like a genuine re-rating on improving fundamentals rather than a hot run into an air pocket, except that the improvement in Global Housing profitability (Adjusted EBITDA +28% FY2025 [FY2025 10-K]) is partly a function of $113.1M of favorable prior-year reserve development (PYD) in 2025 on top of $106.7M in 2024 [FY2025 10-K MD&A, filed 2026-02-19] — a two-year tailwind management itself says will not repeat in H2 2026 (§4, §6). Quality (ROE ~15.9% on a full-year-average-equity GAAP basis, rising from 13.4% FY2023 [ratios.py output on 10-K data]; OCF/NI of 2.10x FY2025) is real but partly inflated by that same reserve-development windfall and by two years of below-average catastrophe losses. Value at the 71st percentile is driven by a trailing P/E of ~13x-15x, not by a discount to book — on a P/B basis (~2.15x) the stock is fully valued for its current ROE (§7). Net read: momentum and quality are directionally real (Connected Living growth, buybacks, improving underwriting discipline) but a meaningful share of the last two years' earnings beats rode a fading reserve-development tailwind, not a permanent step-change in loss experience.

Financial leverage (debt/(debt+equity), carrying value): 27.3% at FY2025-end ($2,206.9M/$8,078.5M), improving to 26.6% at Q2 2026-end ($2,208.1M/$8,306.0M) [10-K Note 18; Q2 2026 10-Q], both comfortably inside the credit facility's 35% maximum covenant [FY2025 10-K, filed 2026-02-19] and within the sector-playbook comfort zone. Debt maturities: no maturities until March 2028 ($300M) and February 2030 ($350M) after Assurant refinanced the February-2026 notes early via a $300M 5.55% 2036 issuance in August 2025 [FY2025 10-K, Note 18]. Buybacks: repurchased 1.4M shares for $299.9M in FY2025 plus $168.4M dividends; Board authorized an additional $700M program in November 2025 (on top of the November 2023 $600M program), leaving $774.6M unused at 12/31/2025 [FY2025 10-K, Item 5 and Note 18]; diluted share count fell from 53.78M (FY2023) to 49.38M (Q2 2026), roughly –8% [XBRL].

7. Valuation Snapshot

Primary method (P/B vs. sustainable operating ROE), per insurance.md. Current P/B ≈ 2.15x ($265.00 price / $123.48 book value per share, using Q2 2026 equity $6,097.9M ÷ 49.382M shares [Q2 2026 10-Q] — this exactly matches the quant pipeline's independently-computed $123.48 book value/share and 2.146x P/B [d4_live_snapshot.parquet], a clean cross-check). GAAP ROE on a full-year-average-equity basis was 15.9% in FY2025, up from 15.3% (FY2024) and 13.4% (FY2023) [ratios.py output on 10-K data]. Stripping catastrophes and the FY2025 PYD windfall from net income (adjusted-ex-cat EPS $22.81 × 51.09M diluted shares ≈ $1,165M, less ~$89M after-tax PYD benefit, over average equity of $5,489M) implies a "cleaned" sustainable operating ROE of roughly 17-20% (analyst estimate, not company-reported). Applying the justified-multiple relation P/B ≈ (ROE − g)/(COE − g) with a conservative g=4% and a sector-typical COE=10% (insurance.md's own P&C benchmark, chosen over a mechanical CAPM figure because AIZ's trailing beta of 0.542 [d4_live_snapshot.parquet] likely understates true cost of equity given catastrophe tail risk): ROE=18% implies P/B≈2.33x; ROE=16% implies P/B≈2.00x; ROE=17% implies P/B≈2.17x — i.e., the current 2.15x multiple is roughly what a mid-to-high-teens sustainable ROE justifies; the stock is not obviously cheap on this framework, though it sits at the low end of the 2-4x band the playbook associates with 15-18% ROE/sub-95%-combined-ratio franchises. Secondary (P/E on operating EPS): trailing P/E on FY2025 adjusted-ex-cat EPS ($22.81) is 11.6x; on GAAP EPS ($16.93, TTM $20.94) it is ~15.7x/12.7x — below the 10-16x diversified-P&C band's midpoint, consistent with the Value factor score. Peers: The Hartford (HIG) trades at ~1.90x P/B against an ~18.7-20.3% TTM core ROE [gurufocus/company 8-K via web search, 2026-09]; Old Republic (ORI) trades at ~9.0x P/E [AAII, 2026-09-11]; Kemper (KMPR) is currently loss-making (negative TTM ROE) [CNBC/company data, 2026-09-17] and is not a clean comparator right now. AIZ's niche (lender-placed/warranty) has few exact pure-plays, as expected. Suppressed and why: EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales and a raw FCF-yield DCF are explicitly not used as primary evidence per insurance.md (debt is not financing against a policyholder-liability balance sheet). Illustratively, valuation.py's reverse-DCF on an OCF-minus-capex FCF proxy ($1,618.8M) against the EV bridge ($13,595.6M) implies the market is pricing in only –5.8% FCF growth for 10 years at a 10% WACC — a nonsensical-looking output that itself demonstrates why the sector playbook bans this method here: this year's OCF is flattered by float timing and the same reserve-release dynamic discussed in §4, not a repeatable distributable-cash base.

8. Bull Case and Bear Case

Bull case

  1. Global Lifestyle's Connected Living unit grew net earned premiums+fees +11.9% in FY2025 on real mobile-subscriber and financial-services-program growth, not pricing/assumption changes [FY2025 10-K].
  2. Balance sheet has gotten safer, not riskier, while returning capital: financial leverage improved from ~29.0% (FY2024) to ~26.6% (Q2 2026), holding-company liquidity nearly doubled from $613M (Q3 2025) to $911.5M (Q2 2026), and the Board added a fresh $700M buyback authorization in November 2025 [FY2025 10-K; Q2 2026 10-Q].
  3. Management has been transparent, not evasive, about the H2 2026 reserve-development comp headwind, disclosing the exact dollar mechanics three quarters running — a credibility signal, not a red flag, and the underlying (ex-PYD, ex-cat) FY2026 guide of "approximately 10%" growth as of August 2026 has only been raised, never cut, in the last four releases [Q1/Q2 2026, Q3/Q4 2025 8-Ks].

Bear case

  1. Two consecutive years of unusually large favorable prior-year reserve development ($106.7M FY2024, $113.1M FY2025, both in Global Housing) inflated reported and adjusted EPS; management guides essentially zero incremental PYD for H2 2026, so the "8-for-8 beat, 8-for-8 raise" pattern investors have priced in may not mechanically continue on the reported line even if the ex-PYD business is healthy [FY2025 10-K MD&A; Q2 2026 8-K].
  2. Global Housing remains genuinely catastrophe-exposed (Hurricane Helene alone cost $92M pre-tax in Q3 2024); FY2025's much lower cat impact ($198.8M vs $245.2M pre-tax) partly reflects a milder hurricane year, not a structural improvement, and can reverse [FY2025 10-K; special 8-Ks, 2024].
  3. At ~2.15x P/B against an analyst-estimated 17-20% "cleaned" sustainable ROE and a 10% cost of equity, the stock is priced for continued high-teens returns with little margin of safety; analyst sentiment is already fully bought-in (8 of 8 recent price-target actions were raises, strong-buy consensus, zero downgrades in 90 days per d4_live_snapshot.parquet), leaving asymmetric downside if H2 2026 prints disappoint even modestly relative to the now-elevated bar.

9. Key Risks & Kill Criteria — What Would Invalidate This Thesis

  1. Global Housing's analyst-computed combined-ratio-equivalent (policyholder benefits + expenses, over net earned premium — see §3/§7 methodology) rises above ~85% for two consecutive quarters (vs. ~79.4% FY2025), signaling the underwriting improvement was reserve-driven, not structural.
  2. FY2026 adjusted-EPS-ex-cat guidance is cut (not merely decelerated on the already-disclosed PYD comp) at the Q3 2026 (on/around 2026-11-03) or Q4 2026 (~Feb 2027) release versus the August-2026 raised range ("mid single digits" headline / "approximately 10%" ex-PYD).
  3. Holding-company liquidity falls back below ~$500M without a clearly disclosed one-off cause (vs. $836-911.5M over the last two quarters).
  4. A single reportable-catastrophe quarter exceeds roughly $150M pre-tax in Global Housing (worse than Q3 2024's Hurricane-Helene-driven $138M) with evidence of reinsurance-recoverable strain or a materially higher retention.
  5. Financial leverage (debt/total capital, carrying value) rises above ~32% (approaching the 35% covenant) via debt-funded buybacks/M&A, or any rated insurance subsidiary is downgraded from A.M. Best "A."

10. Catalysts & Calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026, estimated 2026-11-03 [d4_live_snapshot.parquet estimate] — not yet confirmed by the company in any filing checked (no 8-K scheduling notice found as of 2026-09-25). AJG — Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F38, Wave-2 Standard)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Reservation: reported growth (+13% to +31% YoY across recent quarters) is now almost entirely acquisition-driven. Organic growth in the core Brokerage base commissions/fees has run only 4% in both Q1 and Q2 2026 (vs AJG's historical high-single-digit organic pace), and the pace of new bolt-on M&A has itself slowed (6 deals closed in Q2'26 vs 9 a year earlier; $58M of acquired annualized revenue vs $291M), consistent with leverage (~2.8-3.0x net debt/EBITDA) constraining the very M&A engine the triage praised. The business is high-quality and the price is undemanding, but the growth-durability story needs the next 2-3 quarters to show organic re-acceleration before this is a full-conviction position.

2. Business in plain English

Arthur J. Gallagher is an insurance broker and risk-management consultant: it places commercial and personal insurance for clients with third-party insurance carriers (earning commissions and fees) and separately sells third-party claims administration and risk-consulting services (Risk Management segment, "Gallagher Bassett"). It underwrites no insurance risk itself — it is a distribution and advisory platform, so its economics are closer to an asset-light services business (people, client relationships, data) than to an insurer's balance sheet. Growth comes from two engines: organic (new business, retention, exposure/rate) and an unusually active tuck-in M&A program (independent agencies acquired and folded onto Gallagher's platform), most recently supercharged by the ~$13.45bn acquisition of AssuredPartners, financed in December 2024 and reflected in results since.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv: composite percentile only 0.009 (live_rank 492/503) — the quant model does not like AJG; it reached diligence through the triage/quality-growth screen only (Q05: quality 4, growth 4, price_vs_growth 4, citing 31% revenue growth and a "38x trailing P/E [that] looks cheap once one-time integration costs are stripped out"). This research confirms the triage's own caveat was directionally right — the 38x trailing P/E is indeed distorted by AssuredPartners integration/amortization costs (§6) — but also finds the triage's growth read was too generous: 31% reported growth is ~25-27 points of M&A and only ~4-5 points organic (§4-5), a distinction the triage's reason field did not make. The low quant score is at least partly a real signal (leverage percentile and net-share-issuance from deal financing would penalize AJG in the Quality family), not purely an artefact — flagged as a data_conflict below.

This is the least clear-cut of this analyst's three names: unlike ABT and ADSK, a modestly higher (and, given the leverage, defensible) WACC assumption would flip the reverse-DCF read from "cheap" to "roughly fair" — disclosed explicitly rather than picking the WACC that produces the more flattering answer.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Top-3 global insurance broker with genuinely durable moats (client relationships, specialty expertise, scale in placement/analytics) and a decades-long track record of successful tuck-in M&A. (2) Even at a slowed pace, the M&A engine is still adding real revenue (6-8 deals/quarter), and deleveraging from the AssuredPartners deal should restore capacity for more over the next 2-3 years. (3) Client retention and new business generation both described as "strong"/"outstanding" by management (Q2'26 release) — a qualitative but consistent management claim across releases, not new spin introduced this quarter.

Bear: (1) The headline growth numbers the triage screen liked (31% revenue growth) are overwhelmingly M&A, not organic; organic growth of 4-5% is unremarkable for an insurance broker and well below AJG's own historical high-single-digit organic pace — if this is the new normal (hard commercial insurance-rate cycle turning soft, or genuine competitive share loss), the re-rating case weakens materially. (2) Leverage (~2.8x net debt/EBITDA) is the highest in recent company history and is already visibly constraining the bolt-on M&A pace that is the second growth engine — a negative feedback loop if organic growth doesn't independently reaccelerate. (3) The GAAP/adjusted EPS gap has widened for two consecutive years running; a persistently widening gap between "what shareholders can spend" (dividends, buybacks — funded by cash/adjusted earnings) and "what GAAP reports" is a legitimate long-run earnings-quality concern for a serial acquirer, even when each individual adjustment is well-disclosed.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Total organic change (AJG's own combined Brokerage + Risk Management metric) stays below 5% for three consecutive quarters (currently 4-5% in Q1-Q2'26; below AJG's historical high-single-digit norm).
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x (from ~2.8x now) without a disclosed deleveraging plan.
  3. Quarterly acquired-annualized-revenue run-rate stays below $100M (vs $291-354M a year ago) for three more consecutive quarters, signaling the M&A engine has not recovered capacity.
  4. The GAAP-vs-adjusted EPS gap widens by more than $0.50/share YoY again in a quarter with no new large acquisition to explain it.
  5. A state insurance-regulatory or E&O (errors & omissions) matter is disclosed that is not ordinary-course (none identified this pass — see §11).

dossiers.ALB:
ALB — Albemarle Corporation

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 24–36 months. Named reservation: ALB is a single-commodity (lithium) price bet wrapped in a chemicals company; its own disclosed FY2026 sensitivity table shows adjusted EBITDA ranging 4.5x between a repeat of the 2025 price trough (~$0.95bn) and a return to the 2021–2025 average price (~$4.3bn). The balance sheet is now genuinely strong (net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈0.5x post-divestitures) and the recovery already under way is real and primary-source-verified, not merely a favorable comp — but position size should reflect that this is a commodity-price call, not a diversified-quality call.

2. Business in plain English

Albemarle mines and processes lithium (from Chile brine and Australian hard-rock spodumene, largely through the Talison joint venture) into lithium carbonate/hydroxide sold mostly under long-term contracts to battery and EV makers (Energy Storage segment, ~75% of FY26 sales), plus a smaller, steadier Specialties segment (bromine — flame retardants, oilfield fluids — and lithium specialties for pharma/electronics). It makes money on the spread between its (largely fixed, mining-cost-based) production cost and the market price of lithium, so profits are extremely levered to a single commodity price that has swung from ~$70+/kg (2022 peak) to ~$10/kg (2025 trough) and back to ~$20/kg (2026). Its moat is scale, low-cost brine/hard-rock resource ownership and long-term customer contracts (~40% of Energy Storage salts volume), not pricing power over the commodity itself.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores: composite 0.911765 (decile 10, quintile 5, live_rank 44/~2,300 — a top-2% quant score). Momentum (fam_M≈0.81) and Earnings momentum/SUE (fam_S≈0.61) are the strongest drivers — both real: the stock and earnings estimates are both recovering sharply off the 2025 trough (§4). Value (fam_V≈0.67) looks attractive (pct_bp 0.94, pct_ep 0.35) largely because book value is high relative to a still-recovering earnings base. Quality (fam_Q≈0.71) is respectable (pct_ocf_a 0.60, low leverage pct 0.90) — genuinely improved post Ketjen/Eurecat divestiture debt paydown. Durability judgement: the recovery itself is real (verified realized price $19.53/kg in Q2 2026 vs $12.17/kg a year ago, §4), but its sustainability is entirely a bet on where spot lithium settles over the next 1–3 years — a price the company itself declines to forecast (its own guidance is a three-scenario sensitivity table, not a point estimate, §5). The quant score cannot distinguish "durable" recovery from "cyclical bounce"; only the commodity-price view can.

4. Last two years of results (SEC EDGAR XBRL, CIK 0000915913; calendar fiscal year)

5. Guidance track record: a scenario table, not point guidance (state so explicitly)

Albemarle does not issue traditional next-quarter/next-year point guidance; every quarterly release instead publishes a full-year sensitivity table keyed to three observed lithium-price scenarios — this is disclosed explicitly and is, if anything, a more honest practice than false-precision point guidance:

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Balance sheet is the single best fact in this dossier: as of 30 Jun 2026, total debt $1.9bn, cash $1.6bn, liquidity ~$3.2bn (incl. $1.5bn undrawn revolver), net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈0.5x (company's own credit-agreement definition) — a dramatic improvement funded by the Ketjen/Eurecat divestitures and the earnings recovery. Q2 2026 operating cash flow $710m, free cash flow $638m (83% OCF conversion — company flags this was boosted by Talison JV dividend timing and non-recurring working-capital benefits, i.e. not fully repeatable at this conversion rate). Preferred stock: 7.25% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred (NYSE: ALB PR A) remains outstanding — a real, fixed dividend obligation and a source of common-share dilution on conversion (V1's diluted share count of 136.2m vs the raw 118.0m shares outstanding reflects this if-converted treatment). GAAP-vs-adjusted gap is significant in the recovery quarters (Q2 2026 adjusted EPS $3.75 vs GAAP $3.52 — an 6% adjustment, modest and disclosed) but was much wider in the loss quarters (large non-cash impairment charges drove GAAP losses far below adjusted losses in 2024–2025) — appropriately flagged, not glossed over.

7. Valuation snapshot — V1 says EXCESSIVE; I partially disagree with the input, not the caution

V1 (v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json): NTM P/E 9.65x, own-history percentile 7th (i.e. ALB has traded above today's multiple in ~93% of the last 152 months — nominally cheap), peer median 17.7x, but V1's reverse-DCF implies 33.4% revenue growth needed for 10 years to justify the price at a 10.53% WACC → verdict: excessive, base 3-yr annualised return −1.2%, bear −40.6%, bull +77.8%.

Where I think the specific input is wrong: V1's reverse DCF uses a TTM EBIT margin of 4.27% (ebit_margin_used in v1_valuation.json) as its forward base. That TTM window spans Q3 2025 through Q2 2026 and is still dragging in the Q3 2025 operating loss (−$217.0m) — it has not caught up to the current run rate. Primary-source correction: Q2 2026 alone had a GAAP operating margin of 452.9/1,743.3 = 26.0%; Q1 2026 was 233.5/1,428.7 = 16.3%. Holding a 4.27% margin fixed and asking for 33% revenue growth to reach the same target EV mechanically produces an extreme, near-impossible growth requirement — it is an artefact of the stale margin input, not evidence that the market is pricing in something irrational.

My own reconciliation, built from the company's own FY26 sensitivity table (§5) rather than a margin-fade DCF: applying peer-appropriate EV/EBITDA multiples (8x bear / 7x base / 9x bull) to the company's own $0.95bn / $2.5bn / $4.3bn EBITDA scenarios, net of ~$0.3bn net debt, on 136.2m diluted shares: bear ≈$54/share, base ≈$126/share, bull ≈$282/share — against the $109.73 close. This reads closer to FAIR than EXCESSIVE, and the implied growth in the current price looks roughly in line with the company's own already-realized ~$20/kg run rate, not a bet on a return to the $30/kg 2021–2025 average. valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent = false; both analyses agree on the direction and magnitude of the risk (a return to $10/kg trough pricing would still be a severe outcome) even though they disagree on the point estimate.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) lithium demand (EV + grid storage) structurally grows faster than new supply can be brought online, sustaining or improving on the $19.53/kg realized in Q2 2026; (2) balance sheet is now clean enough (0.5x net debt/EBITDA) to fund growth capex or return capital without re-leveraging; (3) portfolio simplification (Ketjen/ Eurecat exits) focuses management and capital entirely on the highest-return lithium/bromine franchises.

Bear: (1) lithium is a genuinely volatile, oversupplied-prone commodity (Chinese lepidolite/African supply can swing on marginal-cost economics) — a return to the ~$10/kg 2025 average would cut EBITDA ~65% from the Q2 2026 run rate; (2) ~40% of Energy Storage salts volume is on long-term contracts, meaning realized pricing can lag or lead spot in either direction, adding a layer of estimation risk beyond spot price alone; (3) the mandatory convertible preferred is a real, non-trivial claim on cash flow and a dilution overhang not fully reflected in headline EPS.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Realized Energy Storage price falls back below $15/kg LCE for two consecutive quarters (vs $19.53/kg in Q2 2026) — the clearest sign the recovery is reversing.
  2. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 1.5x (vs ≈0.5x at 30 Jun 2026) — would signal renewed balance-sheet stress.
  3. Two consecutive quarters of negative adjusted EBITDA in the Energy Storage segment.
  4. FY2026 total-corporate scenario table is cut below the "~$10/kg" case (i.e., management signals a worse floor than the 2025 trough) at any quarterly release.
  5. Any further material impairment (Item 2.06 8-K) outside the already-disclosed Ketjen/Eurecat divestitures.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-11-04/05 (Q3 2026). No pending M&A as acquirer/target after the Ketjen/Eurecat exits completed in Jan/Mar 2026. Mandatory convertible preferred (ALB PR A) dividend and eventual conversion terms are a recurring capital-structure item to track each quarter.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Material impairment, Item 2.06 8-K (filed 2025-10-27): tied to the Ketjen catalysts-business sale agreement — explains the outsized Q4 2025 GAAP net loss (−$414.2m) relative to the operating trend; disclosed and completed (sale closed 2026-03-02 for ~$547m), not an open/unresolved item.
  • Item 2.01 8-K (filed 2026-03-06): confirms Ketjen sale completion and the concurrent redemption of the 4.650% Senior Notes due 2027 — a deleveraging use of proceeds, not a red flag.
  • No going-concern language, no restatement, no auditor change identified in the reviewed filings.
  • Single-commodity concentration (lithium) is itself the dominant risk factor for this name — see §7/§9.

dossiers.ALGN:
Align Technology, Inc. (ALGN) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F23 | As of: 2026-09-25 close ($146.78) | Depth: Standard

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Named reservation: the stock is genuinely cheap on its own 14-year valuation history, but that trough partly reflects real, disclosed growth deceleration (FY26 guided revenue growth of just 3–4%, likely the slowest since IPO) and recurring GAAP one-off charges; size small pending confirmation that the FY27 margin-recovery commitment is met.

2. Business in plain English

Align makes Invisalign clear aligners (its core, ~82% of revenue) and iTero intraoral scanners plus exocad CAD/CAM software, selling to orthodontists, GP dentists and increasingly DSOs (dental service organizations) worldwide. It earns money per case shipped (aligners) and per scanner/software seat, and is the clear share leader in clear aligners globally, though it now competes with lower-cost aligner entrants and Straumann/others in scanners.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q07) called it "the standout price-vs-growth setup in this batch" on ">100% implied forward EPS growth" against a 12x NTM P/E. Verified: the ">100%" figure is a base-year artifact, not real operating momentum — Q2'25 EPS ($1.72) vs Q2'26 EPS ($1.51) is actually down 12% YoY, and Q3'25 EPS ($0.78) was the weakest print in two years. The apparent explosive forward growth comes from comparing to a temporarily depressed base (Q3'25/Q4'25 carried heavy restructuring, impairment and accelerated-depreciation charges). The 12x NTM P/E being at the ~1st percentile of ALGN's own 14-year history is real and confirmed (V1), but it is priced that way for a disclosed reason (below), not an oversight.

4. Last 8 quarters (SEC 10-Q/10-K + XBRL; GAAP unless marked)

3Q24 977.9 — 69.7% 16.6% $1.55

3Q25/4Q25's margin compression was driven by disclosed one-offs: a manufacturing-facility impairment/ assets-held-for-sale charge, accelerated depreciation on disposed manufacturing assets, and a restructuring program (headcount reduction) initiated in 4Q24 and again 3Q25 (earnings-release GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation notes 1–5). Non-GAAP gross/operating margins were materially steadier throughout (non-GAAP op margin 22.9% in 2Q26 vs 21.3% in 2Q25).

5. Guidance track record (last 4 releases, quoted verbatim from each release)

  • 3Q25 release (Oct 2025) → guided Q4'25 revenue "$1,025M to $1,045M, up sequentially"; actual $1,047.6M — beat the high end. FY2025 revenue guided "flat to slightly up from 2024"; actual FY25 $4,034.96M vs FY24 $3,999.01M = +0.9%, in line.
  • 4Q25/FY25 release (Feb 2026) → guided Q1'26 revenue "$1,010M to $1,030M, up 3–5% YoY"; actual $1,040.1M — beat the high end. Guided Q1'26 GAAP op margin "12.4%–12.8%"; actual 13.6% — beat. Guided FY2026 GAAP operating margin "slightly below 18.0%" (+~400bps YoY) and non-GAAP "~23.7%."
  • 1Q26 release (Apr 2026) → guided Q2'26 revenue "$1,040M to $1,060M, up 3–5%"; actual $1,056.2M, within range. Reaffirmed the FY26 GAAP op-margin guide of "slightly below 18.0%."
  • 2Q26 release (Jul 2026) → guided Q3'26 revenue "$1,000M to $1,020M" (a sequential decline, guided seasonality) and cut FY2026 GAAP operating-margin guidance to "15.1%–15.6%" — roughly 250–290bps below the "slightly below 18.0%" guided just one quarter earlier — because of newly disclosed one-time charges: a $37.5M UK VAT contingent liability (below), ~$30.6M of Q1'26 legal settlements, and further restructuring/ accelerated depreciation, now totaling an expected $90–110M for FY26. Non-GAAP FY26 operating-margin guidance was left unchanged at ~23.7%. This is the single most important adverse fact in this dossier: revenue guidance has not moved (3–4% growth reaffirmed all year and beaten on the top line every quarter), but the GAAP profitability guide was cut materially inside two quarters — an increase in one-off cash costs, not a demand problem. Treat any "GAAP margin beat/miss" narrative with that context.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • UK VAT dispute: clear aligners were ruled VAT-exempt by the UK First-tier Tribunal (2025); ALGN stopped charging UK VAT from Aug 2025. On 2026-07-07 the Upper Tribunal overturned that ruling. ALGN recorded a $37.5M estimated liability (inclusive of interest) in Q2'26 and will charge 20% VAT on UK invoices from 2026-09-07; it intends to appeal, with the outcome "subject to uncertainty" (its own words).
  • Tariffs: subject to Section 122 (Trade Act of 1974) tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled the prior IEEPA tariffs unlawful (2026-02-20); the Section 122 tariffs are themselves under appeal at the Court of International Trade. Company states it does not expect a material impact currently — a live, disclosed, unresolved policy risk rather than a settled cost.
  • Balance sheet: no debt on the balance sheet; cash $1,102.6M (2Q26) vs $1,094.9M (FY25 year-end); total liabilities are dominated by deferred revenue ($1,187.2M) and accrued liabilities, not borrowings — a genuinely strong, low-risk balance sheet.
  • Capital return: $1.0bn buyback program (announced Apr 2025); $733.3M remaining as of 2026-06-30; guided to repurchase $400–500M in 2026. Diluted share count down from 72.59M (2Q25) to 71.52M (2Q26), -1.5%.
  • FCF/SBC: H1'26 operating cash flow $343.8M vs $181.3M H1'25 (+90%); FY26 capex guided $125–150M. SBC ~4.3% of revenue (2Q26), stable.

7. Valuation — reconciled with V1

V1 (systematic) calls ALGN "attractive" (score 0.48), citing NTM P/E of 12.0x at the 1.2th percentile of its own 171-month (14-year) history. I agree the multiple is genuinely at a generational low for this name — that fact is confirmed and I do not dispute it. However, V1's base-case reverse DCF return of +59.65%/yr (3yr) is not credible and I overturn it: it requires revenue growth of 15.6%/yr (4x the company's own guided 3–4% for FY26) and an exit multiple of 39.4x (up from today's 12.0x) simultaneously. V1's own sanity check flags this: the base-case 3-year price target ($597) exceeds even the Street's current 12-month high target ($240, mean $208.60) by 2.5x. I attribute this to V1's reverse-DCF using a TTM EBIT margin (13.2%) that is itself depressed by the 3Q25/4Q25 one-offs (§4) — a low earnings base plus an 11.2% WACC forces the model to assume unrealistic growth just to justify today's EV, which is not the same as the market actually pricing that growth in. My own base case: revenue growth 4–6%/yr (current guide plus modest recovery as one-offs roll off and management's own "at least ~100bps" FY27 margin-improvement commitment is met), GAAP operating margin recovering toward 16–17% by FY27, and the NTM P/E re-rating partially — to 15–17x, not V1's 39x — as growth stabilizes. valuation_view_vs_v1: dossier_view = fair (in_line with my base case), consistent = false (I reject V1's base-case return and exit multiple, not its multiple-percentile finding).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Clear Aligner volume +7.4% YoY in 2Q26 on double-digit international/DSO growth, with revenue beating guidance every quarter this year; (2) net-cash balance sheet funds continued buybacks (-1.5% share count YoY) regardless of near-term margin noise; (3) management has explicitly committed to further ~100bps non-GAAP margin improvement in FY27 on top of FY26's, a specific, checkable promise. Bear: (1) FY26 revenue-growth guidance (3–4%) is the softest in the company's history as a public company, and Systems & Services revenue is guided down 6–8% YoY on a structural mix shift to lower-price/ leased scanners; (2) GAAP operating-margin guidance was already cut once this year (§5) and the UK VAT appeal and Section 122 tariff litigation are both unresolved, open-ended cost risks; (3) the stock's beta (~1.5–1.7) means any confirmation that growth deceleration is structural (not cyclical) could re-rate the multiple down further even from today's 14-year low.

9. Kill criteria

  1. Quarterly Clear Aligner volume growth turns negative YoY.
  2. FY2026 GAAP operating-margin guidance is cut again below the current 15.1%–15.6% range (excluding charges already disclosed as of this dossier).
  3. Full-year revenue growth guidance is cut below the current 3%–4% range.
  4. Net cash (cash − debt) falls below $500M.
  5. Cumulative UK VAT / Section 122 tariff cash outflows exceed $150M beyond the $37.5M already reserved.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-10-28/29 (Q3'26, estimated from the identical prior-year filing date; not yet announced). UK VAT appeal timeline not yet set. Section 122 tariff litigation (Court of International Trade) outcome/timeline not yet set. FY2027 formal guidance expected alongside Q4'26 results (company stated its "strategic and operating model review" is still underway as of the 2Q26 release).

11. Red-flag scan

No going-concern language, material weakness or restatement found in the reviewed 10-Q/10-K/8-Ks. Open items: UK VAT liability/appeal and Section 122 tariff litigation (both above, both genuinely unresolved); two restructuring programs in twelve months (4Q24 and 3Q25) — a real, if modest, signal of cost-structure strain, not a governance red flag. No auditor change noted.

The Allstate Corporation (NYSE: ALL) — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

Prepared by: f1 (fundamental diligence analyst) | Data cutoff: 2026-09-25 close | Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 (10-Q filed 2026-08-05, period ended 2026-06-30); checked for events to 2026-09-25. Next scheduled report: Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04. Basis: consolidated GAAP financial statements throughout (Allstate reports on a single consolidated basis; adjusted net income is the company's own non-GAAP measure, labeled as such wherever used).

Data quality note: all financial figures below are sourced to SEC EDGAR primary filings (10-Q/10-K, 8-K earnings-release exhibits) or SEC XBRL company facts (a machine-readable copy of the same filings), each cited by number in §12; quant/peer context is sourced to the v4 internal lead_prelim_rank.csv and d4_live_snapshot.parquet, labeled as such. Figures marked ¹ are derived (FY minus 9-month YTD, both officially reported) rather than directly reported. The Q4/FY2025 earnings-release exhibit could not be fetched this session (persistent SEC EDGAR 503 errors); FY2024/2025 annuals instead use SEC XBRL company facts, a fully primary but less narrative source — see note at the end of §12. No figure is estimated, interpolated, or recalled from training-data memory. This dossier is research output for internal investment-process use, not personalised investment advice; it is not a recommendation to buy or sell any security, and the reader is responsible for their own decisions.

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 6–18 months

Real, structural personal-lines repair (auto/home) layered on top of an even larger cyclical/base-effect earnings surge; current profitability (44% trailing adjusted ROE) is not a run-rate. Half-weight sizing reflects a genuine business but a high near-term probability that reported earnings decelerate sharply, which the market (7.65x NTM P/E) and the Street (FY2027 consensus EPS −21% vs FY2026) already anticipate.

2. Business in plain English

Allstate is a personal-lines-focused P&C insurer (the "You're in Good Hands" brand) selling primarily auto and homeowners insurance to individuals through captive/exclusive agents, independent agents, and direct channels, plus non-standard auto via its National General subsidiary (acquired 2021). It also runs smaller Protection Plans (extended warranties/appliance protection) and Health & Benefits segments. It earns money through underwriting profit and investment income on reserves, and — unusually for a "carrier" — a meaningful fee-based Protection Services business layered on top.

3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

b1-family prelim scores (source: internal lead_prelim_rank.csv): Q 0.752, V 0.586, M 0.940 (12-1m return +22.4%), composite 0.874. This is the starkest case in the batch of a quant score built substantially on a cyclical peak. Per d4_live_snapshot.parquet, trailing GAAP ROE (Yahoo-sourced field) is 46.1%; per the Q2-26 earnings release (§12 #1), the company's own "adjusted net income ROE (ttm)" is 44.2%, up from 28.6% a year ago (+15.6 pts). No P&C insurer sustains a 44% ROE through a cycle — the sector playbook's own "excellent and rare" bar is 15%+. The d4 quant snapshot explicitly flags this: ntm_flags = "fy1_below_fy0_by_15pct+", ntm_quality = "caution" — FY2027 consensus EPS ($27.74) is 21.3% below FY2026 consensus ($35.26), the largest forward-EPS air-pocket of the three names reviewed (d4_live_snapshot.parquet). Momentum (M=0.940) and the Value score (cheap on trailing/NTM earnings, 7.65x P/E per d4) are two sides of the same coin: the market is pricing today's earnings as unrepresentative. Durable part: per the Q2-26 release (§12 #1), auto insurance policies-in-force are growing (+2.8% YoY) with new business up 8.8%, i.e. Allstate is not just harvesting price increases while losing share — the repricing appears to be holding demand, a real structural signal. Not durable: the magnitude of current combined ratios and ROE.

Per the same Q2-26 release (source #1): Auto recorded combined ratio 83.3% (Q2-26) vs 86.0% (Q2-25), underlying flat at 87.6%/87.8%. Conclusion: as with TRV, the great majority of the YoY "recorded" combined-ratio improvement is a catastrophe base effect and reserve releases, not underlying repricing — underlying auto is flat and underlying homeowners is getting worse.

5. Guidance track record

Allstate, like TRV, gives no formal quantitative EPS/margin guidance in earnings releases (no "outlook"/"guidance"/numeric target found across the releases reviewed). Not applicable; see §3/§8 for forward-looking read.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF/OCF: FY2025 OCF $10.110B, capex $228M, FCF≈$9.882B vs GAAP NI $10.282B (≈0.96x) — reasonable, though (per sector playbook) OCF is partly a float-growth artefact, not a pure quality signal.
  • SBC: $123M FY2025 = 0.18% of revenue — immaterial.
  • Debt: $7.492B (Q2-26) vs $7.490B (FY25) — stable, and consistent with both Yahoo ($7.497B) and the b1 prelim figure ($7.742B); no material data conflict here (unlike TRV/GL — see their dossiers).
  • Buybacks: paused during the 2022-23 capital rebuild ($335M FY23, just $2M FY24) then resumed hard: $1.233B FY25, $1.0B in Q2-26 alone ("share repurchases were increased to $1.0 billion for the quarter"). This buyback reactivation timeline is itself corroborating evidence of the cycle: capital was scarce in 2022-23 (the personal-auto crisis years) and abundant now.
  • Book value: $123.38/share, +49.7% YoY — an extraordinary one-year jump, driven by the earnings surge plus buybacks; not a steady-state compounding rate.
  • Policies in force: total 215.9M (+3.8%); auto 25.95M (+2.8%, new business +8.8%); homeowners 7.82M (+2.9%, new business +16.4%) — growing, not just repricing a shrinking book.

7. Valuation snapshot

(scripts/ratios.py/scripts/valuation.py were deliberately not run: their outputs — EV/EBITDA, FCF-based DCF, generic ROCE/current-ratio — are the specific metrics the insurance sector playbook states are undefined or misleading for underwriters. The P/B-anchored-to-ROE and peer-comparison approach below is the playbook's mandated substitute.)

NTM P/E (d4) 7.65x — the cheapest of the three names on this metric, and the reason is the FY2027 consensus air-pocket, not a re-rating opportunity per se. P/B 1.82x. Peer set (same live snapshot): PGR 3.48x P/B / 34.9% ROE (PGR's own pe_ntm reads as a data anomaly — 0.27x — excluded as unusable, likely a denominator/split artefact); CB 1.71x/14.8%/11.6x; HIG 1.75x/22.1%/9.2x; CINF 1.50x/21.5%/18.3x. Read: ALL trades at a lower P/B than PGR despite a higher reported ROE — the market has already substantially discounted ALL's ROE as unsustainable. Reverse-DCF sense: at 1.8x book, the price requires normalized ROE of roughly only 12-15% to be justified (using the sector playbook's P/B≈(ROE-g)/(COE-g) framework) — i.e. even a large mean-reversion from 44% is largely priced in already. The open question is whether normalized ROE lands at "high teens" (still attractive, supports upside) or reverts closer to the mid-single-digits/negative territory seen in the 2022 personal-auto crisis (FY2022 net income was −$1.289B, per XBRL) if the pricing cycle turns harder than expected.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Policies-in-force and new business are both growing at mid-to-high single/double digits — the repricing is holding volume, unlike a pure harvest-and-shrink strategy. (2) Even after heavy mean-reversion, current valuation (7.65x NTM P/E, 1.82x P/B) leaves room for a "normal-good" outcome (mid-teens ROE) to still look cheap. (3) Capital position fully rebuilt from the 2022 crisis with buybacks now running at $1B/quarter. Bear: (1) 44% ROE and the FY2027 consensus EPS cut of 21% are not compatible with "durable" — a two-year-old bull case (auto repair) has now been almost entirely realized and priced. (2) Underlying homeowners combined ratio is already deteriorating (61.5%, +2.9 pts YoY) even before any broader loss-cost reacceleration — an early crack in the "structural improvement" story. (3) The auto insurance pricing cycle is adversarial: Allstate's own price increases invite competitor re-entry (Progressive, GEICO, State Farm) exactly when Allstate's margins look best, which is the mechanism by which 2022-style compression historically returns.

9. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis is invalidated if any of the following are observed (source: company 10-Q/8-K disclosures each quarter)

  1. Property-Liability recorded combined ratio > 100% for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Auto or homeowners policies-in-force growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (share loss as competitors reprice back down).
  3. Adjusted net income ROE (ttm) stays above ~35% for another two quarters without a corresponding upward revision to FY2027 consensus (would mean the deceleration is being denied, not resolved) — OR falls below ~15% (confirms hard mean reversion, re-underwrite thesis).
  4. Net favorable reserve development flips negative in auto/casualty for two consecutive quarters.
  5. Homeowners underlying combined ratio deteriorates a further ~5 pts from 61.5%.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-11-04 (Q3 2026 — peak-of-hurricane-season print). No investor day/index event identified in this pass.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor change (no Item 4.01 8-K found), no restatement, no going-concern/material-weakness language, no SEC/DOJ investigation disclosed. "No material changes" to FY2025 10-K risk factors per the Q2-26 10-Q. One named routine suit (Holland Hewitt v. Allstate Life, E.D. Cal.) noted in passing in the 10-Q's litigation note — appears to be ordinary-course, not separately escalated. 40 Form 4 filings between 2026-02-23 and 2026-09-08 (SEC EDGAR) — direction not individually tabulated in this pass; no 13D/G activist stake surfaced.
