7. Valuation snapshot and reverse-DCF sense

Price 2026-09-25 close: $263.27. NTM P/E 20.2x (fy1 P/E 19.8x), EV/EBITDA (trailing) ≈ 14.7x ($117.0bn EV / $7.95bn trailing EBITDA — this EBITDA figure understates the run-rate because it spans the merger date and doesn't yet reflect a full clean year of Calpine). Consensus NTM EPS growth ≈ +9.7%. No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for CEG (not in v1_valuation_table.csv), so there is nothing to reconcile against; this section is the analyst's own reverse-DCF read only.

Using a simple Gordon-growth solve on the NTM P/E (P = EPS_ntm×(1+g)/(Ke−g)), with Ke via CAPM (rf 4.16%, ERP 5.0%, beta 1.117 → Ke≈9.75%): the price implies a perpetual growth rate of ≈4.6%. That is a meaningfully lower bar than the ≈9–10% growth consensus expects over the next year, and lower than the double-digit multi-year ramp implied by the Microsoft/Meta contracted volumes and the Crane restart (targeted 2027, DOE-backed $1bn loan guarantee, NRC fuel-license approval received Aug 2026, FERC capacity-interconnection-rights transfer approved). A pure EV/EBITDA sector read is more appropriate for a merchant/contracted generator than a P/E Gordon-growth model (per the utilities-power playbook, contracted generation should trade 9–12x EV/EBITDA and merchant 4–7x on mid-cycle spreads); CEG's ~14.7x trailing multiple is rich by that yardstick even before adjusting for a cleaner forward EBITDA run-rate, which this pass could not independently rebuild from public disclosures in the time available (disclosed limitation — no fleet-level PPA tenor/spread data was sourced).

Bear case (own-history/evidence-based): integration execution risk (a genuinely large, complex M&A with a hard regulatory divestiture deadline already passed for the definitive-agreement stage but not for closing); nuclear PTC volatility already visible in two of the last five quarters as an earnings headwind; a re-rating back toward historical merchant-generator multiples (6–9x EV/EBITDA) if data-center demand growth disappoints or gas/power spreads compress → 3yr annualised return ≈ −4%. Base case: Calpine integrates on plan, the three DOJ divestitures close by year-end 2026 for combined proceeds of ≈$5.9bn (used to delever), Crane restarts on schedule in 2027, guidance is met at the raised $11.50–$12.50 range and grows roughly with the ~9–10% consensus for 2–3 years before decelerating toward mid-single digits as contracted volumes mature → 3yr annualised return ≈ +7%. Bull case: additional hyperscaler PPAs (following Microsoft/Meta/CyrusOne) re-rate the whole nuclear fleet as bond-like contracted cash flow, Crane and license-renewal capacity (two NY units filed for renewal in 2026) all clear regulatory hurdles ahead of schedule → 3yr annualised return ≈ +18%.

valuation_view_vs_v1: no V1 row exists; dossier_view = full (price already assumes execution goes right; growth priced in via the Gordon-growth read is below consensus near-term growth but the EV/EBITDA read is rich versus sector bands) — net view: fair-to-full, not cheap, which under the program's quality-growth-lane rule (growth priced in must be ≤ the analyst's base case) argues for WATCH rather than INCLUDE until the divestitures close and one clean post-merger quarter is reported.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Contracted, 20-year, investment-grade-counterparty PPAs (Microsoft/Crane, Meta/Clinton, CyrusOne) lock in premium pricing for decades, de-risking a large and growing share of nuclear output just as AI/data-center demand for firm carbon-free power accelerates. 2. Calpine adds a large, flexible, dispatchable gas/geothermal/storage fleet and the nation's largest competitive retail electric supply platform (~62 TWh/yr), diversifying away from pure nuclear-merchant exposure and creating commercial cross-sell. 3. A demonstrated four-year record of beating the midpoint of its own guidance, now backed by a raised FY2026 range after only two quarters on the combined basis.

Bear (3 points): 1. Leverage roughly tripled in gross terms with the Calpine deal; the DOJ-mandated divestitures (worth an estimated ~$5.9bn combined) have not yet closed, so both the deleveraging plan and the "clean" post-divestiture earnings base are still forecasts, not facts. 2. GAAP earnings are genuinely volatile quarter to quarter (Q1 2026 GAAP EPS $4.49 vs Q2 2026 GAAP EPS $1.42) on integration and PTC items; investors are relying heavily on the company's own adjusted "Operating Earnings" framing. 3. At ~20x NTM P/E and ~14.7x trailing EV/EBITDA, the stock is not obviously cheap for a business still mid-integration with unresolved regulatory divestiture risk.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable) -- what would invalidate this thesis

  1. Any one of the three DOJ-mandated divestitures (LS Power PJM $5.0bn deal, LS Power ERCOT/Brazos Valley $860m deal, Gregory stake) fails to close by the extended internal target ("end of this year," i.e. by 2026-12-31) or is renegotiated down in price.
  2. FY2026 Adjusted Operating EPS comes in below the low end of the raised $11.50–$12.50 guidance range at year-end.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA (on a clean, full-year-Calpine basis, once reportable) exceeds 4.0x with no credible deleveraging path.
  4. Crane Clean Energy Center restart slips past 2027 or the NRC/FERC approvals already obtained are challenged/reversed.
  5. Two consecutive quarters of GAAP-to-adjusted reconciling items exceeding 30% of adjusted operating earnings, signalling the "adjusted" framing is masking a structurally worse GAAP business.

1. Verdict

REJECT (for a diversified $50–100k moderate-risk account at today's price; revisit as WATCH on a pullback toward mid-cycle valuation, roughly $85–95/share, or on independent-source confirmation that the Iran-related nitrogen supply loss is becoming structural rather than a reversible war disruption). Thesis horizon if revisited: 12–36 months.

One-sentence reason: Every marker in the deep-cyclical "peak" checklist is flashing simultaneously — Q2 2026 operating margin (50.5%) is above the prior all-time-high quarter (2022), the quant model's Value/Momentum scores are being driven by a trailing-earnings base the Street is already marking down in real time, and management itself attributes the spike to a named, live, geopolitical supply shock (the Iran conflict) that outside forecasters expect to fade in 2027 — the textbook low-P/E-at-peak trap.

2. Business in plain English

CF Industries is the largest nitrogen fertilizer producer in North America, making ammonia, granular urea, UAN (urea-ammonium-nitrate solution) and ammonium nitrate at plants in the US, Canada and the UK, plus a 50%-owned JV in Trinidad. Customers are agricultural cooperatives, independent fertilizer distributors, commodity traders and industrial buyers (explosives, diesel exhaust fluid, emissions-control reagents). CF makes money on the spread between global nitrogen product prices (set by worldwide supply/demand, since nitrogen is a globally traded commodity) and its own input cost, which is overwhelmingly North American natural gas (~34% of FY2025 production cost per the 10-K) — historically cheaper than the gas Europe and much of Asia pay, which is CF's structural cost-curve advantage. Its competitive position is a low-cost, first-quartile North American producer with scale, deep-water logistics, and a growing low-carbon-ammonia option (Blue Point JV, Donaldsonville CCS).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Preliminary QVM percentiles (sector-neutral within Materials, lead_prelim_rank.csv): Q = 0.913 (91st pctile), V = 0.922 (92nd pctile), M = 0.788 (79th pctile), preliminary composite = 0.875 (S/earnings-momentum family not yet live). ROE(TTM, pipeline) 28.3%; independently recomputed via ratios.py on FY2025 GAAP: ROE 34.7%, ROIC 29.3%, EBIT margin 32.5% — all genuinely high in absolute terms, which is exactly the problem: both Q and V are largely a function of the trailing-earnings base, and that base is elevated, not typical. V in particular (earnings yield 9.4%, FCF yield 11.0%, EBIT/EV 15.3%) mechanically looks cheap only because the denominator (trailing/NTM earnings) is a cyclical peak. This is not a durable Quality signal — it is a cyclical-margin artefact layered on top of a genuinely well-run, low-cost, low-leverage balance sheet. Momentum (79th pctile) is real (12-1m price return has been strong) but is itself largely a re-rating on the same peak earnings. Strip out the cycle and CF's underlying business quality is good-but-not-exceptional for the sector (10-yr median EBIT margin ~24%, see §7), which is why the Q score should be discounted, not the headline used at face value.

Mid-cycle EV/EBITDA (EBITDA ≈ EBIT + ~$900M normalized D&A = $2.6B) is 7.1x, inside the 5–8x heavy-industry anchor, i.e. roughly fair-to-full, not cheap. (A plain perpetuity-style DCF on the same mid-cycle FCF at an 8.5% WACC instead implies ~15–48% upside — flagged explicitly as a methodological tension: a DCF that discounts a "mid-cycle" cash flow to perpetuity implicitly assumes that estimate is precise and durable forever, which is exactly the assumption a deep-cyclical framework exists to distrust; the multiple-based scenario table is weighted more heavily here.) Closest peers to sanity-check: Nutrien (NTR, 2026 EPS growth guided ~26.5% per Zacks vs. CF's ~68–84% depending on source — CF is the most extreme swing of the group), Yara International (YAR/YARIY, ~61% 2026 growth), LSB Industries (smaller, more leveraged, similar spread economics) — not independently re-underwritten in this pass; noted as the natural next step before sizing.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3): 1. Live, unresolved supply shock could persist or worsen. The Iran conflict has curtailed an estimated 50–60% of Middle East ammonia/urea capacity at points in 2026 and shut the Strait of Hormuz to LNG/ammonia exports; if this drags on or escalates, 2027 nitrogen prices could stay elevated well past the current Street expectation of normalization. 2. Balance sheet and capital return are genuinely best-in-class. Net debt/mid-cycle-EBITDA ~0.5x, no near-term maturities, $750M undrawn revolver, buybacks sustained through the 2024 trough, dividend just raised 20% — this is not a leveraged cyclical that can be forced into a fire sale in the next downturn. 3. Structural, non-cyclical optionality is not yet in the price. Blue Point (1.5M tons nameplate, CF's 40% share, production 2029) and Donaldsonville CCS (45Q credits already flowing, ~$19–24M/quarter and rising) add a genuinely durable, contracted/subsidized earnings stream on top of the cyclical core, which the mid-cycle valuation above does not credit at all.

Bear (3): 1. The central driver of today's margin is explicitly named by management as a war-related supply disruption, not a structural change — CEO Chris Bohn: "the conflict with Iran has further constrained global nitrogen supply." Outside forecasters (World Bank, CSIS, IFPRI, farmdoc) already expect prices to ease in 2027 as exports recover and new supply (including CF's own Blue Point and competitors') comes online — which is precisely what the FY2027 consensus EPS (-27% vs FY2026, and itself likely still too high) is starting to price. 2. The Street is cutting numbers in real time, not raising them, for CF specifically — FY2026 consensus EPS fell from $17.61 (90 days ago) to $15.10 (now), with 6 downward vs. 0 upward revisions in the last 30 days — the opposite pattern to MPC's re-rating, and a sign the peak may already be behind the stock even before a formal top-line reversal shows up. 3. A major safety incident (Yazoo City ammonia release/explosion, 2025-11-05) triggered a shelter-in-place order for the entire town, a still-unresolved ~$48M+ of impairments, active plaintiff-side litigation solicitation, and a guidance slip on the restart timeline (Q4 2026 → H1 2027 as of the Aug-2026 release) — a real operational and reputational tail risk layered on top of the cyclical one.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (thesis-invalidation triggers)

Any of the following would invalidate the "this is a mid-cycle-normalisation story" thesis and should trigger an active re-underwrite (for REJECT, these are also the conditions that would flip the verdict toward INCLUDE on a future pass):

  1. De-escalation of the Iran conflict / Strait of Hormuz reopening to normal flow — watch for a >25% pullback in benchmark urea/UAN prices (NOLA/Gulf) within two quarters of any ceasefire or sanctions relief; this is the single biggest swing factor.
  2. Two consecutive quarters of GAAP operating margin below 30% (i.e. reverting toward the 24% median) would confirm the cycle has turned — exit or re-underwrite at that point rather than before.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA > 2.5x (mid-cycle-adjusted) would be a genuine balance-sheet concern; currently nowhere close (0.4–0.5x), but watch if Blue Point capital calls or a large debt-financed buyback push this materially.
  4. Yazoo City restart slips again past H1 2027, or the incident investigation (OSHA/state) results in a materially larger fine/settlement or a permanent capacity reduction at the site.
  5. Global nitrogen capacity additions (Blue Point, Dangote, others) come online faster than 1.5%/yr demand growth absorbs, per the company's own 10-K framing of the long-run supply/demand balance — a leading indicator of the next down-cycle, visible years before the P&L.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: ~2026-11-04 (Q3 2026, aggregator estimate — not yet confirmed via an 8-K calendar notice; verify closer to the date).
  • Any ceasefire, sanctions, or Strait-of-Hormuz news flow on Iran — the single highest-frequency catalyst for this name right now.
  • Blue Point civil construction start (permits received July 2026; construction was slated to begin August 2026) — watch for an on-schedule confirmation or slippage in the Q3 release.
  • Yazoo City rebuild progress updates (targeted H1 2027 restart).
  • Officer transition: VP/Corporate Controller & Chief Accounting Officer Richard A. Hoker announced retirement (8-K, 2026-09-03), effective 2027-03-03 — routine (retirement, long lead time, no stated dispute), but worth a name-check against any future accounting-related 8-K.
  • No lock-up or index-event triggers identified in this pass.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Safety/operational: Yazoo City ammonia release/explosion, 2025-11-05 — town-wide evacuation/shelter-in-place ordered, no injuries reported, site idled; cumulative impairments to date ≈ $48M (AN-asset-group, Q4'25 $25M + Q2'26 $23M) plus a separate, unrelated $51M Donaldsonville electrolyzer impairment (management concluded the project would not earn an acceptable return, pivoted to CCS instead). Plaintiffs'-bar activity (multiple law-firm blog posts soliciting Yazoo County claimants) indicates likely toxic-tort litigation exposure not yet reflected in a specific reserve as of the last filing reviewed.
  • Auditor/controls: No auditor change, no material weakness, no going-concern language identified in the FY2025 10-K excerpt reviewed; auditor name/tenure and full CAM list were not independently extracted in this pass (source access limitation, not a finding) — verify directly in the 10-K Item 8/9A before final sizing.

PLNL (Trinidad, 50%-owned) faces an ongoing natural-gas-supply contingency — the gas-supply contract with NGC was renewed only through January 2027; non-renewal risk could trigger an impairment of the $36M carrying investment (small in size, but a recurring pattern worth tracking).

CINF — Cincinnati Financial Corporation — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 12–24 months. Genuinely attractive valuation (cheapest of the three names on both peer and own-history basis) and a strong 2025 underwriting-improvement trend, but the most recent quarter (Q2 2026) shows real deterioration — a 100.8% consolidated combined ratio (an underwriting loss), driven by Commercial Lines at 104.1% and Ohio storm losses "nearly four times" the 5-year Q2 average — and current-accident-year ex-catastrophe losses are also rising YoY (85.1%→88.1%), so this is not purely a weather blip. Sell-side FY1/FY0 EPS revisions skew negative (6 down/1 up; 8 down/0 up). Cheap for a reason that needs one more quarter to resolve.

2. Business in plain English

Cincinnati Financial is a super-regional property & casualty insurer selling commercial lines, personal lines, and excess & surplus (E&S) lines almost exclusively through a network of independent agencies (under 3,000 agency relationships, expanding), plus a small life-insurance subsidiary. Its defining feature versus peers is an unusually large equity securities portfolio held for total return (~$13.2bn, ~40% of invested assets) rather than the bond-heavy mix typical of insurers — this makes GAAP net income swing with the stock market, which is why the company (and this dossier, per program instructions) reports on non-GAAP operating income, which strips out realized/unrealized investment gains, as the truer read of underwriting performance.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 composite 0.875 (decile 9), but live_rank 62 and live_top30 = False despite the decile-9 score — an internal inconsistency versus HIG (decile 10, rank 20) and MTB (decile 10, rank 35) that this dossier cannot explain from the data provided (flagged as a data conflict below, not silently accepted). Quant strengths: pct_roe 83rd pctile, pct_ocf_a 93rd, pct_sue 90th (strong earnings-surprise history: beats 7 of last 8 quarters, avg surprise +59% — inflated by the investment-gain volatility in GAAP EPS discussed below, so partly artefact: the model may be rewarding GAAP earnings surprises that are really equity-market beta, not underwriting skill). Momentum family in the CSV shows CINF was NOT among the ≤2-insurers cap in the old v3 CIO rule (v3 held AIZ+HIG as its two insurers, not CINF) — a genuinely new addition versus v3, not a re-underwrite.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP net income/EPS; non-GAAP operating income/EPS labeled; combined ratio = consolidated P&C)

Use operating income/EPS and the combined ratio as the decision-relevant series — GAAP EPS here is materially an equity-market read-through, not an underwriting one.

5. Guidance track record

CINF issues no quarterly or annual quantitative EPS/revenue guidance. The one standing (not release-by-release) figure is a long-term combined-ratio target range of 92–98%, reaffirmed in the Q3 2025 release ("within striking distance of our target long-term annual average range of 92% to 98%") — this is a multi-year aspiration, not guidance that gets raised/maintained/cut quarter to quarter, and it has not been revised across the four releases reviewed. Stated per instructions: no numerical forward guidance to assess raise/cut against.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Investment portfolio is the swing factor: total investments $33.15bn (Jun-26), of which equity securities $13.19bn (39.8%) carrying $8.9bn of pre-tax unrealized gains — a large, undiversified-by-asset-class embedded gain that flows through GAAP income whenever realized or marked, and directly through book value per share (+$7.09/share from equity marks alone in Q2'26).
  • Reserve development is small and favorable but shrinking: consolidated PYD favorable $42M/1.7pts (Q2'26) vs. $63M/2.6pts (Q2'25); FY2025 favorable $196M/2.0pts vs. a Personal-Lines unfavorable $20M in Q4'25 alone — worth watching given Personal Lines' combined ratio also deteriorated YoY in Q4'25 (103.6% FY2025 vs 97.5% FY2024).
  • Book value per share $108.64 (Jun-26) vs. $102.35 (Dec-25), +6%, almost entirely investment-gain-driven (value-creation-ratio breakdown: FY2025 18.8% total = 14.9% book-value growth + 3.9% dividends). Dividend raised to $0.94/share (from $0.87, +8%) — company is a long-tenured consecutive dividend-increaser (exact streak length not independently verified in sources reviewed, so not asserted as a specific number here). Share buybacks were not disclosed/quantified in three of the four releases reviewed (Q1'26, Q3'25, Q4'25 releases state "not stated" for repurchase volume) — an information gap, not a finding of no buyback activity; diluted share count did fall slightly Q2'25→Q2'26 (157.8M→155.7M), implying some repurchase activity nets against option/incentive issuance.
  • No debt/leverage or capital-adequacy figures were surfaced in the press-release extracts reviewed (P&C-appropriate metrics — statutory surplus, RBC — sit in the 10-K/statutory filings, not pulled given the time budget). Disclosed gap, not a red flag.

7. Valuation snapshot (v1 pipeline, 2026-09-25 close)

P/B 1.52x vs. peer median 1.79x — 43rd percentile of CINF's own history: genuinely cheap on both axes, the most attractive of the three names on valuation alone. Justified-P/B implies a sustainable 10.8% ROE, vs. actual TTM (GAAP) ROE 20.0% — but TTM GAAP ROE is itself equity-market-inflated per §6, so the "cheapness" partly reflects the market correctly discounting non-recurring investment gains, not necessarily mispricing. V1 base-case 3-year annualized return +11.5% (bear +2.9%, bull +20.7%) — note bear case here is still positive, unusual among the three names, because book value has a large cushion of unrealized gains. V1 verdict: "attractive."

8. Bull case

  1. Cheapest of the three on both peer-relative and own-history P/B, with a bear-case scenario that still shows a positive 3-year return per V1 — a real valuation cushion.
  2. 2025 underwriting trend (Q1'25 113.3% combined → Q3'25 88.2% → Q4'25 85.2%) shows the franchise can produce excellent combined ratios when catastrophe experience is benign, and agency-count growth (355 new appointments in 2025, 220 more in 1H26, "still under 3,000... a lot of runway") is a genuine, quantified distribution-expansion story.
  3. Large embedded equity-portfolio gains ($8.9bn pre-tax) provide a capital cushion that a pure-bond-portfolio peer would not have in a rising-rate environment.

9. Bear case

  1. Q2 2026 combined ratio of 100.8% is an underwriting loss, with current-accident-year ex-cat losses also rising YoY (85.1%→88.1%) — the deterioration is not fully explained by catastrophe severity alone; Commercial Lines specifically weakened from 92.9% to 104.1% combined YoY.
  2. GAAP earnings and book-value growth are heavily equity-market-dependent (40% of the portfolio); a sustained equity drawdown would hit reported book value and GAAP income much harder than a typical bond-heavy P&C peer, even though underwriting is unaffected.
  3. Sell-side FY1 (6 down/1 up in 30 days) and FY0 (8 down/0 up) EPS revisions both skew decisively negative — consistent with, not contradicting, the Q2'26 underwriting miss.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Consolidated combined ratio stays above 100% for a second consecutive quarter (Q3 2026 report, ~Oct 26).
  2. Current-accident-year ex-cat combined ratio continues rising past ~90% (was 88.1% in Q2'26).
  3. Commercial Lines combined ratio fails to normalize back under ~95% within two quarters.
  4. A sustained broad-equity-market drawdown >20% that visibly impairs book value per share (given the 40% equity allocation).
  5. Net FY1 consensus EPS revisions remain negative for two more months without stabilization.

11. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: ~2026-10-26 (Q3 2026 — estimated/pattern-based, not company-confirmed, per d4 snapshot; historically CINF has reported late-Oct, e.g. Oct 27 2025, Oct 24 2024).
  • Annual dividend-increase announcement typically accompanies the Q4/full-year release (previous increases: $0.81→$0.87 for FY2025, i.e. +7%).

12. Red-flag scan

No auditor change, material weakness, restatement, going-concern language, SEC/DOJ investigation, or short-seller report surfaced in the four earnings releases reviewed. Scope limitation: full 10-K risk-factor diff, Form 4 insider-selling pattern, and litigation/contingent-liability notes were not pulled given the time budget — this is a genuine gap in this pass, not a clean bill of health, and should be completed before sizing any position.

dossiers.CMCSA:
CMCSA — Comcast Corporation

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL. Horizon 12–36 months. Named reservation: Comcast announced on 29-Jun-2026 that it will split into two public companies (a "Comcast" broadband/wireless RemainCo and an independent "NBCUniversal" that also absorbs Sky), targeted to close in ~12 months; the capital structure, dividend policy and exact NBCUniversal stake retained (up to 19.9%, to be sold down) are not yet finalized. The 25-Sep-2026 close ($21.91) already prices in roughly a 16–24%/year perpetual decline in free cash flow — far worse than anything in the last 5–10 years of delivered results — so the valuation gap is real, but realizing it depends on a binary corporate event executing cleanly, not just on the underlying cash flows.

2. Business in plain English

Comcast sells broadband internet, video and wireless service to US households and businesses (Connectivity & Platforms, ~64% of Q2 2026 revenue) and, through NBCUniversal, makes and distributes films, TV and news (NBC, Telemundo, Universal Pictures, Peacock) and operates theme parks including the new Epic Universe (Content & Experiences, ~36% of revenue). It earns money from broadband/wireless subscriptions, advertising, content licensing and park admissions/spending. Its moat in cable/broadband is a regulated-adjacent local infrastructure duopoly; in media it is content IP and distribution scale, both now being reorganized into two separately traded companies.

  • TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) FCF ≈ $20.44bn on TTM CFO $32.52bn − capex $12.07bn (independently re-derived from XBRL; matches v1_valuation.json's D3 TTM figures exactly, cross-check passed). FCF/NI is not meaningful on a simple TTM basis because TTM NI ($11.2bn) spans quarters distorted by the Hulu gain's absence and Versant separation costs; on an adjusted-earnings basis conversion is healthy.
  • Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 operating income dropped sharply (to ~$3.49bn and $4.14bn from a normal $5.5–6.6bn run-rate) — this coincides exactly with the 1-Jan/2-Jan-2026 completion of the Versant spin-off (cable networks USA, MS NOW [renamed from MSNBC], CNBC, Golf Channel, E!, SYFY, Oxygen), which removed a high-margin earnings stream and layered on one-time separation costs. Reported figures from Q1 2026 onward are Comcast ex-Versant; the modest yoy revenue growth despite losing that business implies the comparative periods have been restated to a continuing-operations basis.
  • Capital return: Q2 2026 buybacks $900mn + dividends $1.2bn; no share repurchases after 29-Jun-2026 pending the NBCUniversal/Sky separation — capital return is paused mid-transaction, a real near-term drag on the buyback-driven part of the bull case.
  • Minority interest is immaterial (~$0.19bn).

7. Valuation — reconciled against V1 (v1_valuation_table.csv / v1_valuation.json)

V1 verdict: attractive (score 0.96/1.00). V1's reverse FCFF DCF (WACC 6.05%, 10-year fade to 3% terminal, EV $154.8bn) finds the price implies FCF shrinking at −24.2%/year for 10 years — versus a 5-year delivered CAGR of +2.8% and a 10-year delivered CAGR of +5.1%. V1's scenarios: bear +24.2%/yr, base +62.1%/yr, bull +89.5%/yr (3-yr annualised, including dividends), driven mostly by multiple re-rating (exit P/E 10.0x/17.2x/20.2x vs today's 6.2x) rather than by growth assumptions alone. I agree with the direction (cheap; implied growth is far below any reasonable base case) but not the magnitude. My own base case: low-single-digit FCF growth (0% to +3%/year) — Residential Connectivity is genuinely shrinking (−4.0% yoy) but Business Services (+3.7%), wireless (record adds), and the higher-margin, faster-growing Content & Experiences segment (+22.9%) are real, disclosed offsets. That is still dramatically above the priced-in −24%/year, so implied_vs_base = below, supporting inclusion — but V1's base/bull cases require the market to re-rate the P/E to 17–20x, which depends heavily on the NBCUniversal/Sky spin-off actually closing on favorable terms (clean investment-grade balance sheets for both entities, as management has stated as a goal but not yet delivered). A re-rating case is less certain than a pure cash-flow case, which is why I size this INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE.

8. Bull case

  1. Valuation is priced for a level of FCF decline (−16% to −24%/yr) that is far worse than anything Comcast has delivered even during the worst of cord-cutting (5y CAGR still +2.8%), leaving a large margin of safety if the business merely does not shrink.
  2. The NBCUniversal/Sky spin-off is a disclosed, dated catalyst that management frames as unlocking two focused, investment-grade companies — sum-of-the-parts is a plausible re-rating path given the conglomerate discount visible in the 6.2x multiple today.
  3. Wireless (record 448,000 adds) and Peacock (first profitable quarter) are genuinely inflecting positive at the same time broadband erosion is decelerating (−167k vs −201k a year ago), i.e., the offsets are strengthening, not just theoretical.

Bear case

  1. Residential broadband is still losing subscribers every quarter with no evidence of an inflection to growth — this is the core cash-generating asset and the secular decline (fixed wireless, cord-cutting) is real and ongoing.
  2. The spin-off is announced but unexecuted: terms for splitting debt, the size/duration of Comcast's retained NBCUniversal stake, and each entity's dividend policy are all undecided as of this writing, and buybacks are already paused — a live example of the process constraining shareholder returns before it delivers any benefit.
  3. Q4 2025/Q1 2026 already show what separation costs and losing a profitable segment (Versant) look like in the numbers; the NBCUniversal/Sky separation is a much larger transaction and could produce a similar, or larger, transitional earnings air-pocket.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (thesis-invalidation triggers)

  1. The NBCUniversal/Sky spin-off is delayed beyond Q4 2027 (18+ months from announcement) or is restructured so either resulting entity is sub-investment-grade.
  2. Residential broadband net losses exceed 250,000 in any quarter (vs. −167,000 in Q2 2026), i.e., the recent deceleration reverses.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.0x ahead of the spin (from ~2.3–2.4x now), suggesting the balance sheet is being loaded to fund the separation.
  4. Wireless net adds fall below 300,000/quarter (from 448,000 record in Q2 2026), removing the main offset to broadband erosion.
  5. The dividend is cut or suspended in connection with the spin-off.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 22-Oct-2026 (Q3 2026, per company IR release). NBCUniversal/Sky separation: targeted close ~mid-2027 (12 months from 29-Jun-2026 announcement); watch for the Form 10/S-1-type separation filing and capital-structure disclosure, expected before close.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, restatements or going-concern language identified in this review window. No SEC/DOJ investigation or short-seller report surfaced in this search window (not exhaustively verified against the full 10-K legal-proceedings note — treat as a scope limitation, not a clean bill of health). Data/model gap flagged for the lead: b1_live_scores.csv's exclude_pending_deal flag is False for CMCSA even though a major, dated corporate separation was announced 29-Jun-2026 and is disclosed in the Q2 2026 10-Q; the pending-deal exclusion in the quant pipeline appears scoped to M&A/buyout situations only, not self-initiated spin-offs — worth confirming with the B1 team.

Events checked to 2026-09-25 close, including the 29-Jun-2026 spin-off announcement. GAAP figures are labeled GAAP; adjusted EPS is labeled adjusted; Q4 2024/Q4 2025 figures are marked "derived" (annual 10-K total minus 9-month 10-Q YTD) because no company-published quarterly figure for those periods was directly sourced in this review. CMI — Cummins Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F40, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH (not REJECT — quality/moat are real; not INCLUDE — price already discounts more growth than the evidence supports). Thesis horizon: 12–36 months, revisit on a pullback toward a 13–15x NTM P/E or on two consecutive quarters of EBITDA-margin expansion into the guided range.

2. Business in plain English

Cummins designs and makes diesel/natural-gas engines, powertrains, and — increasingly — large stationary generators ("Power Systems") used for data-center backup and continuous power, plus filtration, emission-control and electrified components. Customers are truck OEMs (PACCAR, Daimler, Navistar), construction/mining equipment makers, and, in the fastest-growing segment, hyperscale data-center developers who need standby/prime power while grid capacity catches up to AI-driven demand. It earns money on engine/parts sales, aftermarket service, and a growing share of high-margin large-genset systems.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 composite flags CMI on quality (low leverage, strong ROE/ROIC) and momentum (+36% trailing). The durable part is real: Power Systems' large-genset backlog is capacity-constrained into late 2026/2027, with orders on the newest platform (QSK95) being taken through H2 2028 (Cummins CEO J. Rumsey, Q2-26 call). The artefact risk is that revenue guidance has been raised three releases running mostly on volume/mix (data-center gensets, NA on-highway recovery, China construction), while EBITDA margin actually fell YoY in Q2-26 (17.5% vs 18.4%) on higher incentive comp and R&D — i.e., the market is paying up for a top-line story whose margin delivery hasn't yet shown through.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP; adjusted noted where material)

Three consecutive raises, verified against the Cummins IR 8-K exhibits (investor.cummins.com/news/detail/701 for Q2-26; SEC 8-K EX-99.1 filings for Q1-26/Q4-25). Correction to triage: the triage note attributed V1's "excessive" valuation flag to price momentum; that is not accurate — V1's flag is a reverse-DCF result (§7) independent of the momentum factor. The guidance raises are genuine and primary-sourced, but they do not by themselves resolve the valuation question.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

FCF/NI ~1.24x (strong). SBC only ~$93M TTM (~0.27% of revenue, per V1/D3 — immaterial). Net debt $3.16bn / TTM EBITDA (~$5.01bn) ≈ 0.6x — low leverage, matches triage's characterisation. No pending M&A disclosed. Share count essentially flat (138.5–142.1M, buybacks roughly offsetting modest issuance). Two large one-offs bracket the two-year window in opposite directions (Atmus gain, Q1-24; Electrolyzer charge, Q4-25) — both are flagged above so GAAP and "clean" trends aren't conflated.

7. Valuation snapshot — reconciled with V1

V1 (systematic reverse DCF, FCFF method, SBC not added back, 10y fade to 3% terminal, WACC 8.74%) verdict: "excessive." NTM P/E 16.19x is only the 48.6th percentile of CMI's own 177-month history (i.e., not rich on a simple multiple basis) and is a discount to peer median 20.06x (CAT/PCAR/WAB) — but the reverse DCF says the $525.06 close implies 15.66%/yr FCF growth for 10 years, versus consensus FY1 growth of 8.95%, 5y delivered CAGR 8.44%, and 10y delivered CAGR 6.67%. V1 base-case 3y annualised return is −3.9% (bear −25.1%, bull +19.4%). I agree with V1's excessive call: the structural data-center tailwind is real, but it would have to compound at nearly double its own trailing rate, for a decade, with margin expansion that hasn't shown up yet, to earn today's price. Unresolved conflict to disclose: sell-side consensus price targets (mean $746, low $530) imply the stock is already below the Street's most bearish target — i.e., analysts are more bullish than either V1 or this dossier. I read that gap as sell-side targets embedding continued guidance raises and multiple re-rating that the reverse DCF treats as already-priced.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) data-center standby-power backlog is capacity-constrained into 2027–28, a multi-year, non-discretionary buildout; (2) balance sheet (0.6x net debt/EBITDA) funds it without dilution; (3) three consecutive guidance raises show real operating momentum, not just estimate resets. Bear: (1) EBITDA margin fell YoY in the most recent quarter despite the raises — the market is paying for margin that hasn't arrived; (2) on-highway engines remain cyclical (Class 8 truck demand swings), a large share of revenue outside Power Systems; (3) the price already implies growth well above anything CMI has delivered in 5 or 10 years.

9. Kill criteria

  1. EBITDA margin stays below 18.0% for two consecutive quarters despite reiterated FY26 guidance (would break the "raises are backed by margin" thesis).
  2. Power Systems / large-genset book-to-bill falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (backlog thesis breaking).
  3. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x (from ~0.6x) without offsetting FCF growth.
  4. NTM P/E re-rates above the 20x peer median without a corresponding upward revision to consensus 10-year growth.
  5. Follow-on shareholder/consumer litigation tied to the 2023–24 DOJ/EPA/CARB Clean Air Act settlement produces a material (>$200M) incremental charge beyond current accruals.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~Nov 4, 2026 (Q3-26; date not yet formally confirmed by IR as of this write-up — estimate based on historical early-Nov reporting pattern).

11. Red-flag scan

  • Regulatory: $1.675bn DOJ/EPA/California Clean Air Act settlement (largest-ever CAA penalty), finalized April 2024, for defeat-device/emissions-certification violations in pick-up-truck engines; >$325M in required remediation spend; ongoing shareholder/consumer follow-on litigation (immaterial accruals disclosed to date, but unresolved).
  • One-offs: Q1-24 $1.3bn Atmus gain (positive); Q4-25 $458M Electrolyzer/Accelera charge (negative) — both must be excluded from any "clean" growth read.
  • Insider activity: routine, small (<$0.6M each) open-market sales by VP-level executives through 2026 (CIO, Treasury VP, HR/CAO); no CEO/CFO sales found this session — no unusual pattern identified.
  • No going-concern language, no auditor change, no disclosed pending acquisition.

All figures are on a consolidated basis (Cummins Inc. and subsidiaries; no material standalone-parent distinction). Most recent period incorporated: Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-04) and the Q2-26 earnings release (2026-08-04). Events checked to 2026-09-25. GAAP figures are labelled GAAP; Cummins' own non-GAAP lens is EBITDA margin (not adjusted EPS) and is labelled as such throughout. This is research, not personalized investment advice.

CMS — CMS Energy Corp. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F40, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), reservation stated explicitly: Moody's moved the outlook on CMS/Consumers Energy to negative (from stable) over the size of a $24bn five-year capital plan relative to regulatory cost-recovery timing, and the balance sheet is securitization-heavy, complicating a clean leverage read. Valuation is not demanding and the earnings-guidance track record is strong. Horizon: 24–48 months (regulated utility — this is a rate-of-return/dividend-growth thesis, not a re-rating trade).

2. Business in plain English

CMS Energy is the holding company for Consumers Energy, Michigan's largest combined electric-and-gas regulated utility, serving ~6.7M of the state's residents. It earns a regulated return on the capital it invests in generation, transmission and distribution, set by the Michigan Public Service Commission (MPSC). It is one of the more purely "regulated-utility" names in its peer set (minimal unregulated/merchant exposure since NorthStar Clean Energy is a small renewables developer segment).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage flagged CMS for a "cheap NTM P/E (15.4x) for above-average guided growth" and a multi-year 6–8% EPS-growth record. That growth record is durable and verified: 2024 adjusted EPS $3.34, 2025 adjusted EPS $3.61 (beat the $3.54–3.60 guide range — the 22nd/23rd consecutive year of meeting-or-beating guidance per company messaging), 2026 guide $3.83–3.90 (raised twice from an initial $3.80–3.87), and a newly introduced 2027 guide of $4.08–4.17 (+6.7% at the midpoint) — all consistent with the reaffirmed 6–8% long-term algorithm. The one thing that looks like an artefact at first glance is the Q2-2026 earnings "miss": adjusted EPS of $0.37 vs. $0.71 a year earlier and vs. a ~$0.76 consensus (a >50% shortfall). Management's own bridge (Q2-26 earnings call) attributes it to items already contemplated in the 2026 plan: an $0.08 unfavourable weather comparison, $0.19 of storm-related O&M, and $0.23 from non-repeating 2025 liability-management benefits — and the company reaffirmed full-year guidance the same day. I read this as a real quarterly print, correctly explained, not a data conflict with the multi-year growth thesis — but it is a reminder that CMS's quarters are lumpy and headline "misses" will recur.

7. Valuation snapshot (no V1 row exists for CMS — independent reverse DCF)

No systematic V1 valuation exists for CMS this cycle (not in v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json); v1_verdict is therefore null. - Reverse dividend-discount model (appropriate for a regulated utility where FCF is structurally negative): price $62.95, current dividend $2.28, cost of equity 7.0–8.0% (rf 5.17% + beta ~0.55 × ERP 4.14%, giving ≈7.45% central), 10y fade to 3% terminal growth → implied 10-year dividend/EPS growth ≈3.9–6.7% (central ≈5.2%). That sits at or below the company's own reaffirmed 6–8% long-term algorithm and below the guided FY26→FY27 step of +6.7% — i.e., the market is not paying for anything CMS hasn't already told investors to expect. NTM P/E ≈16.3x ($62.95 / FY26 guide midpoint $3.865) and EV/EBITDA ≈14.6x are both in the normal range for large regulated multi-utility peers (AEE/WEC/DTE typically trade 13–16x EV/EBITDA in this cycle; exact peer NTM P/E not independently recomputed this session). - Read: implied growth (≈5.2%) < base case (≈7%, the algorithm midpoint) → satisfies the "priced at or below base case" bar for inclusion.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) 20-year unbroken dividend-growth streak and a guidance record that has never been cut in the window checked; (2) FY27 guide (+6.7% at midpoint) shows the growth algorithm rolling forward intact; (3) valuation (16.3x NTM P/E, ~5.2% implied growth) does not demand anything beyond the guided range. Bear: (1) Moody's negative outlook is a genuine forward-looking risk — if the $24bn capital plan outruns rate-case recovery, the credit profile (and eventually the equity story) could deteriorate; (2) securitization-heavy leverage makes headline debt ratios hard to compare to peers and could mask true balance-sheet risk; (3) Q2-26 shows how volatile quarterly prints can be (weather/storm/comp timing) even when the full-year plan is intact — a headline-risk name for anyone who reacts to single quarters.

9. Kill criteria

  1. Moody's or S&P actually downgrades CMS Energy or Consumers Energy (current status: negative outlook only, ratings affirmed).
  2. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($3.83–3.90) is cut mid-year (reaffirmed twice through Q2-26 to date).
  3. An MPSC rate-case order disallows a material (>10%) share of pending capital-recovery requests.
  4. Net debt continues rising without a matching credit-rating cushion or explicit securitization pass-through disclosure.
  5. Adjusted EPS growth falls outside the reaffirmed 6–8% long-term range for two consecutive fiscal years.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~late Oct/early Nov 2026 (Q3-26; exact date not found in the sources checked this session — last year's Q3-25 was reported/filed 2025-10-30, used as the base-rate estimate).

11. Red-flag scan

  • Credit: Moody's negative outlook (~March 2026) on CMS Energy/Consumers Energy tied to the $24bn five-year capex plan vs. cost-recovery timing; S&P affirmed BBB+/stable as of its last confirmed action (Oct 2024 — may be stale, not re-verified this session); Moody's separately has an unsecured rating of Baa1/Consumers Energy shelf (P)A2.

dossiers.COR:
COR — Cencora, Inc. (formerly AmerisourceBergen)

Most recent period incorporated: Q3 FY2026 10-Q (fiscal quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-05) and the Q3 FY2026 earnings release (8-K Ex-99.1, filed 2026-08-05). Also read the FY2025 10-K (period ended 2025-09-30, filed 2025-11-25) for the annual opioid/legal disclosures. Checked SEC EDGAR for events to 2026-09-25; no 10-K/10-Q/8-K dated after 2026-08-05 was found (Cencora's FY2026 10-K, for the year ending 2026-09-30, is not due until ~late Nov 2026 and had not been filed as of this review).

Basis: all figures are consolidated, GAAP, USD, from the 10-Q/10-K/8-K as filed (CIK 0001140859), unless labeled non-GAAP/segment. Cencora's fiscal year ends September 30 — one quarter offset from CAH (June 30) and three months offset from CCI (December 31); flagged because it affects any same-period peer comparison.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon 18–36 months. One-sentence reason: the same drug-distribution oligopoly economics as CAH with a slightly better specialty/oncology mix, a three-quarter-running adjusted-EPS guidance raise streak, and a reverse DCF implying only low-single-digit 10-year growth — against a real, recurring earnings-quality flag (two straight years of PharmaLex goodwill impairments and a business now "exploring strategic alternatives" for several sub-units) that is disclosed and sized, not hidden.

2. Business in plain English

Cencora is one of the three dominant US pharmaceutical wholesalers (with Cardinal Health and McKesson), distributing branded and generic drugs to retail and hospital pharmacies on thin (~1.5–2%) gross margins earned on volume and working-capital efficiency. It has been building a specialty-oncology and now urology physician-services platform (RCA — Retina Consultants of America, acquired Jan 2025; OneOncology, equity stake stepped up to full consolidation in Feb 2026) inside its larger U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment, plus an International Healthcare Solutions segment (mainly World Courier and European distribution) and an "Other" bucket (MWI Animal Health, Profarma, U.S. Consulting Services, remaining PharmaLex units) that management is now exploring strategic alternatives for — i.e., a likely partial divestiture.

3. Why the model likes it, and whether that's durable

Triage's framing (same oligopoly economics as peers, slightly better specialty mix, weak recent momentum despite 20% street upside) holds up. The durable part: adjusted diluted EPS grew 16.3% in FY2025 ($16.00 vs $13.76) and FY2026 adjusted-EPS guidance was raised at every quarterly release reviewed (see §5), driven by real segment operating-income growth, not one-off items — GLP-1 volume and the OneOncology/RCA specialty build-out are named, structural drivers in the company's own release language. The less durable / genuinely mixed part: FY2026 revenue-growth guidance was cut, not raised, over the same year — from "7% to 9%" (Q1 FY26 release) to "4% to 6%" (Q3 FY26 release) for both total company and the U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment — even as EPS guidance kept rising. That combination (revenue guide down, EPS guide up) is consistent with margin/mix improvement and a smaller "Other" segment base (MWI Animal Health reclassified toward held-for-sale), but it means the "growth" the model is scoring should be read as margin-driven, not volume-driven, and the two should not be conflated.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly, GAAP)

Treat GAAP EPS as structurally noisy here; adjusted EPS is the more informative operating series.

5. Guidance track record (last 4 releases)

Q2 FY26 (2026-05-06) $17.65–$17.90 raised (+$0.20/+$0.15) not re-quoted at same breakout in this release —
Q3 FY26 (2026-08-05) $17.75–$17.95 raised (+$0.10/+$0.05) 4%–6% cut from 7–9%

Adjusted EPS was raised (or held) at every checkpoint, never cut, across the year reviewed. Revenue growth guidance, however, was walked down from 7–9% to 4–6% over the same period — the company's own segment guidance table (Q3 FY26 release) shows U.S. Healthcare Solutions revenue growth cut identically, alongside International Healthcare Solutions (~8% growth) and Other (~6% growth, i.e., not being wound down as fast as the "strategic alternatives" language might suggest). This is a genuine, disclosed divergence between the top-line and bottom-line guidance tracks, not a data error.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Entity scope: all figures are consolidated Cencora, Inc. (10-Q balance sheet/cash-flow statement, 2026-06-30), not segment or subsidiary figures unless stated.
  • FCF conversion: nine-month FY2026 OCF was $1,687.5m vs nine-month FY2025 OCF of $741.7m — but quarterly OCF is extremely lumpy (Q1 FY26 alone was −$2,305m, Q2 FY26 −$967m, before a large positive swing) driven by working-capital timing around drug-price cycles and the OneOncology consolidation; nine-month capex was $511.0m. Full-year FCF should be read off the eventual FY2026 10-K, not annualized from any single quarter.
  • GAAP vs adjusted gap: FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS $7.96 vs adjusted $16.00 — roughly a 2x gap, the widest of the three companies in this batch, driven by acquisition-intangible amortization, the PharmaLex goodwill impairments (§3), litigation/opioid items, and (in FY2026) the OneOncology remeasurement gain. Every reconciling line is itemized in the company's own non-GAAP tables (10-Q Exhibit 99.1), not a black box.
  • Leverage: total debt at 2026-06-30 = $11.72bn (long-term $11.44bn + current $0.28bn), up sharply from $7.92bn at 2025-12-31 — the increase is the debt-financed OneOncology step-up acquisition (closed Feb 2026), confirmed in the cash-flow statement ("Cost of acquired companies, net of cash acquired" $4.97bn nine-month FY26 vs $4.00bn prior year). Cash $2.82bn → net debt ≈ $8.9bn. FY2026 guided adjusted operating income ≈$4.2bn base × 1.13–1.14 growth ≈ $4.7–4.8bn, plus run-rate D&A (~$1.0–1.1bn annualized from the nine-month $779m figure) → approximate EBITDA $5.7–5.9bn, putting net debt/EBITDA at roughly 1.5x — moderate, and elevated versus FY2025 levels specifically because of the OneOncology deal financing.
  • Stockholders' equity is thin ($3.05bn at 2026-06-30 vs total assets $83.8bn) — the same buyback-driven capital structure as CAH; not itself a distress signal given the leverage above, but it means small absolute swings in retained earnings move book equity a lot.
  • Opioid litigation: accrued liability for the Distributor Settlement Agreement and related opioid litigation was $4.2bn at 2026-06-30 (down from $4.3bn at 2025-09-30), expected to be paid over the next 13 years, with $396.2m expected in the next twelve months. In Q3 FY26 the company recorded a net credit (income) of $88.6m from litigation/opioid items (a favorable accrual revision or settlement-cost reduction), a data point worth noting as the mirror image of CAH's ongoing net cash outflow.
  • Recurring impairments as an earnings-quality flag: a further $249.5m "impairment of assets, including goodwill" was booked in Q1 FY2026 (nine-month total, per the 10-Q income statement) — on top of the $723.9m PharmaLex impairment in Q4 FY2025 and $418.0m in Q4 FY2024. Three consecutive fiscal years (FY2024, FY2025, FY2026-to-date) with a material goodwill/asset impairment is a pattern, not a one-off, concentrated in the "Other" segment now under strategic review.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

Price used: $306.92 (2026-09-25 close, d4 live snapshot). NTM P/E ≈15.5x (d4, calendarized), trailing P/E 22.8x (distorted by the Q4 FY25 GAAP loss quarter), FCF yield ≈3.5% (materially lower than CAH's, reflecting COR's lumpier working capital and larger recent M&A cash outlay), sell-side mean target $369.31 (+20%, matching the triage note). No V1 row exists for COR — v1_verdict is null.

Reverse DCF (2-stage, per-share, terminal growth 2.5%, FY2026 guided adjusted-EPS midpoint ≈$17.85 used as the owner-earnings proxy): at a WACC of 7.5–9.0%, the $306.92 price implies roughly +0.3% to +3.7% annualized 10-year earnings growth — modestly higher than CAH's implied range but still well below COR's own recent trajectory (adjusted EPS +16.3% FY2025, guided +11–15% FY2026). Analyst base case: high-single-digit (7–9%/yr) 10-year adjusted EPS growth, reflecting some deceleration from the current pace as GLP-1 tailwinds normalize and OneOncology integration matures, but above the market's implied ~1–4%. valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "below" (price implies less growth than the base case), though with a thinner margin of safety than CAH given COR's higher debt load and recurring impairment pattern.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Adjusted EPS guidance raised at every checkpoint in FY2026, on top of 16.3% FY2025 adjusted-EPS growth, evidencing durable execution even as the revenue guide was trimmed. (2) OneOncology/RCA give Cencora a specialty-oncology and retina-care physician-platform business with materially better economics than core distribution, now fully consolidated and contributing to segment profit. (3) The reverse DCF shows the market paying for only low-single-digit growth in a company that has consistently delivered double-digit adjusted EPS growth.

Bear: (1) Three consecutive fiscal years of goodwill/asset impairments (PharmaLex primarily) is a genuine capital-allocation track record concern, not a one-off; the businesses now under "strategic alternatives" review (MWI Animal Health, Profarma, U.S. Consulting Services) could realize further losses on sale. (2) Debt nearly doubled in two quarters to fund the OneOncology step-up ($7.9bn → $11.7bn), and net debt/EBITDA at ~1.5x, while not high in absolute terms, is a genuine increase in financial risk versus a year ago. (3) Revenue-growth guidance was cut from 7–9% to 4–6% during FY2026 — the "raise" story is entirely a margin/mix and buyback story, not a volume story, and that is a narrower, more fragile basis for continued EPS beats if margin gains stall.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut at any quarterly release (breaking the current raise streak).
  2. A further goodwill/asset impairment exceeding $150m is booked in any single quarter (a fourth consecutive year of the PharmaLex-style pattern).
  3. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x without a disclosed, value-accretive reason.
  4. U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment revenue growth falls below 3% for two consecutive quarters (below even the cut 4-6% FY26 guide).
  5. The "Other" segment strategic-alternatives review results in a divestiture loss exceeding $200m versus carrying value.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q4/FY2026 (fiscal year end), expected ~2026-11-04 (d4 snapshot next_earnings_date; the FY2026 10-K would follow, typically ~3 weeks later based on the FY2025 pattern of a 2025-11-25 10-K filing). Watch for: FY2027 initial guidance at that release, and any announcement on the "Other" segment strategic-alternatives review (MWI Animal Health, Profarma, U.S. Consulting Services).

11. Red-flag scan

Recurring PharmaLex-related goodwill impairment (three straight fiscal years, $418.0m FY24 + $723.9m FY25 + $249.5m FY26-to-date) — the clearest, most persistent red flag in this dossier. Opioid litigation: $4.2bn accrued, payments over 13 years — disclosed and, unusually, saw a net credit in the most recent quarter. A $113.5m equity-investment impairment in Q4 FY25 alongside the PharmaLex charge. Debt roughly doubled in two quarters to fund the OneOncology acquisition. No auditor change, restatement or going-concern language identified in the sections reviewed. Insider Form-4 pattern and short-seller reports were not checked in this pass — disclosed gap.

dossiers.CPAY:
CPAY — Corpay, Inc. (fka FLEETCOR) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F41, Wave 2, Standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — real double-digit organic growth at a reasonable adjusted multiple, but a named reservation: leverage (2.55x, above the company's own historical comfort zone), a fresh $100.9m preliminary FTC settlement charge (pending approval), and a wide, growing GAAP-vs-adjusted earnings gap. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

Corpay (ticker changed from FLT to CPAY in 2024) sells corporate-payments software: fuel/fleet cards for trucking and field-service fleets, virtual corporate cards and AP automation ("Corpay One"/"Comdata"), and cross-border B2B payments (formerly Cambridge/AFEX). Customers are mid-market and large businesses that pay Corpay a recurring transaction/interchange-like fee for every fuel purchase, invoice payment or FX transfer it processes. It grows mostly by cross-selling its existing ~800k+ commercial customers into more products and by bolt-on acquisitions, funded with meaningful leverage. Competitive position: #1 or #2 in US fuel cards (WEX is the main competitor), a smaller but growing challenger in cross-border payments (versus Western Union Business Solutions, Convera) and corporate card (versus Amex, Brex).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1/triage flags: Quality (ROE 32%, gross-profit/assets 0.076–0.28th pct in one direction, high leverage percentile pulling composite down slightly), Value (moderate — 42nd EP percentile), Momentum strong (12-1m return ~40%, 79th pct), Earnings-momentum (SUE) very strong (94th pct). Triage: quality 4/5, growth 4/5, price_vs_growth 4/5; "revenue +22%, margin 23%, ROE 29% and 13.1x NTM P/E is a rare combination of real growth and reasonable price." This is partly durable, partly an artefact: organic revenue growth (double digits for 5 consecutive quarters per management) and ROE are real and confirmed in filings. But part of the reported "adjusted EPS" acceleration (+36% YoY in Q2 2026, +29% in Q1 2026) is inflated by (a) heavy share buybacks (diluted share count down 7.1% YoY in Q2 2026) funded by increasing leverage, and (b) a widening list of non-GAAP add-backs (see §6). The earnings-momentum (SUE) factor score is therefore flattered by a metric (adjusted EPS) that management, not GAAP, defines.

5. Guidance track record (last 3 releases)

  • Q4 2025/FY2025 release (Feb 2026): initial FY2026 guide not independently re-verified in this pass (time-boxed); see Q1/Q2 releases below for the trend.

  • Q2 2026 release (Aug 2026): FY2026 revenue $5.290–5.330bn (bottom raised $40m); adjusted EPS $27.15–27.55 (raised ~$0.45 at the midpoint). Q3 2026 adjusted EPS guide $7.05–7.25. Verdict: guidance has been raised at each of the last two releases, consistent with the accelerating organic-revenue narrative — this part of the bull case is verified, not asserted.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • GAAP-to-adjusted gap (Q2 2026, $m): SBC 32.0; amortization 85.1; legal settlements and litigation 100.9 (see red flags); loss on debt extinguishment 6.6; integration/deal costs 38.1; restructuring 2.8; equity-method adjustments 14.3; other 2.6; less gain on disposition (1.1) → total pre-tax add-backs $281.4m vs. GAAP pre-tax income. Adjusted net income $464.4m vs. GAAP $248.3m — adjusted is 87% higher than GAAP this quarter, an unusually wide gap driven by the one-time litigation charge plus recurring heavy acquisition-intangible amortization.
  • FCF conversion (FY, OCF−capex, $m): FY2023 $2,101.1−$153.8=$1,947.3; FY2024 $1,940.6−$175.2=$1,765.4 (−9.3%); FY2025 $1,499.9−$200.8=$1,299.1 (−26.4% YoY). Full-year OCF fell 22.7% in FY2025 despite revenue +13.9% and adjusted EPS growth in the mid-teens–20s — a real cash-conversion deterioration, not just a GAAP-vs-adjusted artefact. Partial offset: H1 2026 OCF ($1,413.5m) is already +32.6% vs. the comparable H1 2025 figure disclosed in the Q2 2026 10-Q, suggesting FY2025's dip was partly working-capital timing rather than a structural break — flagged as unresolved, not dismissed.
  • Leverage: company-stated "2.55x" gross leverage exiting Q2 2026 (down from "2.7x" exiting Q1 2026, per the Q1 release), after refinancing and upsizing the revolver to $3.7bn. Both readings sit above the 2.5x level the prior (v3) audit used as a red line; balance-sheet debt (LongTermDebt, XBRL) rose from $8.0bn (FY24) to $10.6bn (Q2 2026) — a $2.6bn increase over 18 months funding both buybacks ($786m in Q1 2026 alone — 2.4m shares) and M&A.
  • Buybacks/share count: diluted shares fell from 71.4m (Q2 2025) to 66.3m (Q2 2026), a real 7.1% reduction that mechanically boosts EPS growth independent of operating performance.
  • Cash: grew from $1.55bn (FY24) to $3.16bn (Q2 2026), partly reflecting the $81m gain on a business sale in Q1 2026 and debt-facility upsizing.
  • No dividend (buyback-only capital return).

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for CPAY (v1_valuation_table.csv has no CPAY line) → v1_verdict = null; this section is the analyst's own reverse DCF. - Price (25-Sep-2026 close) $398.11; market cap ≈ $26.14bn; NTM P/E ≈13.1x on adjusted-EPS consensus (per triage card); trailing GAAP P/E ≈24.2x (TTM GAAP EPS ≈$16.42 computed from filings). The 13.1x-vs-24.2x spread is almost entirely the GAAP/adjusted gap in §6, not a valuation anomaly. - Reverse DCF (own model, 10-yr explicit + Gordon terminal, r=9.0%, terminal g=3.0%): using a blended base-year FCF of $1,532m (average of FY24/FY25 actual FCF, to dampen the FY25 working-capital dip) implies the market is pricing ≈2.9%/yr 10-year FCF growth; using FY2025's actual (depressed) FCF alone implies ≈5.1%/yr; using FY2024's FCF alone implies ≈1.1%/yr. 1. Verdict

WATCH — overturns the triage advance. Thesis horizon if resolved favourably: 12–24 months. The triage read CPRT as "near-monopoly economics intact" with growth merely decelerating; primary-source work through the just-reported Q4 FY2026 (filed 10-Sep-2026) and the 10-Sep-2026 M&A announcement finds a materially different, more adverse picture: gross margin compressed ~350bps YoY in the quarter, operating cash flow is down year-to-date, the CEO abruptly departed with the founder returning mid-cycle, plaintiff law firms have opened securities-related "investigations," and the company has just committed $1.9B of cash to an antitrust-gated acquisition (ACV Auctions) that management itself says is EPS-neutral in year one. None of this is disqualifying on its own, but together it removes the margin of safety the triage assumed. Condition to move to INCLUDE: a quarter of stabilised-or-improving gross margin, HSR clearance and a credible integration update on ACV, and no material finding from the ongoing securities-law-firm inquiries. No V1 systematic valuation row exists for CPRT; v1_verdict = null.

2. Business in plain English

Copart runs the largest online salvage- and used-vehicle auction network in the US (with UK/international operations), taking vehicles on consignment mostly from insurance companies after a total-loss determination (and, on a smaller "purchase agreement" basis, buying some vehicles outright) and selling them via its own online auction (VB3/VB Advantage) to dismantlers, rebuilders, dealers and exporters. Revenue is mainly per-unit service/auction fees plus, on purchased units, the sale margin itself. The moat is largely a real-asset one — a nationwide land bank of storage/processing yards that is genuinely hard to replicate (permitting, capital, insurer-relationship lock-in) — layered under a software/marketplace business.

Sector routing note: GICS files CPRT under "Diversified Support Services" / "Auto & Truck Dealerships" adjacency, neither of which is a clean fit. Per the stock-analysis skill's routing rules, this is nearest to the retail-ecommerce.md marketplace framework (fee/margin on transaction volume — "GMV × take rate" analog), with the land-bank/permitted-yard asset base treated as a moat feature (analogous to the waste-environmental "permitted disposal asset" logic) rather than the primary profit driver. Explicitly rejected: auto.md (Copart does not manufacture, retail, or finance vehicles) and people-businesses.md (this is not a pure labour/fee brokerage — the yard network is a real capital asset).

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. The land-bank moat (permitted yard capacity, insurer relationships) has not gone away; margin pressure this quarter is explicitly framed by management as investment spend (new products, wholesale facilities), which could reverse once those investments mature. 2. Net-cash balance sheet funds the ACV deal without leverage; if antitrust clearance is obtained and integration goes to plan, management's own framing (accretive from FY28) implies a longer-run earnings step-up. 3. Founder Jay Adair's return as CEO could be read as a stabilising, execution-focused signal after a rocky stretch, by someone who built the business the first time.

Bear (3): 1. Margin compression (−350bps YoY in the reported quarter) plus a YoY EPS decline is a real earnings-quality deterioration, not merely a deceleration in an otherwise-strong story, and the stated causes (new-service investment, facility cost inflation) are exactly the kind of "temporary" explanation that deserves scepticism until at least one more quarter confirms the trend reverses. 2. An abrupt CEO exit (announced 29-Jun-2026, effective 31-Jul-2026, stock −8% same day) alongside multiple plaintiff-firm "securities fraud investigation" press releases is a governance yellow flag that should be tracked to resolution (these law-firm releases are frequently opportunistic and non-predictive of any finding, but the pattern coincided with a real, disclosed earnings deterioration and a leadership change, which raises the bar for dismissing it outright). 3. The $1.9B all-cash ACV acquisition is: (a) subject to HSR antitrust clearance in a space where Copart is already the dominant salvage-auction player, so clearance is not guaranteed on current terms; (b) management's own guidance is EPS-neutral in year one, i.e. no near-term financial benefit is being offered to offset the integration and execution risk; and (c) it follows, rather than precedes, a quarter of margin and cash-flow deterioration — a moment of demonstrated operating softness is an unusual time to deploy the balance sheet's full net-cash cushion.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Gross margin below 43% (i.e., not recovering meaningfully from the reported 44.6% FY26 full-year level) for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Operating cash flow (trailing nine/twelve months) below the prior-year comparable period for a third consecutive reporting period.

  4. Any securities-class-action complaint actually filed (as opposed to a law-firm "investigation" solicitation) naming Copart or its officers.
  5. Diluted EPS down year-over-year for two consecutive quarters.

1. Verdict

2. Business in plain English

CRH is the largest vertically integrated building-materials company focused on the US market: it owns the quarries, cement/aggregates plants and asphalt/ready-mix operations (Americas Materials Solutions), value-added building products (Americas Building Solutions) and an International Solutions segment (Europe/other), selling to public infrastructure (roads, bridges), non-residential and residential construction customers. It makes money by vertically integrating from raw-material extraction (aggregates, cement) through to finished products and paving/ construction services, capturing margin at each step, and by consistently acquiring smaller regional players ("bolt-ons") to densify its footprint. Share count ~665.3m, quarterly dividend $0.39/share (+5% YoY), active $0.3bn/quarter buyback program alongside the acquisition spend — capital return continues even while funding M&A, a sign of balance-sheet confidence, though also a reason leverage is rising on both fronts simultaneously.

7. Valuation snapshot — no V1 row exists for CRH; independent reverse-engineered view

d4 snapshot: NTM P/E ≈13.4x, TTM P/E ≈15.0x. No V1 row exists for CRH in v1_valuation_table.csv (confirmed by direct search); v1_verdict is therefore null. Own calculation: market cap (25-Sep-2026 close $85.04 × 665.3m shares) ≈$56.6bn; using 30-Jun-2026 net debt ≈$14.9bn, EV ≈$71.5bn; against FY26-guided adjusted EBITDA midpoint $8.3bn, current EV/EBITDA ≈8.6x. Triage's own peer read (VMC/MLM, the two closest US aggregates comparables) typically trade at meaningfully higher EV/EBITDA multiples reflecting premium "pure-play aggregates" positioning; CRH's discount reflects its more diversified (and historically slower-growing) European/International Solutions mix and its heavier M&A/integration load, but the 12-month-old margin-expansion and cash-generation trend is not priced at a premium the way it is for its narrower peers — this is the crux of the "cheap despite steady fundamentals" triage thesis, and primary-source results (§4–6) corroborate rather than contradict it. This does not require heroic growth assumptions to work: even a continuation of the current guided EBITDA trajectory (no re-rating credit at all) supports a positive base case; a modest re-rating toward peer multiples (plausible given fresh S&P 500 index inclusion — noted in the FY2025 release — and Arcosa accretion) would add meaningfully more. Implied growth in the current price is below what my base case would deliver (i.e. the market is not even crediting CRH with simply executing its own already-guided plan at its current multiple) → implied_vs_base = "below".

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) the pending $8.5bn all-cash acquisition of Arcosa (announced 22 Jun 2026, 11.5x 2026E EBITDA, ~35mt of 2025 aggregates shipments plus a top-3 critical-infrastructure-products platform) reinforces CRH's #1 US aggregates position and is management-guided to be accretive to earnings, margin and cash flow within 12 months of completion, with $175m of run-rate synergies targeted by year three; (2) US infrastructure/data-center/reshoring capex provides multi-year structural demand for aggregates and related products; (3) 12 consecutive years of margin expansion plus continued bolt-on M&A discipline is a proven, repeatable capital-allocation model ("CRH Winning Way").

Bear: (1) leverage is rising on two fronts simultaneously (organic M&A pace + the debt-financed Arcosa deal, pro forma FY2026E net debt/adjusted EBITDA guided to 2.4x by the company itself) — a US non-residential/ infrastructure demand slowdown (e.g., federal IIJA funding lapse) would hit EBITDA and leverage at the same time; (2) Arcosa closing is not guaranteed — subject to Arcosa stockholder approval and regulatory (antitrust) clearance, expected to close only in Q1 2027, leaving a multi-quarter integration/execution risk window; (3) the stock's 12-month momentum (−20.5%) shows the market is currently unwilling to pay up for this story despite the fundamentals — a "value trap" risk if the re-rating catalyst (index inclusion, Arcosa accretion) does not show up in the numbers on schedule.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.0x (vs ≈1.8x today, 2.4x pro forma guided for the Arcosa close) — would jeopardize the stated investment-grade commitment.
  2. Arcosa deal fails to close or closes later than Q1 2027 guidance (stockholder vote or regulatory block) — a specific, dated, binary catalyst-failure trigger.
  3. FY2026 guidance (Net income $3.9–4.1bn / Adj. EBITDA $8.1–8.5bn) is cut at any remaining 2026 release — the first guidance cut since the framework was initiated in Feb 2026 would be a material trend break.
  4. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracts more than 100bps YoY in any two consecutive quarters (vs the +100bps FY2025 expansion and the 12-year expansion streak management cites).
  5. Any quarter of negative organic (ex-M&A) revenue growth in Americas Materials Solutions, the core aggregates franchise, for two consecutive quarters.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-10-29 (Q3 2026). Arcosa stockholder vote and regulatory clearance process ongoing; expected deal close Q1 2027. S&P 500 index inclusion already completed (per FY2025 release) — a one-time technical tailwind already realized, not a forward catalyst. Quarterly dividend cadence and $0.3bn/quarter buyback continuing.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Item 3 Legal Proceedings (FY2025 10-K): boilerplate — "The Company is from time to time a party to various legal proceedings that arise in the ordinary course of business. We do not believe any pending legal proceeding... will have a material effect" — no material litigation identified, a notably clean profile relative to typical large-cap peers.

  • No going-concern language, no restatement, no material-weakness or auditor-change items identified.
  • Rising leverage trend (§6/§8) is the closest thing to a red flag in this filing set — real, disclosed, quantified, and explicitly bounded by management's own 2.4x pro forma target.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — a near-monopoly commercial real-estate data/analytics moat funding a large, multi-year residential ("Homes.com") build-out that has just turned an EBITDA-positive corner; named reservation: GAAP earnings are still near breakeven, full-year revenue guidance was actually cut even as EBITDA guidance was raised, and capital-allocation credibility is still being rebuilt under activist (Third Point) pressure. 2. Business in plain English

CoStar Group sells subscription data, analytics and marketing services to the commercial real-estate industry (CoStar, LoopNet, Apartments.com, Ten-X, STR, Matterport 3D-capture, and others) — a business with a genuine, decades-old data moat (CoStar's owned research/photography/leasing-comp database is very hard to replicate) and ~47% margins in its core segments per the triage note. Since 2021 it has plowed several billion dollars into building "Homes.com," a residential listing portal, to compete with Zillow — a large, still-loss-making bet that has drawn activist pressure (Third Point) to cut spending.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage: quality 4/5, growth 4/5, price_vs_growth 4/5; b1 factor read shows very strong momentum-percentile inputs but weak-to-negative quality percentiles on ROE/OCF-to-assets (consistent with the depressed consolidated GAAP profitability below) — i.e., the model likes CSGP mostly on growth/momentum, not on quality ratios, which are genuinely poor at the consolidated level right now. The core CRE-data moat (durable) is being partly offset in the reported numbers by the Homes.com investment phase (a real, disclosed, temporary drag, not an accounting artefact) — durability judgment: durable moat, temporarily depressed consolidated profitability, and the Q2 2026 print is the first primary-source evidence the drag is easing.

NTM P/E per triage card 16.9x (on consensus/adjusted EPS); trailing P/E 156x (GAAP, essentially meaningless given the near-zero FY2025 GAAP EPS base — do not use trailing GAAP P/E for this name). - Mechanical reverse DCF on trailing (depressed) FY2025 FCF ($123m): implies the market is pricing in an implausible ≈27%/yr 10-year FCF growth rate. The normalized-proxy implied growth (~9.5%) is close to, and very slightly below, a defensible base case (~10%) → implied_vs_base = "in_line." This is a genuinely uncertain estimate (the normalization assumption is a judgement call, not a disclosed figure) — confidence on this section is low-to-medium, not the "cheap at a 7-year low" framing the initial triage note suggested; our own analysis lands closer to fair value than to a clear bargain.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Core CRE-data business is a genuine, multi-decade moat with ~47%-margin economics (per triage) that keeps compounding regardless of the Homes.com outcome; (2) Q2 2026 was the first quarter the Residential segment (including Homes.com) was Adjusted-EBITDA-positive, a real, primary-source-verified inflection, with EBITDA guidance raised in the same release; (3) net cash balance sheet gives real optionality (buyback authorization, further bolt-ons) without leverage risk. Bear: (1) GAAP profitability is essentially zero (FY2025 net income $7m on $4.3bn+ of revenue) and has been declining for three straight years as Homes.com spend ramped — the "inflection" is one quarter of data; (2) full-year revenue guidance was cut in the same release that raised EBITDA guidance, a genuinely mixed signal that the market (correctly, per stock-price reaction) treated as a caution flag, not an unambiguous positive; (3) management's capital-allocation credibility is still being actively rebuilt under Third Point activist pressure — the $300m 2026 spending cut was a response to investor pressure, not a self-initiated pivot, and the company does not reach sustained positive Homes.com profitability until 2029–2030 on its own guidance.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Full-year revenue guidance is cut again at the next quarterly release (already cut once, Jan→Jul 2026).
  2. Residential-segment Adjusted EBITDA reverts to negative for two consecutive quarters after the Q2 2026 inflection.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 24–36 months.

CVS is a genuine, multi-quarter operational turnaround (Aetna medical costs improving, Medicare Advantage star ratings recovered sharply, guidance raised in three of the last four releases) trading at a statistically cheap multiple (10.6x NTM P/E, 8.8th percentile of its own 14-year history). CVS Health is a diversified health-care conglomerate with three engines: Aetna (health insurance, including a large Medicare Advantage book), Health Services (CVS Caremark, the pharmacy-benefit manager that negotiates drug prices and rebates for employers/insurers, plus Oak Street Health primary-care clinics and Signify Health home assessments), and Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness (roughly 9,000 retail pharmacies).
