dossiers.GD:
General Dynamics (GD) — Diligence Dossier

Recency gate: Most recent period incorporated: Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-07-05, 10-Q filed 2026-07-29; earnings released 2026-07-29). Checked for events to 2026-09-25 close, including the FY2027 continuing resolution signed 2026-09-01 (funds the government, defense included, through 2026-12-11). Data-quality note: this session obtained GD's Q2'26 earnings-release exhibit directly from SEC EDGAR (Archives access was intermittently down earlier in the session but recovered); the FY2025 10-K's narrative risk-factor and legal-proceedings sections were not independently re-read in full in this session — the litigation items below come from secondary sources and a prior-year (FY2023-era) 10-K reference and should be re-verified against the current 10-K before this dossier is relied on for sizing a position. GD reports very little non-GAAP adjustment — figures below are GAAP unless stated otherwise.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months. Of the three companies in this batch, GD has the cleanest and most currently-confirmed positive story: three consecutive quarters of raised full-year guidance, a record $136.5B backlog with a 1.4x book-to-bill, broad-based growth across all four segments (including a Marine Systems margin that is improving, not deteriorating, contrary to the multi-year execution-risk narrative this dossier set out to test), strong free cash flow, and the lowest leverage of the batch. The main reason it screened with only a middling Momentum score is that the quant snapshot underlying this batch appears to predate GD's Q2 2026 report (see the data-quality note below) — the fundamental picture as of this writing is stronger than the screen shows.

2. Business in plain English

General Dynamics is a diversified US defense and aerospace prime operating four segments: Aerospace (Gulfstream business jets — design, manufacture, and after-market support), Marine Systems (nuclear submarines — Columbia-class and Virginia-class — built at Electric Boat, plus surface ships at Bath Iron Works and NASSCO), Combat Systems (armored vehicles including the Abrams tank and Stryker, plus munitions), and Technologies (GDIT — federal IT/mission-systems services, plus Mission Systems electronics). It earns money primarily from multi-year contracts with the US government (Navy, Army, federal civilian agencies) and, in Aerospace, from private and corporate buyers of business jets.

3. Why the model likes it

From the preliminary quant screen (lead_prelim_rank.csv, families Q/V/M): GD ranks #36 of ~500, prelim composite 0.726 — meaningfully lower than JBHT (~#12) or UPS (~#16) in this same batch, driven by strong Quality (0.813) and Value (0.878), but only middling Momentum (0.486). Independently verified in this dossier: the Momentum reading is very likely stale. The screen's underlying financial snapshot reconciles to GD's Q1 2026 results (see the data-quality note), and GD's stock and fundamentals both moved meaningfully in Q2 2026 (guidance raised a third time, backlog hit a record, shares rose after the July release) — data that the snapshot had not yet incorporated. This does not change the Quality/Value read, which is durable and evidenced independently here: ROE ~15–16%, ROIC ~13–14%, net debt/EBITDA <1.1x, interest coverage 12–17x — the strongest balance sheet of the three names in this batch.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

FCF conversion: very strong — H1'26 FCF/NI ≈ $3.598B/$2.285B (Q1+Q2 NI) ≈ 157%; FY2025 FCF (CFO $5.120B − capex $1.161B) = $3.959B vs NI $4.210B ≈ 94%. GAAP vs. adjusted: minimal gap — no material non-GAAP EPS adjustment was identified in the sources reviewed (unlike UPS in this batch), which is itself a quality signal, though this should be confirmed against the FY2025 10-K's own non-GAAP reconciliation note as a follow-up. Effective tax rate is a modest ~17.9% (FY2024–25 blended, per ratios.py), below the US statutory-plus-state expectation — plausibly R&D credits and export incentives (FDII) common for an aerospace/defense exporter; not flagged as aggressive, but noted for the record. Leverage: gross debt ~$9.8B, cash $3.65B, net debt/EBITDA ≈ 1.0x, interest coverage 12–17x — the strongest balance sheet of the three names in this batch, and debt is being actively reduced ($498M paid down in Q2'26 alone; long-term debt fell from ~$7.0B (Q3'25) to ~$6.3B (Q1'26) per XBRL). Working-capital / percentage-of-completion caution (per the sector playbook): this dossier did not independently verify GD's unbilled-revenue growth vs. revenue growth or cumulative CFO/EBITDA over a 3–5 year window — both are the sector's standard lie-detector for POC-accounting aggressiveness and should be run before a large position is sized; flagged as a gap, not a finding either way. M&A: none material identified in 2025–2026. Capital return: dividends $834M and buybacks $319M in H1'26 (well covered by FCF); dividend yield ~1.8%, payout ratio ~35–38% — comfortable, with room to grow, a clear contrast to UPS in this batch.

7. Valuation snapshot

NTM P/E (calendarized, per d4_live_snapshot.parquet) 18.5x; trailing P/E 21.0x (via valuation.py EV bridge: EV $97.3B on FY2025 EBITDA ~$6.3B → EV/EBITDA 15.5x, EV/EBIT 18.2x); FCF yield ~6.5%. The sector playbook's cited range for global defense primes is ~15–22x P/E with a "visibility premium" for backlog-driven revenue — GD's 18.5x NTM sits comfortably inside that band, neither obviously cheap nor stretched. Reverse-DCF (WACC 8.0%, terminal growth 3.5%): using a $5.9B normalized FCF base, the current EV implies slightly negative FCF growth over the next decade — i.e., the market's implied assumption looks conservative relative to a company that just raised guidance for the third straight quarter and is sitting on a record, growing backlog; this is the clearest quantitative support for the Value-family screen result. A probability-weighted bear/base/bull scenario (bear $15.50 EPS/16x, base $16.85/19x, bull $18.50/22x) centers on ~$324/share, close to fair value (-3.8%) — this dossier does not find GD dramatically mispriced either way; the case here rests on business quality and trend durability, not a valuation anomaly. (A separate forward-DCF run using a more aggressive 10%/5yr growth assumption produced an implausibly high per-share value and is not reported as a serious estimate — flagged here so the lead does not mistake scenario sensitivity for a price target.)

8. Bull case

  1. A verified, three-quarter pattern of guidance raises with record, growing backlog ($136.5B, +32% YoY, 1.4x book-to-bill, funded backlog $104.1B/76% of total) — this is about as close to a "show me" thesis being actually shown as this batch contains.
  2. Marine Systems — historically the segment most exposed to execution risk on multi-decade submarine programs — is currently improving, not deteriorating: margin +40bps YoY, Columbia-class labor hours earned +37% YoY, sequence-critical material deliveries +65% YoY. If this holds, it removes the single largest historical overhang on the stock.
  3. Balance sheet and capital allocation are the strongest of the three names in this batch: net debt/EBITDA ~1.0x, actively deleveraging, dividend well covered at ~35–38% payout with room to grow, no dependence on non-GAAP adjustments to tell the earnings story.

9. Bear case

  1. Multi-decade submarine programs (Columbia/Virginia-class) carry real, structural execution risk that a few good quarters does not retire — the sector playbook is explicit that these programs have historically produced multi-year margin surprises (favorable and unfavorable) via estimate-at-completion adjustments; this dossier did not independently audit GD's EAC adjustment history and recommends that as a follow-up before treating the current improvement as durable.
  2. Budget/appropriations risk is live, not hypothetical, right now: the government is funded only through a continuing resolution to 2026-12-11 (signed 2026-09-01); the FY2027 defense appropriations process is far from complete (House has passed 3 of 12 spending bills, Senate none, as of this session), and a further shutdown or a CR-driven funding gap remains a real near-term risk to contract obligations and cash timing, even though GD's multi-year backlog buffers the revenue line better than most industrials.
  3. Gulfstream (Aerospace) is a large and growing share of the growth story (+15.1% revenue in Q2'26) but is the segment most exposed to a general economic or corporate-profit downturn — business-jet demand is discretionary and cyclical in a way the defense segments are not; a re-acceleration narrative built partly on Gulfstream deliveries is not immune to a macro shock.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

These are the specific, observable, time-bound conditions that would invalidate the INCLUDE thesis above: - Marine Systems margin reverses back below ~6.5% for two consecutive quarters, or a disclosed unfavorable EAC adjustment on Columbia or Virginia-class work exceeds a low-single-digit-percent of segment revenue. - Book-to-bill falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (backlog visibility deteriorating). - FY2027 appropriations lapse into a full-year continuing resolution or shutdown that measurably delays contract funding or payment (watch specifically around the 2026-12-11 CR expiry). - Full-year guidance is cut, or fails to be raised, at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release — breaking the three-quarter raise streak. - Gulfstream order intake or deliveries decelerate for two consecutive quarters alongside broader signs of corporate-capex weakness.

Litigation: no current (2025–2026) material litigation, SEC investigation, or export-control enforcement action was found in this session's research. dossiers.GE:
GE Aerospace (GE) — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

Verdict: WATCH — thesis horizon 12–36 months if valuation resets or the growth algorithm proves out for longer than 3 years. One-sentence reason: the LEAP/CFM engine duopoly and its ~70%-of-revenue aftermarket annuity are as good a moat as this analyst has diligenced this wave, guidance has been raised or held at every checkpoint for three straight quarters, but at ~35–42x earnings the stock already prices in about 17%/yr FCF growth for a decade versus a ~13%/yr evidence-based base case, so it is a "great business, full price," not a name to add at the current price.

1. Business in plain English

GE Aerospace designs, manufactures and services jet engines for commercial aircraft (Commercial Engines & Services, "CES" — LEAP via the 50/50 CFM International joint venture with Safran, plus GEnx, GE90) and military/defense propulsion (Defense & Propulsion Technologies, "DPT" — T700, F110, Avio Aero). It makes most of its money the way razor-blade businesses do: engines are often sold near breakeven, and the real profit comes from decades of high-margin spare parts, overhaul and repair ("shop visits") on an installed base of ~50,000 commercial and ~30,000 military engines. GE Aerospace is the standalone industrial successor to the old General Electric conglomerate, following the 2023 spin-off of GE HealthCare and the April-2024 spin-off of GE Vernova; the consolidated entity still carries a legacy run-off insurance block and a Polish mortgage portfolio (Bank BPH) from the old GE Capital, which are not part of the aerospace operating business (see §6, §12 for entity-scope detail).

2. Why the model likes it / is it durable

b1 quant composite is moderate (composite 0.413, decile 5, live_rank 292) — Quality (fam_Q 0.599) and Momentum/Earnings-momentum (fam_M 0.522, fam_S 0.524) are all mid-to-upper range, but Value (fam_V 0.262) is weak (earnings yield 2.6%, FCF yield 2.5%, both raw and low) reflecting the rich multiple. The fundamental triage independently scored quality 5/5, growth 4/5 with no disqualifying red flags — "21% revenue growth on the LEAP ramp and a widening services backlog justify a 35x NTM P/E." The durability case (a duopoly moat, a multi-decade aftermarket annuity as the young LEAP fleet ages into its first shop visits) is well evidenced in the filed backlog and delivery data below and is genuinely different in kind from a cyclical growth story.

4. Guidance track record (last 3 checkpoints; FY2026 adjusted EPS)

  • 22-Jan-2026 (FY2025 results): INITIATED FY2026 guide: adjusted revenue growth "+LDD" (low double digit), operating profit $9.85–$10.25bn, adjusted EPS $7.10–$7.40, FCF $8.0–$8.4bn (>100% conversion) — vs. FY2025 actuals: adjusted revenue $42.3bn (+21%), operating profit $9.1bn, adjusted EPS $6.37 (+38%), FCF $7.7bn.
  • 21-Apr-2026 (Q1 2026 results): MAINTAINED the same guide, explicitly "holding our full-year guidance across the board and…trending toward the higher-end of the range."
  • 16-Jul-2026 (Q2 2026 results): RAISED across the board — adjusted revenue growth to "high-teens," operating profit to $10.55–$10.75bn, adjusted EPS to $7.65–$7.85, FCF to $8.9–$9.2bn. Net: initiate → maintain → raise, with no cut in the period reviewed — a clean, well-documented track record, driven by real backlog conversion (orders +17% YoY in Q2 2026; total commercial-services backlog >$210bn).

5. Moat and competition

  • Duopoly + annuity model: CFM International (GE/Safran 50-50 JV) LEAP engines and legacy CFM56 compete narrowbody-for-narrowbody essentially only against Pratt & Whitney's PW1000G geared turbofan (which has had its own well-publicized durability/inspection issues industry-wide); GE also holds GEnx/GE90 widebody positions. ~70% of GE Aerospace's revenue is services/aftermarket on an installed base that is still young relative to its service life, i.e. shop-visit revenue should keep growing for years even without a single new engine sale.
  • LEAP durability program: completed certification of the LEAP-1B durability kit (upgraded HPT blade) in Q2 2026, expected to ~2x time-on-wing, full fleet cutover from "beginning of 2027" — a real, dated engineering fix to a known durability issue, not yet fully executed.
  • Commercial momentum: Q2 2026 orders $16.5bn (+17%); total engine deliveries +31% in H1 2026 (LEAP deliveries +41%); named wins include Copa Airlines (up to 120 LEAP-1B), Turkish Aerospace (F404), Leonardo Helicopters (CT7), American Airlines (300+ LEAP-1A), United/Delta (GEnx).
  • Defense & Propulsion Technologies: smaller, lower-margin (13.8% Q2 2026 operating margin vs. CES 27.3%) but growing (orders +12% Q2 2026), with early-stage next-gen programs (XA102, GE426 for the USAF's Autonomous Collaborative Platform).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Entity scope — read carefully: GE Aerospace's consolidated balance sheet still includes a legacy run-off Insurance segment ($36.2bn of insurance/annuity benefit liabilities backed by $37.9bn of investment securities, per the 10-Q) and the Bank BPH mortgage portfolio in Poland, both explicitly called out by the company as legacy GE Capital exposures, not aerospace operating assets/liabilities. All consolidated balance-sheet figures below include these; aerospace-only (industrial) leverage is materially better than the consolidated numbers imply, but this analyst did not find a clean, separately-filed "industrial net debt" line to substitute (flagged, not asserted).
  • Consolidated balance sheet at 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q): total assets $127.67bn (down from $130.17bn at YE2025); cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash $9.35bn (down from $12.39bn); total borrowings $19.16bn (down from $20.49bn at YE2025 — GE Aerospace is net deleveraging); total shareholders' equity $17.64bn.
  • TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) GAAP profit ≈$10.37bn (derived: FY2025 $10.0bn − 1H2025 $4.63bn + 1H2026 $5.00bn); TTM FCF (non-GAAP) ≈$8.81bn (FY2025 $7.69bn − 1H2025 $3.57bn + 1H2026 $4.69bn) → FCF/TTM GAAP profit ≈85%, a high conversion rate consistent with an asset-light aftermarket model, though this mixes a non-GAAP cash-flow measure against a GAAP income measure (both are the company's own reported figures; no independent restatement attempted).
  • BETA Technologies mark-to-market: an unrealized gain of $47M (Q2 2026) and unrealized loss of $262M (six months 2026) flowed through "other income" — a real, disclosed source of non-operating earnings volatility the company itself excludes from adjusted EPS.
  • No discrete quarterly capex or SBC figures were independently re-derived from XBRL in this pass (GE does not tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment in the standard way used elsewhere); flagged rather than asserted.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (no V1 systematic valuation row exists for GE)

Inputs: EV ≈$342.3bn (market cap $339.4bn + net debt); TTM FCF ≈$6.59bn (vendor figure, reconciles to a TTM operating-cash-flow of $9.80bn that matches this analyst's independent XBRL derivation exactly); WACC 8.5% (beta 1.35); terminal growth 2.5%; 10-year horizon. Solving for the constant FCF growth rate that justifies the price: ≈17.0%/year for 10 years. - Bear (10y FCF CAGR ≈6%): the LEAP durability-kit cutover slips past 2027, a fleet-wide airworthiness directive or a durability/safety issue re-emerges (industry-wide GTF-style event), defense budgets tighten. - Base (10y FCF CAGR ≈13%): the current backlog-driven services ramp (+22–38% adjusted EPS growth over the last four quarters) decelerates over several years toward a high-single/low-teens sustainable rate as the LEAP fleet's shop-visit growth normalizes — still very good, but not indefinitely at the current pace. - Bull (10y FCF CAGR ≈20%): the "aftermarket bathtub" (young fleet aging into decades of shop visits) plus defense upside sustains near-current growth rates for far longer than a typical industrial cycle would suggest. Implied vs. base: ABOVE. ~17% priced in vs. a ~13% evidence-based base — the market is extrapolating the current exceptional multi-quarter beat-and-raise streak rather than a normalized decade-long trajectory.

8. Bull case

  1. A genuine engine duopoly with a young, growing installed base (~50,000 commercial + ~30,000 military engines) and a >$210bn services backlog — one of the highest-quality moats diligenced this wave, independent of near-term price.
  2. Guidance has been raised or held at every checkpoint for three consecutive quarters, backed by verifiable order growth (+17% to +87% YoY across the last several quarters) and delivery growth (+31% H1 2026, LEAP +41%).
  3. The LEAP-1B durability kit (certified Q2 2026, ~2x time-on-wing) directly addresses the industry's best-known engine-durability risk and should reduce shop-visit frequency risk once fully cut over from 2027.

9. Bear case

  1. The price already implies ~17%/yr sustained FCF growth for a decade at a premium 35–42x multiple — a high bar even for an exceptional aftermarket annuity business, leaving little room for a normalization of growth toward mid-cycle industrial rates.
  2. Consolidated financials still carry legacy run-off Insurance ($36.2bn liabilities) and Bank BPH Poland mortgage exposures explicitly flagged by the company as capital/liquidity risks in its own forward-looking-statement disclosure — a real, if secondary, source of tail risk not present in a "pure-play" engine maker.
  3. The durability-kit fix is not yet fully executed (full fleet cutover begins 2027); any slippage, cost overrun or a new durability/safety finding (an industry-wide risk given the PW1000G precedent) would directly hit the aftermarket thesis the valuation depends on.

10. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis-invalidation triggers (what would change this verdict)

  1. FY adjusted EPS guidance is cut in an upcoming release (breaking the initiate→maintain→raise pattern of the last three checkpoints).
  2. Total engine deliveries growth decelerates below +15% YoY for two consecutive quarters (LEAP ramp stalling).
  3. Non-GAAP operating profit margin contracts below 20% for two consecutive quarters.
  4. Total borrowings rise back above $20bn for two consecutive quarters (releveraging, reversing the current delever trend).
  5. A confirmed new LEAP/CFM durability or safety issue requiring a fleet-wide airworthiness directive beyond the already-announced HPT-blade durability kit.

  • LEAP-1B durability-kit full fleet cutover: "beginning of 2027" (company-stated timeline) — a key milestone to track.

Gen Digital Inc. (GEN) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F28, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH — not now, despite genuinely cheap headline valuation, because of a live, unresolved, potentially transformative M&A situation disclosed one day before this dossier's cutoff. Condition to revisit: GoDaddy talks are confirmed dead (revert to INCLUDE-SMALL/INCLUDE case below) or a signed agreement discloses concrete financing terms that can be underwritten. Thesis horizon if resolved favourably: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

Gen Digital sells consumer cybersecurity, identity-protection and privacy subscriptions under the Norton, Avast, LifeLock, AVG and (since fiscal 2026) MoneyLion brands — a recurring-revenue, high-margin subscription business monetised mostly through auto-renewing annual plans and OEM/retail bundling. It is the product of the 2022 NortonLifeLock/Avast merger and has spent the years since integrating and deleveraging that deal.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv: composite 0.71 (live_rank 144/503), driven by a high V-family score (FCF yield 12.0%, earnings yield 8.1%) and strong earnings momentum (SUE 0.65). Triage (Q12_triage.json) called it "a cash cow… priced for outright decline" at 7x NTM P/E / 12% FCF yield, flagging two red flags: elevated leverage from the Avast deal (3.2x net debt/EBITDA) and the historical Avast/FTC data-selling settlement (resolved). Verified: deleveraging is real and evidenced in primary filings — SEC XBRL long-term debt has fallen from $10.06bn (Sep-2022) to $8.16bn (Jul-2026), and the company states it hit its 3.0x net-leverage target a full year ahead of schedule in fiscal 2026, funded by $2.4bn of debt paydown, alongside $1.3bn of buybacks and ~$1.1bn of tuck-in M&A (primarily MoneyLion) (Gen Digital Q4 FY26 earnings materials, May-2026; Investing.com summary of the same). Revenue growth is genuinely accelerating: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 3-Jul-2026) revenue grew 11% YoY, the fastest since Gen was created, and full-year FY27 guidance was raised at that release (see §5). So the "cheap cash cow" read holds up on growth and leverage. What the triage missed entirely, because it happened after the triage ran: a preliminary ~$12bn takeover approach for GoDaddy, reported 24-Sep-2026 — see §11. This is not an artefact of the scoring model; it is a live corporate- action risk that changes the capital structure and strategic direction question entirely, and it arrived one day before this dossier's data cutoff.

Market cap $12.94bn. EV (net debt $7.62bn) ≈ $20.56bn. Trailing P/E 20.8x on GAAP EPS (elevated by the depressed post-MoneyLion margin base); non-GAAP forward multiple is the ~7x the triage cites. Reverse DCF (WACC 9.0%, terminal growth 3.0%, 10-year horizon, base FCF = TTM $1,548m, EV anchor $20.56bn): implied stage-1 FCF growth ≈ -0.4% per year for 10 years — the market is pricing Gen as a slow-decline subscription book, which contradicts the primary evidence of accelerating, guidance-raised growth (+11% Q1 FY27, FY27 guide raised to 9–11%). An evidence-based base case of +5–7%/yr FCF growth (organic mid-single-digit growth plus continued buyback-driven EPS accretion, moderated for integration costs) sits comfortably above the implied path. Implied vs base: below (cheap) — on the standalone business, before the GoDaddy situation is resolved. No V1 systematic valuation exists for this name yet.

Scenario table (non-GAAP EPS basis, consistent with how guidance and consensus price the stock; 3-year horizon, dividend yield ~2.3%/yr added to price return): | Scenario | Prob. | 3y-forward non-GAAP EPS | Exit P/E | Value/share | 3y annualised total return | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Bear | 30% | $2.60 | 8x | $20.80 | ~+1.0%/yr | | Base | 45% | $3.10 | 10x | $31.00 | ~+15.1%/yr | | Bull | 25% | $3.55 | 12x | $42.60 | ~+27.7%/yr |

None of these scenarios price in a GoDaddy transaction; see §11 for why that matters and why the verdict is WATCH, not INCLUDE, despite a favourable standalone reverse DCF.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Deleveraging is ahead of schedule and evidenced in primary filings (10.06bn→8.16bn LT debt over four years), freeing cash for buybacks. (2) Revenue growth is accelerating, not decaying, and guidance was just raised. (3) 77–81% gross margins and near-zero capex make this one of the highest-FCF-conversion names in the whole diligence set.

Bear: (1) A preliminary ~$12bn takeover approach for GoDaddy (reported 24-Sep-2026, talks at an early, non-binding stage) would need to be financed largely with equity given Gen's own ~$8bn net debt versus GoDaddy's ~$3.8bn — this is exactly the kind of "pending deal" the program's own sleeve-construction rules treat as an automatic exclusion for other names (WBD, KVUE, TECH, AES, NSC, D), and it was invisible to both the quant screen and the original triage because it broke the day before the data cutoff. (2) Operating margin has compressed roughly 8–10 points from its FY25 peak on integration and litigation costs even before any GoDaddy deal. (3) A $900m note matures Sep-2027, inside the thesis horizon, competing for capital with whatever the GoDaddy situation ultimately requires.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. A signed, binding GoDaddy (or other >$5bn) acquisition agreement is announced without disclosed financing terms that keep pro-forma net debt/EBITDA under ~3.5x within 12 months.
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x for any reason (deal-related or organic).
  3. Quarterly organic revenue growth below 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters (current: accelerating, 11% last quarter).
  4. FY27 guidance cut at any subsequent release (currently raised twice in the trailing year per the sources reviewed).
  5. Buyback program suspended or materially reduced to fund M&A — a direct signal capital allocation has shifted away from the "cash cow" thesis this dossier is built on.

Next earnings: ~5-Nov-2026 (Q2 FY27, per d4 estimate). The GoDaddy situation is the dominant near-term catalyst/risk: watch for (a) confirmation talks have ended without a deal, (b) a definitive agreement with financing terms, or (c) a formal rejection from GoDaddy's board.

dossiers.GEV:
GEV — GE Vernova Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F44, wave 2, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH — overturns triage's implicit "price is fine" read (price_vs_growth 4/5). This is a genuinely strong, accelerating business (backlog $176bn, orders +88% organically in 2Q26, guidance raised in each of the last three quarters), but the 25-Sep-2026 close prices in roughly 20%+ annualized growth for a decade — well above a defensible base case. Per the wave-2 mandate, a great business priced for more than it can deliver is WATCH, not INCLUDE. Thesis horizon: revisit if the multiple de-rates or backlog conversion confirms the 2028 outlook is on track without relying on Wind-segment improvement that the numbers don't yet show.

2. Business in plain English

GE Vernova (spun off from General Electric in 2024) makes the equipment that generates and moves electricity: gas turbines and related services (Power segment), grid/transformer/switchgear equipment increasingly sold into AI data centers (Electrification), and wind turbines (Wind, structurally loss-making). It sells to utilities, independent power producers, grid operators and, increasingly, data-center developers and their power suppliers — riding the AI-driven electricity-demand buildout.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q09) cited a $176B backlog, gas-turbine backlog growing from 100 to 116+ GW, data-center electrification orders exceeding all of 2025 in Q1'26 alone, and guidance raised each of the last two quarters, concluding the elevated 36x NTM multiple was supported. Diligence confirms every one of those facts from primary sources (2Q26 press release, filed 2026-07-22) and adds a third consecutive guidance raise (see §5) — the momentum is real and durable in the sense that it is order-book-driven, not accounting-driven, in Power and Electrification. The valuation conclusion does not survive contact with the numbers, however (see §7): the market is not pricing "strong growth," it is pricing growth at a pace GE Vernova's own long-range outlook does not project past 2028.

4. Results — last three reported quarters plus FY2025 (GAAP unless noted)

Net income margin 12.8% not separately reviewed 50.9% 5.8%

Critical GAAP-vs-adjusted flag: 1Q2026's $4,749mm GAAP net income (50.9% margin) is not organic profitability — the release states it is "inclusive of $4.5B pre-tax M&A net gains, primarily from Prolec GE" (a transformer joint-venture consolidation gain). Six-months-2026 GAAP diluted EPS was reported as $19.96, driven almost entirely by this one-off; 2Q26-alone diluted EPS was $2.47. FY2025's $4,900mm net income (12.8% margin) similarly "includes a $2.9B tax benefit due to a U.S. valuation allowance release" — also non-operating. GAAP net income and GAAP diluted EPS are not usable as run-rate figures for this company in 2025–26; adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow are the only reliable operating metrics disclosed. GE Vernova does not report an "adjusted EPS" non-GAAP metric.

5. Guidance track record — three consecutive raises

Release FY2026 revenue guide FY2026 adj. EBITDA margin FY2026 FCF guide
4Q2025 (28 Jan 2026) $44–45bn (up from $41–42bn, to include Prolec GE) 11–13% $5.0–5.5bn (up from $4.5–5.0bn)
1Q2026 (22 Apr 2026) $44.5–45.5bn (up from $44–45bn) 12–14% (up from 11–13%) $6.5–7.5bn (up from $5.0–5.5bn)
2Q2026 (22 Jul 2026) $45.5–46.5bn (up from $44.5–45.5bn) 12–14% (maintained) $11.5–12.5bn (up from $6.5–7.5bn)
Guidance has been raised, never cut, in every quarter reviewed — a genuinely strong track record. The FCF guide nearly doubled in one quarter (from $6.5–7.5bn to $11.5–12.5bn) while the revenue and margin guides moved only modestly — this is disproportionate and not explained in the press release. The likely driver (not confirmed in the exhibit reviewed) is customer milestone/progress-payment timing on the surging gas-turbine and data-center backlog, which is a working-capital tailwind that would reverse if order growth slows — flagged as a valuation-quality issue, not merely a positive.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Balance sheet: $3.72bn total debt vs $12.72bn cash and short-term investments (d4 snapshot, 2026-09-25) — net cash of roughly $9bn, minimal leverage risk. Capital returned to shareholders: $3.6bn (FY2025), $1.4bn (1Q26), a further $2.5bn (2Q26, cumulative $3.9bn YTD) — includes a $0.50/share quarterly dividend and buybacks; dividend yield is negligible (~0.2%) so this is predominantly buybacks.
  • Segment quality — Wind is a live, unreconciled red flag: FY2025 Wind segment EBITDA loss was −$598mm (full year). The 4Q2025 release guided FY2026 Wind losses to narrow to "approximately $400 million." That guidance figure was repeated unchanged in both the 1Q2026 and 2Q2026 releases even though 1H2026 Wind segment EBITDA was already −$657mm — i.e., the first six months of 2026 alone lost more than the full-year target, and the 2Q26 quarter's Wind EBITDA margin (−13.6%) was worse than the year-ago quarter's (−7.3%). This is a genuine, primary-source data conflict: either the FY2026 Wind guidance is stale/wrong, or management expects a swing to Wind profitability in 2H2026 that is not stated anywhere in the reviewed releases. This was not something triage caught (its red flag was about a forward-EPS base-year distortion, not this).
  • Segment strength: Power segment EBITDA margin 18.8% (2Q26) and Electrification 18.4% (2Q26), both expanding meaningfully y/y (+245bps and +357bps respectively on the quarter) — the parts of the business actually driving the guidance raises are executing well.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (own model; no V1 row exists for GEV)

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for GEV — v1_verdict is null. Standard capital-goods valuation (EV/EBITDA, not FCFF DCF given the WC-driven FCF noted above) at the 25-Sep-2026 close of $957.63 (market cap $255.0bn; EV ≈ $246.1bn using $3.72bn debt and $12.72bn cash, per d4 snapshot) against FY2026 guidance-midpoint adjusted EBITDA of ~$5.98bn (46bn revenue × 13% margin midpoint) implies ~41x forward EV/EBITDA. Reverse-DCF: solving for the 10-year EBITDA CAGR that justifies this EV at a 10% discount rate and a 14x exit multiple (a reasonable mid-cycle multiple for a scaled, still-growing capital-goods/grid-equipment franchise) requires ~22–23% annualized EBITDA growth for 10 straight years; even generous assumptions (16x exit multiple, 9% discount rate) still require ~20%. My own base case — GE Vernova's own 2028 outlook ($56bn revenue, 20% margin ≈ $11.2bn EBITDA, implying ~37%/yr for the next two years) decelerating over years 3–10 toward a still-strong 8–10%/yr as the AI-power capex supercycle normalizes toward broader grid/utility capex growth — blends to roughly ~14%/yr over 10 years. Implied vs base: above. The stock is priced for continued hyper-growth well beyond the company's own explicit two-year outlook; per the eligibility rule, this makes GEV ineligible for INCLUDE/INCLUDE-SMALL regardless of how good the underlying business is.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Orders +88% organically (2Q26) and backlog +$13bn sequentially for two consecutive quarters show the AI/data-center power buildout is, if anything, still accelerating, not decelerating. (2) Power segment margin expansion (18.8% and rising) shows genuine operating leverage, not just volume. (3) Net cash balance sheet plus $12bn+ of FCF guided gives enormous flexibility to fund capacity expansion (management's own 20 GW→24 GW→30 GW gas-turbine output ramp) without dilution. Bear: (1) The valuation (~41x forward EV/EBITDA, ~20%+ implied 10-year growth) leaves no room for even a modest disappointment — a single guidance miss would likely produce a large de-rating. (2) Wind segment losses are running well ahead of the company's own stated full-year guidance with no public reconciliation — either a forecasting problem or an undisclosed 2H26 assumption; either way it is evidence the guidance numbers deserve more scrutiny than the "raised every quarter" headline suggests. (3) The FY2026 FCF guide nearly doubled in one quarter on a much smaller revenue/margin guide change — consistent with a working-capital/progress-billing tailwind from backlog growth that would reverse if order intake decelerates, meaning today's FCF yield may overstate sustainable cash generation.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Quarterly order growth (y/y, organic) falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (vs +71% 1Q26, +88% 2Q26).
  2. Adjusted EBITDA margin fails to reach the 12–14% FY2026 guided range in either 3Q or 4Q2026.
  3. FY2026 Wind segment EBITDA loss is confirmed (at FY2026 results) to exceed $700 million (vs the standing ~$400mm guide), i.e., the current guidance/actuals gap is never reconciled.
  4. Free cash flow for 2H2026 comes in below $5 billion combined (i.e., the raised $11.5–12.5bn FY guide is not met), confirming the 2Q26 FCF jump was working-capital timing rather than sustainable.
  5. EV/forward-adjusted-EBITDA multiple compresses below 25x without a corresponding fundamental deterioration (a valuation-only de-rating would be the point at which this name becomes newly investable on the same fundamentals).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 results not yet dated in the filings reviewed; based on the 22 Jul / 22 Apr / 28 Jan release cadence, estimate mid-to-late October 2026 (unconfirmed — flagged as an estimate). CEO Scott Strazik's stated near-term milestones: 20 GW annual gas-turbine output run-rate by 3Q2026, "at least 125 GW" of gas equipment under contract by year-end 2026.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, restatements, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation disclosures found in the press-release exhibits reviewed. The Wind-segment guidance/actuals gap (§6) is the primary quantitative red flag from this diligence pass and was not identified by triage. Limitation: the 10-Q/10-K Legal Proceedings sections and insider Form 4 activity were not separately reviewed within this time-box — flagged as gaps.

12. Data basis, recency and disclaimer

Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 (period ended 2026-06-30), 8-K Ex-99 filed 2026-07-22; cross-checked against the 1Q2026 (filed 2026-04-22) and FY2025/4Q2025 (filed 2026-01-28) releases. Events checked to 2026-09-25. GAAP figures are labelled GAAP; adjusted/non-GAAP figures are labelled adjusted throughout; GAAP net income and EPS are flagged as unreliable run-rate indicators for this company given disclosed one-off gains. This is research, not personalized investment advice, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell.

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months

Financially the cleanest of the three names — earnings are programmatic rather than cyclically inflated, guidance has been raised four consecutive times with full transparency on the prior range, and capital (RBC 316%) is solid. Held to half weight, not full, because of a real, unresolved, business-model-specific tail risk: a 2+ year old securities class action tied to 2024 short-seller allegations about sales practices at its largest subsidiary has just reached the class-certification stage, and GL's whole model depends on recruiting and retaining the career agents those allegations targeted.

2. Business in plain English

Globe Life is a niche life and supplemental-health insurer selling simplified-issue term life, whole life, and supplemental health products to lower-middle- and middle-income U.S. households, primarily through multiple career-agency distribution channels: American Income Life (labor-union-affiliated), Liberty National, Family Heritage (payroll/worksite health), United American (Medicare supplement), and a smaller Direct-to-Consumer arm. It earns money on the underwriting margin between premium and claims/expenses on relatively small, simple policies, plus investment income on reserves — a capital-light model whose main "raw material" is a large, constantly-recruited independent/career agent force.

3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

b1-family prelim scores: Q 0.726, V 0.480, M 0.750 (12-1m return +21.8%), composite 0.734 — the lowest composite of the three, reflecting a smaller, steadier growth profile rather than a cyclical spike. This is the one name where the model's read looks reasonably durable, not an artefact: unlike TRV/ALL, d4 shows GL's FY2027 consensus EPS ($16.52) is +5.1% above FY2026 consensus ($15.71) — no forward air-pocket (ntm_flags blank, ntm_quality = "ok"). Life/health earnings emerge programmatically over the life of a policy rather than swinging on a single quarter's catastrophes, which is exactly what the data shows: net operating income per share grew in 8 of the last 9 quarters by double digits (company's own claim, corroborated by the EPS series in §4). The main caveat: even GL's own guidance implies deceleration — FY2026 guidance (now $15.55-$15.95, midpoint $15.75) is only +8.5% over FY2025's actual $14.52, versus FY2025's own +17.4% growth over FY2024 — so "durable" does not mean "re-accelerating."

Book value/share $78.18 (+18% YoY); ex-AOCI $100.04 (+11% YoY) — solid, less inflated than ALL's +49.7%.

7. Valuation snapshot

(scripts/ratios.py/scripts/valuation.py were deliberately not run: their outputs — EV/EBITDA, FCF-based DCF, generic ROCE/current-ratio — are the specific metrics the insurance sector playbook states are undefined or misleading for underwriters. The P/B-ex-AOCI-anchored-to-ROE and peer-comparison approach below is the playbook's mandated substitute.)

NTM P/E (d4) 10.25x; P/B 2.14x (1.67x ex-AOCI, the more meaningful figure per the sector playbook). Best available peers in the same live-snapshot dataset (not perfect business-model matches, but consistent methodology): AFL 1.88x P/B / 16.9% ROE / 15.4x NTM P/E; MET 2.27x / 13.1% / 9.2x; PFG 2.03x / 12.9% / 11.3x. Read: against a net-operating-ROE-ex-AOCI of ~14-16%, 1.67x tangible book and 10.25x NTM earnings look reasonable-to-slightly-cheap versus AFL's 15.4x, and the gap is plausibly explained by the litigation overhang (§9/§11) rather than a business-quality discount — i.e., this is a catalyst-dependent (litigation-resolution-dependent) value case, not an obviously mispriced one on fundamentals alone.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Four consecutive guidance raises with full transparency, broad-based growth across all five distribution channels, RBC within target — the most "boring and programmatic" of the three earnings streams, which is a genuine virtue for a diligence process that just got burned by a v3 audit citing omitted adverse facts. (2) Large, sustained buyback program (~50-60% of NI) directly compounding per-share value. (3) Valued at a discount to a reasonable life-insurer peer (AFL) despite comparable-or-better guidance execution — if the litigation resolves without a material loss, there is a re-rating case. Bear: (1) The City of Miami Matter securities class action — derived from the April 2024 Fuzzy Panda/Viceroy short-seller reports alleging fraudulent policy issuance, forged signatures, and unauthorized withdrawals at American Income Life — reached the class-certification-motion stage on 2026-05-15 and remains fully unresolved; several derivative suits are stayed pending its outcome. This is exactly the kind of adverse fact the prior (v3) process was found to have omitted. (2) The alleged misconduct centers on the agent-recruitment/sales-practice engine that is GL's entire distribution model — even absent a large monetary judgment, reputational damage to agent recruiting/retention is a plausible, harder-to-quantify risk the numbers wouldn't show until it shows up in net sales or agent-count growth. (3) Guidance growth is decelerating (FY26 guided +8.5% vs FY25's actual +17.4%) even as it beats-and-raises — the easy comps may be behind it too.

9. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis is invalidated if any of the following are observed (source: company 10-Q/8-K disclosures each quarter)

  1. FY guidance is cut (not just a smaller raise) versus the prior quarter's range — would break the multi-year beat-and-raise pattern and signal real deterioration.
  2. Consolidated Company Action Level RBC ratio falls below ~280% (below its own 300-320% target band).
  3. Adverse class-certification ruling, or a settlement/verdict in the City of Miami Matter exceeding roughly 5% of shareholders' equity (~$310M on $6.16B equity).
  4. Life or health underwriting margin growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters at any major division.
  5. Net operating ROE ex-AOCI falls below ~12% (vs. 14.3% 1H26).
  6. Disclosure of a formal DOJ/SEC enforcement action or order (an escalation from the current "no mention" status in the Q2-26 10-Q — see §11).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-21 (Q3 2026). Litigation calendar: class-certification motion in the City of Miami Matter was pending as of the Q2-26 10-Q (filed 2026-08-05) with no ruling date disclosed — a ruling, whenever it comes, is a binary-ish catalyst for the litigation overhang.

11. Red-flag scan

Per the Q2-26 10-Q (Note 5, Commitments and Contingencies): a consolidated federal securities class action (City of Miami Gen. Emp. & Sanitation Emp. Ret. Trust v. Globe Life Inc., E.D. Tex., Case No. 4:24-cv-00376) derived from the April 2024 Fuzzy Panda and Viceroy short-seller reports; Lead Plaintiffs moved for class certification 2026-05-15. dossiers.GM:
General Motors Company (GM) — Diligence Dossier

1. Verdict: INCLUDE. Thesis horizon 12–36 months. GM's underlying (adjusted-basis, automotive-net-cash) economics are priced far more cheaply than the headline GAAP numbers or the model's V1 valuation suggest; two consecutive 2026 guidance raises, shrinking EV losses and tariff relief support the case, against real cyclicality and EV-transition risk.

2. Business in plain English. GM designs, builds and sells cars, trucks and SUVs globally (Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac, Buick, and Wuling/Baojun in China through a JV), and separately runs GM Financial, a captcaptive finance arm that funds dealer and customer loans/leases. It makes most of its profit from full-size trucks and SUVs in North America; it is also investing in EVs and software-defined vehicles while winding down the loss-making Cruise robotaxi business.

3. Why the model likes it. b1_live_scores.csv shows GM ranks well on Value (pct_ep 0.97, pct_fcfp 0.99 — 97th/99th percentile earnings and FCF yield) and moderately on Quality (gp/assets, ROE), with a composite live_rank of 128/1172 and price_vs_growth triage score of 5/5. This is durable operating cash generation (TTM OCF $23.2bn per 10-K/10-Q, FCF ~$14.4bn), not an accounting artefact — but the reported GAAP earnings used in several of these ratios are themselves distorted by 2025–26 one-off charges (see §7), so the "cheapness" is real but understated rather than overstated.

EPS / $9.5–11.5bn adj. auto FCF. 6. Earnings quality & balance sheet. - FCF conversion: TTM OCF $23.2bn, capex $8.8bn → FCF ~$14.4bn vs GAAP NI $1.95bn — ratio is not meaningful because NI is itself charge-depressed; against adjusted EBIT ($14.4bn TTM) FCF conversion is close to 1x, healthy for an automaker. - GAAP vs adjusted gap: driven almost entirely by EV strategic-realignment and China-restructuring charges (Q1'26 $1.077bn, Q2'26 $2.279bn, Q4'25 $7.2bn) — disclosed, one-time in nature, and shrinking sequentially. - Balance sheet nuance (important): GM's consolidated net debt (~$104bn per Yahoo/D4) is dominated by GM Financial's captive-finance debt ($111.7bn total GM Financial short+long-term debt at Q2 2026), which funds customer loan/lease receivables and is not operating leverage. That is far more consistent with the triage view ("5.6x NTM P/E … look too cheap") than with V1's "excessive" tag. valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent = false. Against 3 rough peers (Ford ~6.6x NTM P/E per V1 peer set, Tesla far higher on a different growth basis), GM screens cheap on both GAAP and adjusted bases; Street 12-month target range $75–$132 (mean ~$104) brackets the $82.63 close and implies further upside on consensus.

8. Bull case / Bear case. - Bull: (1) tariff relief (Supreme Court ruling) plus further guidance raises compound — three raises already in 2026; (2) EV segment losses keep shrinking toward breakeven, removing the biggest GAAP-vs-adjusted drag; (3) $6bn buyback authorization (only partly used) plus a net-cash automotive balance sheet supports continued EPS-accretive repurchases and dividend growth. - Bear: (1) North American truck/SUV profit pool (GM's main profit source) is cyclically exposed — a US auto-demand downturn would hit adjusted EBIT hard given operating leverage; (2) China JV remains a drag (restructuring charges recurring) and a full exit/impairment is not off the table; (3) EV strategy could require further capacity write-downs if policy support (consumer incentives) does not return, repeating 2025's $7.2bn charge pattern.

9. Key risks & kill criteria. 1. Adjusted EBIT-adjusted guidance cut (vs the current $14.0–16.0bn FY26 range) at any of the next two quarterly releases. 2. Automotive segment swings from net-cash to net-debt positive (i.e., Automotive debt exceeds Automotive cash+securities) for two consecutive quarters. 3. Gross tariff-cost estimate re-raised above the current $2.5–3.5bn 2026 range. 4. Two consecutive quarters of GAAP-to-adjusted EBIT gap driven by new (not previously disclosed) restructuring/impairment charges exceeding $1bn/quarter. 5. China equity income (currently modestly positive, $83M in Q2 2026) turns negative for two consecutive quarters.

10. Catalysts & calendar. Next earnings: 2026-10-20 (Q3 2026, confirmed via GM IR press release). GM Financial releases Q3 2026 results separately around the same week. No investor day or lock-up events identified in the window.

11. Red-flag scan. Cruise robotaxi: GM ended public robotaxi operations and folded Cruise in-house in Dec 2024 (after >$10bn cumulative spend), with further ~1,000 job cuts in Feb 2025 — a de-risking event now largely behind the company, not a live red flag, but evidence of past capital-allocation misses in "growth" bets. No auditor change, restatement, going-concern language, SEC/DOJ investigation, or short-seller report identified in this review window. Insider Form-4 pattern not reviewed at standard depth (flagged as a data gap). EV-realignment and China-restructuring charges are disclosed, recurring-but-shrinking, and reconciled above — not concealed.

dossiers.GOOGL:
GOOGL — Alphabet Inc. (Class A)

1. Verdict

WATCH. Horizon 12–36 months. Google Cloud's growth is the single most impressive number in this whole batch (82% YoY), and the "cheap" trailing P/E (17.3x) is real but partly a GAAP artefact of one-off investment gains. On a 10-year reverse DCF, the $343.92 close requires a constant ~16.6% revenue CAGR — well above an evidence-based base case of ~11.3% — and the company just raised $70bn of new equity and debt to fund capex while an unresolved DOJ appeal (seeking Chrome divestiture) hangs over the core Search business.

2. Business in plain English

Alphabet mainly sells advertising attached to Google Search, YouTube and its ad network (still the majority of revenue and nearly all of its profit), plus a fast-growing Google Cloud business (infrastructure, data/AI platform services, and Workspace) sold to enterprises, and "Other Bets" (Waymo etc.), which lose money. It makes money by auctioning ad placements against user intent/attention and, increasingly, by renting AI compute and selling Gemini-based enterprise software.

3. Why the model likes it — durability check

b1 composite 0.820 — the highest of the four (decile 9, quintile 5, live_rank 89, closest to the quant top-30 of this group). Driven by very strong Momentum (fam_M 0.915) and Earnings momentum (fam_S 0.969) — both are trailing, backward-looking factors reflecting the stock's huge run and beat streak (8/8 EPS beats, avg surprise +50%), not necessarily forward durability. Quality (fam_Q 0.448) is middling and Value (fam_V 0.181) is the weakest of any family score shown here — i.e., on the model's own percentile-ranked earnings-yield/FCF-yield/EBIT-EV/book-price basis, Alphabet screens as expensive, not cheap, despite the low headline trailing P/E. This is the key "artefact" flag: trailing EPS ($19.93) is inflated by non-operating equity/investment gains (Alphabet reported a $99bn paper gain in Q2 2026 alone from its investment portfolio), which mechanically depresses the trailing P/E without reflecting recurring earnings power. The momentum/earnings-momentum drivers are real but not necessarily durable at this magnitude for a decade.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly highlights, $bn GAAP unless noted)

Quarter Total revenue YoY Google Cloud revenue Cloud YoY Op. margin (co.)
Q4 2025 — — — 48% —
Q1 2026 — — $20.0 63% —
Q2 2026 $119.8 +24% $24.8 +82% 34% (+2pp YoY)

Cloud operating income reached $8.8bn in Q2 2026 (from $2.8bn a year earlier) — cloud margin expanded from roughly 20% to ~35% in one year, a genuine profitability inflection, not just a top-line story. Remaining performance obligations (RPO): $467.6bn as of Mar-2026, of which $462.3bn is Google Cloud; cloud backlog reported at $514bn by Q2 2026, up >$50bn sequentially, with just over half expected to convert to revenue within 24 months [Alphabet Q1/Q2 2026 10-Qs and press releases; MirrorReview]. TTM revenue (d4, through Q2 2026): $445.9bn. NTM consensus EPS $16.44 (d4); trailing EPS $19.93 (includes the equity-gain distortion above).

5. Guidance track record

FY2026 capex guidance was raised twice: from $180–190bn to $195–205bn at the Q2 2026 call, following an earlier raise from original guidance — each raise driven by AI infrastructure demand exceeding the prior plan, not by a miss. This is guidance being raised on capex, not necessarily on cloud revenue growth, which is a distinction worth holding onto: the company is confident enough in demand to keep re-raising spend, which is bullish for revenue but a genuine burden on near-term free cash flow (see §6).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • H1 2026 capex: $80.6bn, more than double H1 2025's $39.6bn. Depreciation is rising fast (R&D and "Other Cost of Revenues" both cited depreciation as a primary driver of their increases) [Alphabet Q1 2026 10-Q/press release].
  • Operating cash flow adjusted for SBC climbed 35.2% YoY to a record $148bn TTM — the underlying cash-generative core (mostly Search/YouTube) remains very strong even as Cloud consumes capital.
  • Financing shift, not just self-funded growth: in June 2026 Alphabet raised $49.6bn of new equity (Class A/C common plus mandatory convertible preferred) and $20.3bn of net proceeds from senior unsecured notes — its first meaningful external capital raise in years, and share count rose this quarter rather than falling, ending what one tracker called "the buyback era" for now [Beancount.io, MarketScreener, 2026-07]. This directly weakens the buyback-driven EPS tailwind embedded in consensus models.
  • d4 snapshot: total debt $120.8bn, total cash $242.5bn (still net-cash), EBITDA $173.2bn, FCF (Yahoo definition) $22.7bn TTM — comfortably solvent, but FCF is being compressed by capex even before the July equity/debt raise is reflected.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (no V1 row exists for this ticker; valuation performed directly here)

10-year reverse DCF: using a 12% discount rate, 36% terminal operating margin (vs. today's 34% and rising), 18% tax, ~12.23bn diluted shares (implied from market cap/price) and a 21x terminal P/E (in line with Alphabet's own recent 5-year average forward multiple), the $343.92 close requires a constant 10-year revenue CAGR of ~16.6% to be justified.

My base case: Cloud decelerating from 82% today to the 20s% by year 3 (the segment is compounding off an increasingly large base — $514bn backlog already implies multi-year visibility, but 80%+ growth cannot persist for a decade against a $100bn+ annualized cloud business) blended with mature, single-digit-to-low-teens Search/YouTube growth. Explicit path (20%/17%/14%/12%/11%/10%/9%/8%/7%/6% company-wide) gives a 10-year compound-equivalent of ~11.3% and a base-case fair value of ~$220 — ~56% below the current $343.92, the largest gap of the four names reviewed. implied_vs_base: above.

The base case barely breaks even over 3 years — the price already embeds most of the next few years of even a genuinely strong outcome. The evidence supports the "Azure/cloud is real" thesis more for Google Cloud's margin inflection and Gemini token growth (22bn tokens/minute, up from 16bn a quarter earlier) than it does for the stock being cheap at $344.

8. Bull case

  1. Google Cloud's operating-margin inflection (20%→35% cloud margin YoY) is arguably the single best evidence in this whole batch that "AI infrastructure is becoming profitable," not just growing — a scale argument, not a hope.
  2. $514bn backlog with >50% converting inside 24 months gives real multi-year revenue visibility, independent of new bookings.
  3. Gemini app has 950m MAU and Alphabet can monetize AI at multiple points in the stack (infra, Vertex, Gemini Enterprise, Workspace) — more monetization surface area than a single-product competitor.

Bear case

  1. Trailing "cheap" valuation is partly a GAAP artefact of one-off equity/investment gains; on the model's own value-factor percentile (fam_V 0.18) Alphabet screens as expensive, not cheap.
  2. The June 2026 equity+debt raise ($70bn combined) signals internally that even Alphabet's enormous free cash flow could not fully fund the capex plan without external capital — a genuine, dated data point on capex burden, not speculation.
  3. DOJ/state AGs cross-appealed the December 2025 search-remedies final judgment, specifically pressing for Chrome divestiture and termination of the Apple default-search agreement — remedies the district court declined to order but that remain live on appeal, likely extending into 2027. This is unresolved binary risk to Search's distribution economics, not priced to zero.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (thesis-invalidation triggers — signposts to watch)

  1. Google Cloud revenue growth decelerates below 40% YoY for two consecutive quarters (a signal the 82% print was a peak, not a new trend).
  2. Cloud operating margin fails to hold above 30% for two consecutive quarters (would undermine the profitability-inflection thesis).
  3. D.C. Circuit sets a briefing schedule that puts Chrome divestiture or Apple-agreement termination back in play as a live remedy (currently not yet scheduled as of this cutoff).
  4. FY2026 capex guidance is raised a third time beyond $205bn without a corresponding upward revision to Cloud revenue guidance (would indicate capex is running ahead of demand, not behind it).
  5. Full-year buybacks fall to zero / net share count rises for two consecutive quarters (confirms the "end of buyback era" is structural, not one quarter).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-28 (Q3 2026). EU DMA self-preferencing/Google Play steering non-compliance investigations ongoing (opened under the DMA, no fine date set at this cutoff). DOJ/state AG appeal of the search-remedies final judgment: briefing schedule not yet set as of Sep-2026, expected to extend into 2027.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, restatements or going-concern language identified. The $99bn Q2 2026 "paper gain" reported alongside earnings is a real disclosed item, not a red flag by itself, but it materially distorts trailing GAAP EPS/P/E and must not be used uncorrected in any headline valuation comparison (flagged explicitly in §3 and §7). Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F23 | As of: 2026-09-25 close ($935.45) | Depth: Standard

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Named reservation: the price requires the current capital-markets upcycle (record trading/IB/AWM revenues) to prove durable near a ~19–20% through-cycle ROE, not merely a cyclical peak; GBM (trading + banking) is still >75% of firm net revenues, CET1 buffer has fallen two quarters running, and a live ~$1bn Malaysia arbitration is unresolved.

2. Business in plain English

Goldman Sachs is a global investment bank and asset manager: it advises on M&A and raises capital for companies (Investment Banking), trades stocks/bonds/currencies/commodities and finances clients' positions (Global Banking & Markets), and manages money for institutions and wealthy individuals (Asset & Wealth Management, $4.04tn of assets under supervision). It has been steadily unwinding its lower-return consumer lending push (Marcus, the Apple Card partnership) to refocus capital on these higher-return, less capital-intensive franchises.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q05, sourced to data/triage_cards.csv) flagged "42.5% revenue growth from a strong trading/banking cycle, 16.9% ROE, at just 12.9x forward." Verified against the 2Q26 earnings release (Exhibit 99.2, filed 2026-07-14): 2Q26 net revenues $20,338M (+39% YoY, record), annualised ROE 23.5% (2Q26) — already above the 16.9% triage used, because ROE has accelerated every quarter for a year per the four quarterly earnings releases cited in §12: 14.2% (3Q25) → 16.0% (4Q25) → 19.8% (1Q26) → 23.5% (2Q26). Part of this is durable (management states AWM/alternatives mix-shift and the Apple Card exit lifted returns ~500bps since its last Investor Day) and part is cyclical (record Equities intermediation/financing, record Debt underwriting, #1 in announced/completed M&A — all classic late-cycle capital-markets strength that mean-reverts). The model's "growth" score is real but its persistence at the current rate is not something the filings let me confirm.

In August 2025 Malaysia demanded a further ~$1bn payment; GS disputes this (believes recoveries already exceed $1.4bn) and the matter is in ongoing arbitration (initiated by GS, October 2023) with no resolution date. A related 2018 securities class action (SDNY) also continues (third amended complaint, Sept 2025 ruling let claims proceed against the firm). The criminal DPA with the DOJ was dismissed in May 2024 per its terms; the QPAM exemption was extended through 2031 (June 2026) — the criminal/regulatory tail is closed, the civil arbitration and class action are not.

Bull: (1) IB fee backlog rose QoQ into 3Q26 even as debt-underwriting backlog fell — advisory strength looks self-sustaining; (2) AWM alternatives platform hit a record $59bn quarterly fundraising, a durable, less-cyclical fee stream; (3) capital return (dividend +25% YoY, $4bn/quarter buybacks) directly supports per-share value even if trading normalizes.   2. GBM (Global Banking & Markets) net revenues down >15% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  3. Annualised ROE below 12% for two consecutive quarters.

No going-concern language, no material weakness, no restatement in the reviewed 10-Q/10-K. Open items: 1MDB civil arbitration (~$1bn) and securities class action (both described above); Apple Card exit now substantially executed (transition agreement signed, portfolio in held-for-sale) — a resolved, not open, overhang. Verdict: WATCH — thesis horizon 12–36 months if valuation resets or growth outperforms base case for longer than 3 years. One-sentence reason: a best-in-class MRO distributor (46% ROE, three straight quarterly guidance raises, a Q3-2025 profit dip that was a clean one-off UK-exit charge rather than an operating problem) is nonetheless priced at ~25–27x forward adjusted EPS for ~13%/yr of implied 10-year FCF growth versus a ~10%/yr evidence-based base case — a smaller valuation gap than the other two names in this batch, but still "above," not "at or below," base.

1. Business in plain English

Grainger distributes maintenance, repair and operating (MRO) supplies — safety equipment, tools, fasteners, motors, cleaning supplies — to businesses and institutions across North America and, through its majority-owned Japanese subsidiary MonotaRO and its Zoro e-commerce brands, in Japan/Europe/North America respectively. It runs two segments: High-Touch Solutions – N.A. (large-account, high-service relationships, ~85% of sales) and Endless Assortment (Zoro, MonotaRO — a long-tail, e-commerce marketplace model). Hasbro, Inc. (NASDAQ: HAS) — Diligence Dossier

Agent f10 | As of 2026-09-25 close ($88.09) | Most recent period incorporated: Q2 FY2026 (period ended 2026-06-28), 10-Q filed 2026-07-30; checked for events to 2026-09-25.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon 18–36 months. Hasbro has become a Magic: The Gathering / Wizards of the Coast (WotC) company with a legacy toy business attached, not the reverse. WotC is growing double-digit-to-high-20s%, guidance has been raised or held in three of the last four releases (including through an active cyberattack), and the stock trades below the Street's own 12-month low target. Sized full-weight, but with explicit awareness that Consumer Products (toys) is loss-making at the operating line and carries real, tariff-driven impairment history.

2. Business

Hasbro is a "games, IP and toy" company reporting three segments: Wizards of the Coast & Digital Gaming (Magic: The Gathering tabletop + MTG Arena/MTGO digital, Dungeons & Dragons, digital licensing) — now the profit engine; Consumer Products (Nerf, Transformers, Play-Doh, Monopoly, Peppa Pig — physical toys sold through mass retail, largely China-sourced); and Entertainment (film/TV licensing and location-based, shrunk after the 2023 eOne Film/TV divestiture). Routing note: GICS/Yahoo file Hasbro under "Leisure" → fmcg-consumer.md, appropriate for Consumer Products, but the dominant profit segment (WotC) is a hybrid of branded tabletop IP and a growing subscription/digital card-game business (Arena) that behaves more like it-saas.md/telecom-media.md (bookings, digital mix) — explicitly flagged as a multi-segment company where the profit-driving segment does not cleanly fit one playbook; Consumer Products and Entertainment are read through fmcg-consumer.md and telecom-media.md respectively as secondary lenses.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 composite 92.6th percentile (live_rank 37). fam_V 79th pct (cheap) is durable — HAS trades near the cheapest NTM multiple in over a decade. fam_Q (72nd pct) is partly an artefact: trailing ROE/quality inputs are distorted by the FY25 GAAP net loss (see §6), which mechanically shrinks the book-value denominator and can flatter ROE-based quality metrics — treat the Quality score with caution. fam_M (momentum, 15.9th pct) and fam_S (earnings-momentum/SUE, 10.8th pct) are both weak, likely because the lumpy GAAP swings from the 2025 impairment corrupt trailing return/surprise measures — a genuine base-rate value+improving-fundamentals story that the momentum/SUE factors cannot currently see through the accounting noise.

Read-through: raise → new-year initial guide (beat) → held through an active cyberattack → raise again, explicitly WotC/Magic-driven. A materially more durable guidance track than SWK's.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • The FY25 GAAP loss is real and tariff-linked, not accounting noise: a $1,021.9m non-cash goodwill impairment in Consumer Products in Q2 FY25 was recorded "following completion of an interim quantitative assessment of goodwill triggered by the implementation of tariffs" — direct primary-source confirmation that tariffs did lasting, balance-sheet-level damage to the toy business, not just a margin headwind.
  • Consumer Products is structurally weak even in a good quarter: Q2 FY26 segment operating loss of $15m (adjusted -$8m), "reflects incremental tariff expense, entertainment-related mix shifts, and normal seasonality." Q3 FY25 CP adjusted operating profit was down -32% YoY "primarily driven by tariff expense."
  • A second impairment recurred in Q2 FY26: $56m against the "refocused Digital Games portfolio for 2028 and beyond" (video-game unit) — inside the otherwise-strong WotC segment, showing the digital-gaming diversification bet has had its own stumbles.

Peer-set caution: b1/V1's GICS sub-industry ("Leisure Products") peer bucket contains only HAS itself (peer_n=1) — the quant valuation screen's "vs. peers" read is not meaningful; the real-world comparable (Mattel, MAT) sits in a different sub-industry code and was not pulled. Benchmarking here rests on HAS's own history. FCF yield 5.5%; dividend yield 3.23%. WACC 7.77% (beta 0.90). Reverse DCF implied 10y growth -3.7% vs. consensus FY1 +6.8% and delivered 10y CAGR +0.7% — the market is pricing continued mild decline even as the company guides mid-to-high-single-digit growth and consensus agrees with the company, not the price — a real tension. Street target range $90–120 (mean $109.5, "strong buy," 14 analysts) — current price ($88.09) sits below the Street's own 12-month low target ($90), flagged by V1 as "base 3y value below Street 12m low target." Independent re-run of scripts/valuation.py reproduces V1's EV bridge exactly (EV $15,263.4m) and gives an FCF-anchored reverse-DCF implied growth of -3.8%/yr, consistent with V1's -3.7%.

8. Bull case

  1. WotC/Magic is a structurally higher-margin, faster-growing business than the legacy toy company the market may still be pricing: first-ever $500m Magic quarter (Q2 FY26), +27% segment revenue, high-40s/50%+ segment operating margins, "line of sight to continued growth in 2027" (CEO).
  2. Guidance raised or held in three of the last four releases, including through an active, costly cyberattack — genuine execution credibility.
  3. Trades below the Street's own 12-month low target and near the cheapest NTM multiple in company history.

9. Bear case

  1. Consumer Products (traditional toys) is shrinking, operating-loss-making in Q2 FY26, structurally exposed to China-sourcing tariffs, and already took a $1.02bn goodwill write-down in 2025 — a large share of revenue sits in secular/tariff-driven decline.
  2. The network-intrusion incident is open-ended: total cost and insurance-recovery timing are both unknown, and management explicitly warns of "additional costs… in future periods."
  3. Profit growth is concentrated in a single IP (Magic: The Gathering); a misstep in release cadence, secondary-market/collector dynamics, or competitive TCGs would hit consolidated results disproportionately, and the Digital Games impairment shows the diversification hedge has its own execution risk.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. WotC/Digital Gaming revenue growth decelerates below ~10% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Consumer Products operating margin fails to turn positive in the seasonally strong Q4.
  3. Cumulative unauthorized-access costs or any disclosed regulatory/privacy penalty exceeds ~$50m.
  4. FY guidance is cut (breaking the current positive streak).
  5. Any goodwill/intangible impairment inside WotC itself (as opposed to CP or Digital Games) — would signal the core thesis is broken.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings ~2026-10-22 (Q3 FY26, per D4 snapshot). Watch for further quantification of cyberattack costs/insurance recovery and any Magic 2027 release-slate commentary flagged by management.

12. Red-flag scan

Two impairments in the last five quarters (CP goodwill $1,021.9m Q2 FY25; Digital Games $56m Q2 FY26) — a real, disclosed pattern rather than a concealment issue. Ongoing, not-fully-quantified cybersecurity incident (Item 8.01 8-K, 2026-04-01) is the single largest open item. No auditor change, restatement or going-concern language identified in the documents reviewed. Insider Form 4 pattern and litigation docket not reviewed in this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as open, not asserted clean.

dossiers.HBAN:
HBAN — Huntington Bancshares Incorporated — Diligence Dossier (Agent F44, wave 2, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE — evidence-based valuation, credit quality and execution (two completed integrations, systems conversion done) support full weight; the market has not yet re-rated the stock for the accretion already delivered. Thesis horizon: 12–24 months.

2. Business in plain English

Huntington is a Columbus, Ohio-based super-regional bank that closed two acquisitions within weeks of each other in early 2026 — Veritex Holdings (Texas, systems converted mid-January 2026) and Cadence Bank (Texas/South, closed 1 Feb 2026, systems converted mid-June 2026) — to build a Texas/South franchise on top of its legacy Midwest retail and commercial-banking base. It earns money on the spread between what it pays depositors and what it charges borrowers (commercial, consumer, auto, mortgage), plus fee income from wealth management, capital markets and payments.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q06) flagged +36% forward EPS growth, +48% revenue growth (both mechanically driven by the acquisitions, like FITB) and a 9.2x NTM P/E, noting "flat momentum despite good news." That last observation holds up under diligence: both deals are fully closed and both systems conversions are complete (Veritex Jan-26, Cadence mid-June-26) — Huntington is further through integration than FITB (whose Comerica conversion was still pending as of the Q2 2026 release) — yet HBAN's NTM multiple is cheaper than FITB's. The durable part of the story: net interest margin has expanded every quarter shown (3.11%→3.24%/3.21%(seq. dip then recovery)→sequential improvement), tangible book value per share has grown for four straight quarters ($9.13→$9.55/$9.89 seasonal dip→$9.65), and the bank resumed buybacks ($159mm in Q2 2026, $309mm YTD, ~19mm shares) while FITB has not — a tangible signal of confidence in the combined balance sheet.

4. Results — last five reported quarters (GAAP)

5. Guidance track record

Like FITB, Huntington's press releases carry no quantified full-year guidance — only qualitative commentary from the CEO. That commentary has been consistently constructive: Q1 2026 ("strong start to 2026... excellent credit performance"), Q2 2026 ("by the fourth quarter, the full earnings power of these partnerships will be clearly evident... confident in our outlook... positioned to achieve our financial targets"). No cut or walk-back identified in the reviewed window. As with FITB, the absence of a quantified target (e.g., a specific cost-synergy dollar figure or an ROTCE target with a date) limits how precisely "guidance raised/maintained/cut" can be assessed — flagged as a confidence limiter, not resolved.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • GAAP vs adjusted: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS ($0.39) exceeds GAAP ($0.33) by $0.06, driven by acquisition-related Notable Items ($152mm pre-tax) — a real, disclosed, merger-specific gap, not a recurring add-back pattern. Adjusted ROTCE 17.5% vs GAAP 15.1%.
  • Capital: CET1 10.0% (Q2 2026) vs 10.2% (Q1 2026) — modest decline, but HBAN resumed and continued buybacks through the same period ($159mm in Q2 2026), which FITB has not done — a real difference in disclosed management confidence. Adjusted CET1 (incl. AOCI ex cash-flow hedges) 9.0%, down from 9.2%.
  • Credit: allowance for credit losses $3.4bn / 1.78% of loans, essentially flat q/q; net charge-offs 0.25% (Q2 2026), among the better levels shown, but nonperforming-asset ratio has risen for two straight quarters (0.72%→0.85%) even as charge-offs stayed low — the same "NPA drift while NCOs look fine" pattern flagged at FITB, and worth cross-checking against both banks' Texas commercial real estate exposure given both just added large Texas books.
  • Funding: average deposits +9% q/q, +37% y/y (acquisition effect); average loans +9% q/q, +42% y/y, with commercial loans growing fastest (+59% y/y) — consistent with two commercially-oriented acquisitions.
  • Share count & capital returns: buybacks resumed at scale (~19mm shares YTD) even while integrating two deals — this is a positive signal not present at FITB, though it also means less capital cushion if credit deteriorates.

7. Valuation

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for HBAN — v1_verdict is null in the summary JSON. Using the same P/TBV excess-return framework as FITB (appropriate for a bank; FCFF DCF is not): at the 25-Sep-2026 close of $15.64 and TBVPS of $9.65, HBAN trades at 1.62x tangible book — materially cheaper than FITB's 2.25x despite comparable or better underlying returns. Solving (ROE−g)/(COE−g) = 1.62 with a long-run adjusted ROTCE assumption of ~16% (between the Q2 2026 adjusted 17.5% and a haircut for integration risk) and a 10% cost of equity implies the market is pricing in only ~0–1% perpetual growth — essentially a no-growth, "prove it" valuation. My own base case (mid-single-digit organic growth once Cadence synergies are fully realized by Q4 2026, per management's own commentary, plus a resumed buyback compounding TBVPS) is well above zero. Implied vs base: below — this is the strongest evidence-based reason for the INCLUDE verdict: the market is pricing HBAN as if the two 2026 acquisitions add nothing, while the primary-source numbers (NIM expansion, buybacks resumed, systems conversions both complete) say otherwise.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Both acquisitions are fully integrated (systems converted) months ahead of FITB's still-pending Comerica conversion — Huntington should show clean, comparable quarters sooner. (2) Management's own language ("by the fourth quarter, the full earnings power... will be clearly evident") sets a testable, near-term catalyst. (3) At 1.62x TBV for a ~15–17% ROTCE franchise that has already resumed buybacks, the valuation gap to FITB (2.25x TBV) is hard to justify once Q4 2026 results are clean. Bear: (1) NPA ratio rising two quarters running (0.72%→0.85%) while the bank just added two sizable, unseasoned (from HBAN's perspective) loan books — if this is nascent Texas CRE or C&I stress rather than noise, credit cost could surprise higher just as buybacks are consuming capital. (2) CET1 at 10.0% (adjusted 9.0%) with continued buybacks leaves less room to absorb a credit shock than FITB's more conservative capital stance. (3) "Flat momentum despite good news" (triage's own observation) could mean the market has already seen something in Huntington's Texas book that these two quarters of data don't yet show.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Nonperforming-asset ratio rises above 1.00% (vs 0.85% at Q2 2026) for two consecutive quarters.
  2. CET1 ratio falls below 9.5% (reported) without a disclosed pause in buybacks.
  3. Adjusted ROTCE fails to reach 17% by Q4 2026 (management's own implied bar — "full earnings power... clearly evident" by Q4).
  4. Net charge-off ratio rises above 0.45% for two consecutive quarters (vs 0.25% at Q2 2026).
  5. Efficiency ratio fails to improve below 58% by Q1 2027 (vs 61.5% at Q2 2026, post both systems conversions).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 results not yet dated in the filings reviewed; based on the 23 Jul / 23 Apr / 22 Jan release cadence, estimate mid-to-late October 2026 (unconfirmed — flagged as an estimate). Management's own Q4 2026 "full earnings power" comment is the key near-term test.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, restatements, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation disclosures found in the exhibits reviewed. Limitation: Part II Item 1 (Legal Proceedings) of the 10-Q and the 10-K's risk-factor diff were not separately read within this time-box, nor was insider Form 4 activity — flagged as gaps, not a clean bill of health. The rising NPA ratio (§6) is the one quantitative flag from the reviewed documents themselves.
