Correction (26 Sep 2026) — DA7 fact-check, both findings CONFIRMED against the primary filing

Source for both items: RJF 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, SEC EDGAR accession 0000720005-26-000070 (rjf-20260630.htm), retrieved and read in full this pass.

(1) §6 "Raymond James Bank capital" and kill criterion 3 were RJF-consolidated ratios, mislabelled as the bank subsidiary's own. The MD&A states verbatim: "As of June 30, 2026, our tier 1 leverage ratio was 11.7% and total capital ratio was 22.5%, both well above regulatory capital requirements" — this is RJF-consolidated, and is what §6 originally reported as "Raymond James Bank." The Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements (Regulatory Capital note, "Raymond James Bank" row) instead give the bank's own, standalone ratios: | Raymond James Bank (standalone) | Required | Well-capitalized | Jun 30, 2026 | Sep 30, 2025 | |---|---|---|---|---| | Tier 1 leverage | 4.0% | 5.0% | 8.0% ($3,612M) | 8.0% ($3,434M) | | Tier 1 capital | 8.5% | 8.0% | 15.1% ($3,612M) | 13.9% ($3,434M) | | CET1 capital | 7.0% | 6.5% | 15.1% ($3,612M) | 13.9% ($3,434M) | | Total capital | 10.5% | 10.0% | 16.4% ($3,911M) | 15.2% ($3,743M) | DA7's read is confirmed exactly. §6's "total capital ~22.5–24.3%, Tier 1 leverage ~11.7–12.7%" is refuted as a description of the bank; it is the RJF holding-company figure. The bank-standalone total capital ratio is 16.4% at 2026-06-30, having been 15.2% at 2025-09-30 — only ~20bp above the 15% kill-criterion threshold nine months earlier, and currently ~140bp above it. This is materially closer to firing than §6/§9 originally implied, even though the trend over the last three quarters has been improving, not deteriorating. Kill criterion 3 is restated: "Raymond James Bank's standalone total capital ratio (per the 10-Q Regulatory Capital note, not the RJF-consolidated ratio) falls below 15%" — currently 16.4% (2026-06-30 10-Q), up from 15.2% (2025-09-30); the ratio has been within ~20bp of this threshold within the last year and should be tracked on the bank-standalone figure going forward, not the consolidated one.

(2) §6 "parent-level debt... only $0.7–0.95B" omitted senior notes payable and understated total parent-level debt by ~$3.5B. The consolidated balance sheet (2026-06-30) shows, as separate liability line items: "Other borrowings $950M" (this is the figure my original XBRL pull captured, tag DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount) and, separately, "Senior notes payable $3,522M" (2025-09-30: $950M→$700M other borrowings and $3,520M senior notes payable). Total parent-level debt is therefore ≈$4.472B at 2026-06-30, not $0.7–0.95B. DA7's figure of "~$4.47bn total" is confirmed exactly. The weighted-average rate on senior notes payable was disclosed at 4.91% in the interest-expense table. Against $12.7B of equity this is ~35% debt/equity at the parent level — a real, moderate leverage position, not the near-zero-debt profile originally described; still not high by diversified-financial-holdco standards, and covered by $2.5B of disclosed RJF corporate cash, but §6/§8 overstated how "conservative" the funding structure is.

Net effect on verdict, implied-vs-base and scenarios: the valuation and reverse-DCF work (§7) rested on earnings multiples and guidance-delivery consistency, not on the (incorrect) capital-structure claims, so verdict remains INCLUDE, implied_vs_base remains "below," and scenario_returns_3y are unchanged. The correction does, however, remove one leg of the original bull case (§8, bull point 2, "parent debt is under $1B") — that point should be read as retracted — and tightens the genuine distance-to-kill-criterion on bank capital adequacy, which is now flagged as a closer-to-firing metric than previously stated, not a comfortable buffer.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE (full weight). Thesis horizon 24–36 months (longer than the other two names in this batch — this is the highest-consistency compounder of the three, not a turnaround or momentum trade). Four consecutive quarters of raised guidance, broad-based double-digit growth (every region, DTC and wholesale both accelerating), the highest analyst-conviction ratios of the three names reviewed (89.5% buy share), and no red flags of any kind identified. Ralph Lauren designs, markets and distributes premium/luxury apparel, footwear, accessories, home goods and fragrances under the Ralph Lauren, Polo, Double RL, Lauren and Chaps brand tiers, sold through wholesale (department/specialty stores, ~30% of FY26 revenue) and direct-to-consumer (own stores, concessions and digital, ~70%) across North America, Europe and Asia. The strategy of the last several years — "PELOTON"/brand-elevation, reducing promotional depth, raising average unit retail (AUR) — is the single thread running through every metric in this dossier.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Prelim rank: Q 0.829, V 0.509, M 0.672, composite 0.670 — notably, RL's Quality score is the lowest of the three names in this batch (still 83rd percentile) and its Value score is barely above the sector median (51st percentile, consistent with its higher absolute multiple). Independently verified: FY26 GAAP operating margin 14.5% (adj. 16.0%, +200bps YoY), FY26 diluted EPS GAAP $15.11/adj. $16.59 (+~30% YoY), Q1 FY27 gross margin 73.7% GAAP (+140bps YoY). This is durable, not an artefact. The improvement is broad-based (every region positive, DTC comps up low-double-digits and wholesale accelerating to mid-teens in the latest quarter — not one channel cannibalizing the other) and is explicitly attributed by management, quarter after quarter, to AUR growth and mix, i.e., pricing power from brand elevation — the same causal story for eight consecutive quarters, which is exactly what "durable" should look like. The comparatively modest Q score (vs. DECK/TPR) mainly reflects RL's lower absolute ROE-type profile and higher leverage-adjacent metrics inherent to a company that carries real estate/showroom and wholesale receivables exposure — a structural, sector-normal feature, not a warning sign.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Dividend raised 10% to $1.00/quarter ($4.00 annualized) with the Q4 FY26 release; buyback >$300m in Q1 FY27 alone (~$250m of Class A stock), authorization $1.4bn remaining. Share count continues to shrink (FY25 64.0m diluted → FY26 62.3m → Q1 FY27 trend ~61.3m per the balance-sheet-adjacent series) — a steady, unspectacular per-share tailwind. Tariffs are acknowledged every quarter but not quantified in dollars or bps in any of the four releases reviewed (language is consistently "tariffs and other product costs," offset by AUR/mix/lower cotton costs) — a real transparency gap relative to TPR's explicit bps disclosure, though RL's margin trend shows no evidence the offset is failing. Inventory: "down 5%" YoY at Q1 FY27 ($1.2bn) — a clean, well-managed level, not a build-up. No GAAP/adjusted gap concerns — the ~9–13% GAAP-to-adjusted spread each quarter is small, stable, and consistent with routine restructuring/SBC add-backs rather than aggressive normalization.

7. Valuation snapshot

Price $357.10 (2026-09-25), mid-range within its 1-year band ($299.66–$413.24) and up more than 4x from its 5-year low of $77.94 (2021, COVID trough). NTM P/E 17.96x, forward P/E 17.1x — the highest absolute multiple of the three names in this batch, consistent with the lowest Value-factor percentile (51st), but arguably earned: FY26 GAAP EPS grew ~30% YoY and the growth has been the most consistent of the three. FCF yield ≈4.1–5.8% (d4 vs prelim, modest divergence, not a conflict of substance — RL's is naturally lower than DECK's given its higher multiple). Own-history context: FY09–FY26 GAAP EPS grew from $4.01 to $15.11 (~7.9% CAGR including a 2017 trough and a 2021 COVID loss), so the current growth rate (high-teens to twenties) is well above RL's own long-run trend — the multiple is paying for a cyclical high, not the historical average, which is a fair characterization rather than a red flag given the demonstrated AUR/mix durability. Analyst sentiment is the strongest of the three: rec_mean 1.53 (buy), 89.5% strong-buy/buy share, target mean $446.70 (~25% above current price), 17 analysts. Peer set: Tapestry and Capri Holdings (accessible luxury), PVH (Calvin Klein/Tommy Hilfiger, more mid-market) and Burberry (LSE-listed, true luxury) are the natural comps; exact current multiples for CPRI/PVH/Burberry were not independently pulled this session (FMP hit a rate limit) and are flagged not available rather than estimated.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) The most consistent execution of the three names — AUR-led margin expansion for eight straight quarters, broad-based across every region and both DTC and wholesale channels simultaneously (not a zero-sum channel shift). (2) Asia/China is now the fastest-growing and re-accelerating region (Q1 FY27 China "+more than 40%"), the opposite of the China-consumer-weakness narrative affecting some luxury peers. (3) Balance sheet is net-cash, dividend was just raised 10%, and the company has now raised guidance four releases running with no sign of the streak breaking. Bear: (1) The multiple (18x NTM) and 4x-off-lows share price already reflect a lot of this good news — the lowest Value-factor percentile of the batch means less margin for disappointment. (2) Tariff cost is real (explicitly cited as a headwind every quarter) but never quantified — if AUR/mix gains ever stall, the offset mechanism is opaque and un-auditable from public disclosure alone. (3) A greater-than-40%-growth China quarter is a spectacular number that also raises the bar very high for the next comparison and increases single-region concentration risk (geopolitical/tariff-retaliation and China-consumer-cyclicality exposure) precisely where the growth is most concentrated. Note on this v3 holdover specifically: the original v3 thesis for RL is not contradicted by anything found here; if anything the AUR/margin trend has strengthened in the last four quarters relative to what v3 would have seen.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Constant-currency revenue growth falls below 5% for two consecutive quarters (from 10–14% currently).
  2. Adjusted operating margin expansion reverses (YoY compression) for two consecutive quarters, after 8 straight quarters of expansion.
  3. FY2027 guidance is cut at any point (would break the four-release raise streak — the cleanest of the three names).
  4. China/Asia growth decelerates below 10% YoY (from the current 22–40% range) — would signal the single largest current growth driver is fading.
  5. Any quantified tariff-cost disclosure (if RL ever provides one) showing a materially larger drag than peers' bps-level impact, which would retroactively make the current "offset via AUR" narrative harder to trust.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~Nov 5, 2026 (Q2 FY2027). Governance event: COO Bob Ranftl retiring effective Nov 29, 2026, duties absorbed by Halide Alagöz (promoted to Chief Operating & Product Officer, also taking AI-strategy and architecture/design leadership) — announced via 8-K filed 2026-09-03 (report date 2026-08-31), i.e., inside this dossier's review window. This reads as an orderly, internally-succeeded transition (three other executives simultaneously had responsibilities expanded in the same release), not a departure under pressure — no severance/dispute language found. No investor day identified in the window reviewed (a September-2025 investor day was referenced in passing by a search result but not independently confirmed with a primary source this session).

11. Red-flag scan

No material weakness, restatement, SEC/DOJ investigation, going-concern language, or short-seller report identified (WebSearch, 2025–2026 window). Short interest is the lowest of the three names (2.79m shares short, ~4.6% of shares outstanding). Insider selling patterns were not separately pulled this session (FMP insiderTrades tool is gated on the current plan tier) — flagged not available rather than assumed clean; the one governance event found (COO retirement) was checked directly against its primary 8-K and is clean. No litigation of note identified. This is the cleanest red-flag scan of the three names in this batch.

dossiers.SCHW:
SCHW — The Charles Schwab Corporation (F47, wave-2 diligence)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), thesis horizon 24–36 months. Reason: the largest US discount brokerage/custodian is compounding revenue and EPS at an unusually high rate (Q2 2026 revenue +21% YoY, adjusted EPS +42% YoY) with net interest margin still guided to expand further into Q4 2026 — but the named reservation is that a large share of this growth is NIM mean-reversion and post-TD-Ameritrade deleveraging, not a repeatable annual rate, plus an unresolved cash-sweep class action.

2. Business in plain English

Charles Schwab is the largest US retail brokerage/custodian by client assets, serving self-directed investors, registered investment advisors (RIA custody) and workplace-plan participants. It earns money three ways: net interest revenue on client cash swept into its affiliated bank and on securities-based/margin lending; asset-management and administration fees (proprietary funds, advisory programs); and trading revenue (commissions are largely zero for stock/ETF trades, so this is mostly options/futures and order-flow-related revenue). It completed its ~$26B acquisition of TD Ameritrade in 2020, and the last several years have been about realizing the scale/cost synergies from that integration while normalizing net interest margin after the 2022–23 rate shock.

3. Why the model liked it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q05, quality 4/5, growth 4/5, price_vs_growth 4/5): "43% eps growth and 38.8% margins as integration synergies flow through, at only 13.3x forward earnings." b1 quant: composite 0.760 (decile 8, live_rank 120 — comfortably in the model's better tier), fam_S (earnings momentum) 0.883, fam_Q 0.597, fam_M 0.599, fam_V only 0.322 (weakest family — SCHW does not screen as statistically "cheap" on the model's value factors, consistent with its ~18x trailing GAAP multiple). Durability check: the EPS growth is a blend of (a) durable organic growth — net new client assets, RIA custody share gains, buyback-driven share count reduction — and (b) a large, partly mechanical NIM-recovery/deleveraging effect: management's own Q2 2026 commentary attributes the 12bp sequential NIM expansion to "growth in margin and bank lending... reduced aggregate use of wholesale funding and lower rates paid on most funding sources" — i.e., paying down the expensive wholesale/supplemental funding taken on to bridge TD Ameritrade integration and cash-sorting outflows. That tailwind is finite; once wholesale funding is fully unwound and NIM reaches its guided ~3.25–3.30% Q4 2026 exit rate, the growth rate should decelerate toward the durable organic component.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP, USD millions except EPS; SEC 10-Q/10-K, XBRL companyfacts)

5. Guidance track record (quote the numbers; versus prior)

Schwab has raised guidance twice in 2026 on both revenue and NIM — a genuine "beat and raise," quoted rather than asserted: - At its May 2026 Investor Day, management guided full-year 2026 revenue growth of 14%–15%. - By the Q2 2026 release (2026-07-21), that was raised to 17.5%–18.5% full-year revenue growth. - Full-year 2026 net interest margin guidance was raised to a range of 3%–3.10%, with an average Q4 2026 NIM expected at 3.25%–3.30% (i.e., management is explicitly guiding to a rising exit rate, not a plateau). This is a clean, quotable, verifiable raise (source: company earnings-call commentary and release, cross-checked across two independent summaries) — but note it also means the market has already been told to expect the acceleration seen in Q1–Q2 2026; the open question for the reverse DCF (§7) is what happens once the Q4 2026 exit NIM is reached and the "reduced wholesale funding" tailwind is exhausted.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Cash conversion / FCF: per the sector playbook, operating cash flow for a bank/broker is dominated by client deposit and loan-book movements and is not a meaningful FCF signal — not used as a primary valuation input here.
  • Balance sheet (2026-06-30, 10-Q): total assets $517.3B, total liabilities $467.1B, stockholders' equity $50.1B (~9.7% equity/assets). Cash & equivalents $40.6B (elevated, consistent with the seasonal sweep-cash inflow noted above). Long-term debt + capital leases (including current maturities) $22.7B, up from $20.2B a year earlier — debt has grown, not shrunk, even as "wholesale funding" language suggests deleveraging elsewhere in the funding stack; this is a mild internal tension worth flagging as a data point to watch, not yet a red flag.
  • AFS securities unrealized losses (the SVB-era legacy issue): the accumulated unrealized loss on available-for-sale debt securities was $4.385B at 2025-09-30, improving to $3.869B (Dec'25), $3.862B (Mar'26) and $3.850B (Jun'26) — a steadily shrinking mark, now ≈7.7% of stockholders' equity (down from a materially larger share in the 2022–23 rate-shock period). This is the single most important bank-sector-specific metric per the playbook (duration mismatch risk), and the trend is favorable and improving, not deteriorating.
  • Regulatory capital: CET1 ratio 26.3% (2026-03-31) — "well in excess of the regulatory minimum of 4.5% combined with the [stress capital buffer] of 2.5%"; consolidated Tier 1 leverage ratio 8.9% (Q1'26, down from 9.3% at year-end 2025) and 8.7% (Q2'26, preliminary), well above regulatory minimums. Schwab disclosed its 2026 CCAR/stress-test results without a capital-distribution constraint noted in the sources reviewed.
  • Capital return: dividend $1.28/share annualized (1.19% yield at 2026-09-25 close); active buyback programme (not separately quantified this pass).
  • SBC: ~$126–138M/quarter in Q1 2025/Q1 2026, small relative to revenue (~2%).

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

V1 systematic valuation table (v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv) and v1_valuation.json have no SCHW row — SCHW was not in the 69-name V1 universe, so v1_verdict = null; nothing to reconcile against.

  • Price 2026-09-25 close: $99.03; market cap $171.26B; shares out 1,729.3M.
  • Trailing GAAP P/E ≈ 17.7x on TTM diluted EPS (Q3'25 1.26 + Q4'25 ~1.42 derived + Q1'26 1.37 + Q2'26 1.54 ≈ $5.59), close to the quant snapshot's 18.04x trailing figure. NTM P/E per the quant snapshot ≈ 12.6–13.3x — a large trailing-to-forward gap consistent with the market already expecting the EPS growth to continue near-term.
  • Per the sector playbook, a bank/broker-custodian is properly benchmarked on ROE-vs-COE and P/TBV rather than FCFF DCF; a full P/B build was not completed this pass (time-boxed).
  • Reverse DCF (own build, earnings-based two-stage): assuming a 10.5% cost of equity (CAPM: rf ≈4.2%, ERP 5.5%, beta ≈1.15 for a scaled, diversified brokerage/bank) and a 3% terminal growth rate after year 10, the $171.3B market cap implies roughly 5.9%/yr (TTM-NI-based) to 7.7%/yr (FY2025-NI-based) sustained 10-year net-income growth. My evidence-based base case — durable organic net-new-asset growth plus buybacks giving mid-single-digit underlying EPS growth, plus a genuine but temporary NIM-recovery tailwind through the guided Q4 2026 exit rate that then flattens — nets to ~9–11%/yr over 10 years if the near-term NIM tailwind is given even partial credit, but only ~5–7%/yr if it is excluded as non-repeatable. This straddles the implied range rather than clearing it cleanly, which is exactly why the verdict is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE: on the more optimistic base case the stock is cheap (implied below base), but on the more conservative "normalize away the funding-cost tailwind" base case it is roughly fairly priced (implied in line). valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "below" (using the mid-point base case of ~9%, above the ~6–8% implied range), with the reservation stated explicitly rather than averaged away.
  • Peers (directional only, not independently re-pulled this pass): Interactive Brokers (IBKR), LPL Financial (LPLA), Morgan Stanley's wealth-management segment — SCHW's mid-to-high-teens trailing multiple sits broadly in line with this peer set for a business of its scale and franchise quality.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Two consecutive guidance raises in 2026 (revenue growth 14–15% → 17.5–18.5%; full-year NIM raised, with a guided Q4 2026 exit NIM of 3.25–3.30%, still rising) show genuine, quoted operating momentum, not a one-off beat. 2. The AFS unrealized-loss overhang from the 2022–23 rate shock is steadily shrinking (~$4.4B → ~$3.85B over four quarters, now ~7.7% of equity) — the balance-sheet risk that dogged the stock in 2023 is measurably resolving, not worsening. 3. Regulatory capital is strong and improving in absolute dollar terms (CET1 $36.5B, Tier 1 capital $42.8B at 2026-06-30) — no capital-raise or dividend-cut risk visible in the disclosures reviewed.

Bear (3): 1. A material share of the recent EPS acceleration is attributable to NIM recovery and reduced wholesale-funding cost — management's own words — which is a mean-reversion effect with a visible end point (the guided Q4 2026 exit NIM), not a structurally repeatable growth driver; the reverse DCF is genuinely ambiguous once this is excluded. 2. Long-term debt + capital leases actually grew YoY ($20.2B → $22.7B) even as management describes "reduced wholesale funding" — worth reconciling in a deeper pass rather than treating as fully resolved. 3. An active cash-sweep class action alleges Schwab used client sweep cash economics to help finance the TD Ameritrade acquisition and takes an "outsized" share of the spread; early related cases against Schwab were dismissed, but litigation continues, and the SEC has broadened scrutiny of cash-sweep programs industry-wide (Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo have disclosed their own SEC investigations) — an unresolved legal/regulatory overhang with an uncertain financial outcome.

9. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis-invalidation triggers (measurable, would break the thesis; verbatim into summary JSON)

  1. "Full-year net interest margin fails to reach the guided 3.00%–3.10% range for FY2026, or the guided Q4 2026 exit NIM of 3.25%–3.30% is not achieved" (a miss here would confirm the NIM-recovery bull case was over-extrapolated).
  2. "Accumulated AFS unrealized loss position rises back above $5B or above 10% of stockholders' equity" (currently ~$3.85B / ~7.7%, trending down; a reversal would be a genuine balance-sheet red flag per the sector playbook).
  3. "Long-term debt + capital lease obligations rise above $28B without a disclosed, NIM-accretive rationale" (currently $22.7B, already up YoY — this is the metric to watch for the debt/wholesale-funding tension noted in §8).
  4. "The cash-sweep litigation results in a certified class and/or a disclosed reserve/settlement exceeding $500M" (scaled to SCHW's larger size versus the RJF equivalent trigger).
  5. "Consolidated Tier 1 leverage ratio falls below 7.5%" (currently 8.7–8.9%, trending down slightly QoQ — worth monitoring, not yet a breach).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-10-15 (Q3 2026, per the quant snapshot's Yahoo calendar field).
  • Q4 2026: the guided NIM exit rate of 3.25%–3.30% is the single most falsifiable near-term test of the bull case.
  • Ongoing: cash-sweep litigation docket; any further SEC scrutiny of sweep-cash programs industry-wide.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation: active putative class action(s) alleging fiduciary breach and "outsized benefits" from the cash-sweep program, including a claim that sweep-cash economics helped fund the TD Ameritrade deal; some earlier related claims against Schwab were dismissed, but litigation continues as of 2026 (source: Bloomberg Law, ThinkAdvisor, Law360, Top Class Actions, Citywire coverage, cross-checked against multiple independent outlets — not yet independently verified against SCHW's own 10-Q litigation note text in this pass, flagged as a gap).
  • Regulatory: the SEC has broadened scrutiny of cash-sweep programs industry-wide (peer disclosures at Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo); no SCHW-specific enforcement action or investigation was identified in the sources reviewed, but the sector-wide scrutiny itself is a disclosed risk.
  • Balance sheet: AFS unrealized-loss trend is improving (see §6/§8) — the opposite of a red flag, but the level (~$3.85B) is still large in absolute terms and worth tracking against future rate moves.
  • Accounting: no restatement, auditor change or going-concern language identified in this pass.
  • Insider activity: not reviewed this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as a gap for a deeper dive.

dossiers.SHW:
The Sherwin-Williams Company (SHW) — Diligence Dossier

Agent F56 | Wave 3 | As of 2026-09-25 close ($329.10) | Research only, not personal investment advice

1. Verdict

WATCH. Thesis horizon: would revisit at 12–24 months, or sooner if the market re-prices. One-sentence reason: this is a genuinely excellent, category-leading business, but the 25-Sep-2026 close prices in roughly 11.2%/yr of 10-year earnings growth against an evidence-based base case of ~8%/yr given management's own words ("no meaningful improvement in demand," guiding only ~5% adjusted EPS growth for FY2026) — a great business priced for more than the evidence supports is a WATCH, not an INCLUDE, per this program's verdict discipline.

2. Business in plain English

Sherwin-Williams makes and sells paint and coatings — mostly through its own ~5,000 company-run Paint Stores (contractors, DIY, industrial), plus consumer brands (Valspar, sold through retailers) and performance/protective coatings (industrial, marine, packaging, auto refinish). The store network and direct contractor relationships are the moat: professional painters return to the same store for credit, color-matching and same-day product, which is hard for big-box retail or e-commerce to replicate.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q13): quality 5, growth 4, price_vs_growth 3, "no disqualifying red flags," but flagged its own reservation — "net debt/EBITDA 3.1x, elevated partly from buyback funding — confirm this stays disciplined." b1 quant: fam_Q strong (pct_gp_a 0.50, pct_roe 0.84, pct_ocf_a 0.42), value percentiles weak (pct_ep 0.19, pct_fcfp 0.33 — not statistically cheap), momentum modest (pct_mom_12_1 0.58). ROE of ~65% (per d4, y_returnOnEquity) is real but is inflated by a thin/negative equity base from years of buybacks funded partly by debt (see §5) — this is partly an artefact of capital structure, not purely operating excellence, and should be read alongside net debt trends, not in isolation.

Independent leverage check vs the triage card's "3.1x": using the company's own EBITDA reconciliation tables (8-K Ex-99.1 exhibits, four most recent quarters: Q3-2025 adjusted EBITDA $1,359.0m + Q4-2025 $993.1m + Q1-2026 $998.2m + Q2-2026 $1,458.6m = $4,808.9m TTM adjusted EBITDA) against net debt of $12,072.1m − $293.5m cash = $11,778.6m, net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈ 2.45x, not 3.1x. Basis: price $329.10; forward earnings base = FY2026 guided adjusted diluted EPS midpoint $12.00; r (CAPM, rf 5.17% + beta 1.089 × ERP 4.14%) = 9.68%; terminal growth 3.0%. Solving for the growth rate that reconciles today's price to a 10-year DCF gives implied 10-year EPS growth ≈ 11.2%/yr. - Peer check: PPG Industries (closest scaled coatings peer) trades at 12.7x NTM P/E (d4) vs SHW at ~24.9x NTM P/E (d4) / ~27.4x on the FY26 GAAP guide midpoint — SHW trades at roughly double its most direct peer's multiple, which the market has historically paid for SHW's superior store-network moat and margin, but it raises the bar for what "priced in" means. - My evidence-based scenarios: bear 3% (prolonged housing/repaint stagnation, no volume recovery, "no meaningful improvement" per management persists for years) → fair value ≈ $183; base 8% (near-term guide of only ~5% EPS growth, but repaint/replacement demand is non-discretionary over a full cycle and eventually recovers, plus continued margin/buyback accretion — landing at high-single-digit EPS growth over 10 years) → fair value ≈ $261; bull 13% (housing/DIY volume recovery + raw-material deflation + continued aggressive buybacks) → fair value ≈ $375. - Implied growth (11.2%) sits above my base case (8%) → implied_vs_base = "above". Dossier valuation view: full/expensive relative to the near-term evidence, even though the long-run business quality is not in question.

7. Bull case

  1. Store-network/contractor-relationship moat is real and durable; new-account wins and share-of-wallet gains continued even in a soft macro (Q2-2026 same-store sales +4.2% against management's own description of "no meaningful improvement in demand").
  2. A U.S. housing/renovation cycle recovery (rate cuts, existing-home turnover) would flow disproportionately to Paint Stores Group volume, the highest-margin channel.
  3. FY26 guidance was genuinely raised twice in 2026 (Q1 reaffirm, Q2 raise) — management is not currently missing its own numbers.

8. Bear case

  1. Management's own language ("no meaningful improvement in demand," "little to no recovery in most end markets") describes a business growing EPS mainly through pricing, cost control and buybacks, not volume — that combination is exactly what makes an 11%/yr 10-year growth assumption hard to underwrite from here.
  2. Leverage is rising (net debt +$1.2bn in two quarters per the 10-Q) while equity keeps shrinking; a demand downturn combined with continued buyback-funded leverage would compress the safety margin.
  3. SHW trades at roughly 2x PPG's NTM multiple; any multiple compression toward peers, even with earnings on plan, would be a meaningful drawdown.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Two consecutive quarters of Paint Stores Group same-store sales growth below 2% (vs +4.2% in Q2-2026).
  2. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA (per the company's own EBITDA reconciliation) exceeds 3.0x at any quarter-end.
  3. FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut below $11.50 (the current low end) at any subsequent quarterly release.
  4. Stockholders' equity turns negative (it fell from $4.60bn to $3.85bn in H1-2026; a continuation of that trend at the same pace would approach zero within roughly 18 months).
  5. Any adverse ruling or settlement in the pending lead-pigment/lead-based-paint litigation (see §11) that results in an accrued liability being recorded (currently none is accrued).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-27 (Q3-2026). No pending M&A disclosed in the reviewed filings.

11. Red-flag scan — the one substantive finding

Lead pigment and lead-based paint litigation is real, ongoing, and not accrued. From the Q2-2026 10-Q (Note on Contingencies, Item 1 Legal Proceedings): SHW is a defendant in multiple Wisconsin "risk contribution" cases (Gibson, Valoe, Beal) alleging injury from historical lead pigment/lead-based paint. Per the filing's own dates: in the Gibson case, discovery is "scheduled to be completed by December 15, 2026"; in Valoe, the federal court on April 6, 2026 stayed all proceedings pending resolution of certain issues; Beal continues in Milwaukee County Circuit Court with cross-claims against landlord defendants. The company states it "currently [has] not accrued any amounts for the pending lead pigment and lead-based paint litigation... because the Company does not believe it is probable that a loss will occur, or the Company believes it is not possible to estimate the range of potential losses," and separately warns any adverse outcome "may have a material adverse effect." This is a decades-old, well-known overhang for SHW specifically (distinct from ordinary-course litigation) and is disclosed here with filing-sourced dates per the wave-3 mandatory rule. No auditor change, restatement or going-concern language found.

1. Verdict

WATCH, horizon 12–36 months (re-underwrite when FY2027 guidance clarifies cycle duration). Reason: a genuinely strong, structurally-improved business (NAND flash for AI-datacenter storage) riding a real, primary-source-verified demand shortage — but at a price that requires the current cycle-peak margins and cash flow to persist and then compound at a double-digit rate for a decade. That is a higher bar than even the bull case (management itself frames the shortage as lasting through 2027, not permanently), so per the mandate's own rule, a great business priced for more than it can deliver is a WATCH, not an INCLUDE — this reconciles with, and independently corroborates, V1's "excessive" verdict.

2. Business in plain English

Sandisk makes NAND flash memory chips and the SSDs/storage systems built from them, sold to hyperscale cloud providers (AI/datacenter), PC/mobile OEMs, and retail (branded flash drives/cards). It manufactures almost entirely through the "Flash Ventures" joint venture with Kioxia (~80% of its capacity comes from this JV, per its own 10-K — it does not fully control its own manufacturing). It was spun off from Western Digital on 24 February 2025 and has under two years of independent trading history.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Per v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv (as of 2026-09-25): composite percentile is the highest of the entire 45-name wave-1 batch (decile 10, quintile 5, live_rank 4) — driven by extreme quality (roe=0.727, gp_a=0.643, both per the b1 factor file, 2026-09-25 snapshot) and momentum (mom_12_1=+1,296% in the same b1 file, 2026-09-25 — the stock is up roughly 13x over the trailing 12 months per that file) scores. This is real, not a data artefact — the underlying revenue and earnings numbers below (§4, per SEC XBRL/10-K) are equally extreme and independently confirmed in SEC filings — but it is a cycle-peak reading of quality metrics that will mean-revert as NAND pricing normalizes; the model's factor definitions do not know that (own-history percentile for SNDK could not even be computed — only 5 months of trading history, per V1).

4. Last quarters since spin-off (GAAP, USD millions except EPS; fiscal year ends ~early July; source: SEC XBRL

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (10-Q/10-K through FQ4'26, filed 17 Aug 2026)

  • FCF conversion: FQ3'26 operating cash flow $3.038B, capex $45M (implied), free cash flow $2.993B on net income $3.615B — FCF ≈ 83% of NI, healthy and not propped up by working-capital drawdown in this quarter.

  • Buybacks: "$4.5 billion of stock repurchased" in FQ4'26 alone (per the earnings release) — a very large, cycle-funded capital return; shares outstanding roughly flat (146–148M) over the year despite this, implying the buyback offset significant dilution/vesting rather than shrinking the float much — worth re-checking against the next 10-K's exact weighted-average share count.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

V1 row exists (v1_valuation_table.csv): NTM P/E 7.87x (vs peer median 19.6x), verdict "excessive" (verdict_score -0.74, the second-worst in the wave-1 batch), implied 10-year growth 29.4% vs consensus FY1 growth 18.3% (from V1's FCFF-from-EBIT reverse DCF, WACC 13.56%). V1's own bear/base/bull 3-year scenario returns could not be computed ("insufficient history" — SNDK has under a year of the trading history V1's engine requires). I agree with V1's excessive verdict, and independently corroborate it two ways: (a) I re-ran a simpler FCF-yield-based reverse DCF (TTM FCF $7.72B [Yahoo] to $11.49B [D3 PIT], EV $252–274B, same 13.56% WACC, 10y fade to 3% terminal) and got implied growth of 16–21%/yr — lower than V1's 29% (methodology differences: V1 does not add back SBC to FCFF; I used reported OCF-minus-capex), but still a demanding double-digit decade-long requirement. (b) Both of our reverse DCFs use a TTM FCF base that is itself a cycle peak (FQ4'26 alone contributed more revenue than the whole of FY2025). Anchoring a 10-year growth requirement to an already-peak base, and then requiring that base to also compound at 16–29%/yr for a decade, is a materially higher bar than the AI-datacenter-shortage bull case actually claims (management's own framing is "bits on allocation... beyond 2027" — a multi-year, not decade-long, tailwind). valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent = true; implied_vs_base = "above."

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) management's own Q4 disclosure cites the NAND market growing from $300B (CY26) to $500B (CY27) with bits on allocation beyond 2027 — a primary-source, not analyst-extrapolated, claim of a multi-year shortage. (2) Zero debt, $4.76B cash, and a demonstrated ability to return $4.5B in a single quarter give real optionality. (3) No customer concentration risk, unlike the common perception of memory suppliers being hostage to 2–3 hyperscalers. Bear: (1) NAND/DRAM has historically been one of the most brutally cyclical sub-industries in semis — multi-year up-cycles have every time been followed by sharp price collapses as customers who over-ordered under allocation work down inventory and new industry capacity comes online; nothing in this cycle's structure (an industry-wide capacity response is already being discussed in trade press, not verified here) suggests immunity. (2) The stock is up ~13x in 12 months (mom_12_1) — pricing in a large amount of this cycle's persistence already. (3) The reverse DCF, on any reasonable methodology, requires the current record margins to both persist and keep compounding for a decade — a bar the bull case's own multi-year (not decade) framing does not clear.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (verbatim, copied into summary JSON)

  1. "Sequential revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive fiscal quarters (vs the +21%/+31%/+97%/+51% sequential path of the last four quarters)."
  2. "Non-GAAP gross margin falls below 60% (from the current 78.4%, FQ3'26), signalling NAND pricing normalization."
  3. "Management commentary shifts from 'bits on allocation beyond 2027' to any statement of easing allocation or customer inventory correction."
  4. "Net cash position (currently ~$4.76B, zero debt) reverses into net debt without an offsetting M&A rationale."
  5. "Quarterly guidance is met or missed (rather than blown through), signalling the extreme-beat pattern of the last four quarters has ended — itself a leading indicator the cycle is normalizing."

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 6 Nov 2026 (FQ1 FY2027, per d4 snapshot next_earnings_date). Watch specifically for the FQ2 FY2027 guide: a second consecutive quarter where the beat-margin narrows meaningfully (vs. widening every quarter through FY2026) would be the first hard evidence of cycle moderation.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Extreme earnings volatility is itself the primary flag: a $1.9B net loss to $6.9B net income swing within four quarters is disclosed and verified, not hidden, but it means every "quality" metric the model likes (ROE, margins) is a cycle-peak snapshot.
  • Manufacturing concentration: ~80% of capacity via the Flash Ventures JV with Kioxia — a single-partner structural dependency disclosed in the 10-K.
  • No customer concentration (>10%) — a genuine mitigant, verified in the 10-K, contrary to a common prior about memory-industry customer risk.
  • Spin-off complexity: as a company spun off in Feb-2025, historical comparability (pre-2025 numbers) reflects a divisional carve-out from Western Digital, not a standalone operating history — flagged as a data-quality caveat for any pre-2025 comparison, not itself a red flag.

Risk Factors (10-Q Item 1A): "no material changes" versus the FY2025 10-K. The one substantive, filing-sourced red flag is the CEO succession described in §8, which this dossier treats as a governance/key-person risk rather than an operating red flag, since operating results since the transition have been strong and the Board's succession planning was pre-existing (per the company's own 8-K statement).

S&P Global Inc. (SPGI) — Diligence Dossier

Agent F56 | Wave 3 | As of 2026-09-25 close ($403.30) | Research only, not personal investment advice

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon: 24–36 months. One-sentence reason: a duopoly ratings/index/data franchise with 50–70% segment margins, priced for growth modestly below (not above) the analyst's own base case — but FY2026 is the first year of standalone reporting after the 1-Jul-2026 Mobility spin-off, so the stub-period accounting and stranded-cost run-rate are not yet proven across a full cycle. That single, named, quantifiable transition risk is the reservation that keeps this at half weight rather than full.

2. Business in plain English

S&P Global sells things almost every large financial transaction needs: credit ratings on bonds (Ratings), the S&P 500/Dow Jones/other benchmark indices licensed to trillions of dollars of ETFs and derivatives (Indices), data/analytics/workflow tools for investment banks and asset managers (Market Intelligence), and commodity price benchmarks/analytics for oil, gas and shipping (Energy — now including "supply chain" products moved in from Market Intelligence). It earns money mostly on volume (bond issuance, AUM tracking its indices, subscriptions) rather than on assets it owns, so the businesses are extremely high-margin and capital-light. Competitive position: Ratings is effectively a duopoly with Moody's; Indices and Market Intelligence face more competition (data aggregators, in-house analytics, AI-native entrants) but have high switching costs.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

b1 factor context: ticker == SPGI, live_rank 273/… (mid-pack quant rank; not the reason it's here), quality-family score fam_Q ≈ 0.86 percentile (pct_gp_a 0.25 modest, pct_roe 0.49, pct_ocf_a 0.87 strong), value percentile low (pct_ep 0.15, pct_fcfp 0.30 — the stock is not statistically cheap on the quant screen), momentum weak (pct_mom_12_1 0.18), earnings-momentum (SUE) very strong (pct_sue 0.90). SPGI reached full diligence through the whole-index triage lane (Q05: quality 5, growth 4, price_vs_growth 3), not the systematic model. The durable part of the story — Ratings' regulatory-moat duopoly and Indices' >70% segment margin on assets it doesn't have to manufacture — is structural, not an artefact of one quarter. The weak momentum/value quant scores simply reflect that the market already prices SPGI as a quality compounder; that is evaluated directly in §7.

Long-term guidance (7–9% EPS CAGR) has been consistently affirmed across all three releases reviewed. This is a genuinely stable, three-times-affirmed guidance track, unlike ES's cut or CEG's raise — worth stating plainly rather than averaging across the batch.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Capital recycling program, not yet closed. Two large announced sales are central to the de-risking thesis the triage note credits: (a) sale of a 45% equity interest in Sempra Infrastructure Partners to affiliates of KKR — per the Q2 2026 release (6 Aug 2026), "remains on track and is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026" (i.e., by 2026-09-30, essentially concurrent with this review's data cutoff — not confirmed closed as of the sources reviewed); (b) sale of Ecogas México — approved without condition by Mexico's antitrust authority and "expected to close in August" per the same release. Neither closing was independently confirmed via a subsequent 8-K in the filings reviewed (the most recent 8-Ks found, 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-21, were unrelated hybrid/junior-subordinated-notes financings, not deal-closing announcements). Treat both sales as pending, not done, until a closing 8-K is located.

"Over $6 billion" invested in H1 2026 alone, part of a "record five-year 2026–2030 capital plan of approximately $65 billion, with 95% allocated to investments at our Texas and California utilities" (Q2 2026 release). This is the direct cause of the deeply negative reported free cash flow (−54% FCF yield per the live snapshot) — per the sector playbook, negative FCF during a rate-base build is a normal growth signal, not distress, provided it converts into an approved, earning rate base, which the Oncor/SDG&E/SoCalGas capex largely should.
  • Oncor is equity-accounted, not consolidated. The balance sheet carries "Investment in Oncor Holdings" at $19,002m (up from $17,472m at 2025-12-31) — Oncor's own growth (ERCOT hit a new all-time peak load of 91 GW in July 2026; the PUC of Texas approved a streamlined large-load interconnection framework; Oncor's new base rates took effect 1 June 2026) flows to Sempra through equity earnings and dividends, not through consolidated revenue — a structural point that matters for how "SRE growth" should be read and modelled.
  • Dividend: $0.6575/quarter declared Feb 2026 ($2.63/share annualised, +1.9% vs 2025's $2.58).

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse-DCF sense

Price 2026-09-25 close: $77.93. NTM P/E 14.4x (fy1 14.08x); P/B 1.56x; ROE (trailing) ≈6.7%; dividend yield ≈3.4%; consensus NTM EPS growth ≈+8.4% (broadly consistent with the company's own guided 7–9% long-term CAGR). No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for SRE.

Using the same justified-P/B framework as the ES dossier (Ke via CAPM: rf 4.16%, ERP 5.0%, beta 0.564 → Ke≈7.0%; earned ROE 6.7%): solving 1.56 = (0.067 − g)/(0.070 − g) gives a negative implied g (≈ −4%), which is not economically meaningful as a growth read (it mechanically falls out of a trailing ROE that sits below the CAPM cost of equity — i.e., on a pure trailing-ROE-vs-book basis the stock "shouldn't" trade above book at all, yet it does at 1.56x). That mismatch is itself informative: the market is not valuing SRE on trailing ROE/book, it is valuing it on the forward earnings power once Oncor's Texas growth, the LNG ramp (Port Arthur) and the post-recycling balance sheet show up — consistent with the company's own affirmed 7–9% long-term EPS CAGR and FY2030 outlook of $6.70–$7.50 (implying roughly 8–9%/yr growth off the FY2026 guidance midpoint, i.e., management's own guided growth is within, not below, the top of its stated range — a useful cross-check that the story is guided, not merely hoped for). On a straightforward NTM-P/E Gordon-growth solve instead of P/B (P = EPS_ntm×(1+g)/(Ke−g)): 77.93 = 5.423×(1+g)/(0.070−g) → g ≈ 5.6%, comfortably below the company's own guided 7–9% CAGR. That is the more decision-relevant read: the price is not paying up for the full guided growth rate.

Bear case: the KKR (45% Sempra Infrastructure) and Ecogas sales slip, are repriced lower, or fail to close, leaving Sempra to fund the $65bn capex plan with more debt/equity dilution than planned, while California wildfire-liability exposure (SDG&E, under AB 1054/SB 254) remains an open tail risk explicitly flagged in the company's own forward-looking-statement risk list → 3yr annualised return ≈ 0%. Base case: both sales close roughly as described (Q3 2026 for KKR, August 2026 for Ecogas), proceeds fund the capital plan without material incremental equity dilution, Oncor's ERCOT-driven growth and the guided 7–9% EPS CAGR are delivered → 3yr annualised return ≈ +11%. Bull case: ERCOT demand growth (91 GW peak, the $7bn+ transmission pipeline Oncor is positioned to build) pulls SRE's growth toward the top of, or above, the 7–9% range, and Port Arthur Phase 2 (third-party-financed) comes online on schedule → 3yr annualised return ≈ +19%.

valuation_view_vs_v1: no V1 row exists; dossier_view = cheap (NTM-P/E-implied growth ≈5.6% sits below the company's own consistently affirmed 7–9% long-term guidance) — satisfies the program's eligibility test for INCLUDE-type verdicts; held to INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE because two large, non-yet-closed asset sales are load-bearing for the balance-sheet side of the thesis and were not independently confirmed closed in this review.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Guidance has been affirmed, not cut or dramatically raised, across three consecutive quarterly releases (Q4'25, Q1'26, Q2'26) at $4.80–$5.30 adjusted EPS, with FY2027 and a first FY2030 outlook ($6.70–$7.50) also issued — an unusually stable, multi-year guided growth path for the sector. 2. Oncor's ERCOT exposure captures genuine, evidenced structural demand growth (91 GW record peak load, PUCT-endorsed multi-billion-dollar transmission buildout) that most of the peer batch does not have. 3. The capital-recycling program (KKR infrastructure stake, Ecogas) is explicitly designed to fund the $65bn five-year capex plan without proportional balance-sheet strain — a credible, disclosed plan, even though not yet fully executed.

Bear (3 points): 1. Trailing ROE (6.7%) is the lowest in the peer batch per the quant data, and reported free cash flow is deeply negative (−54% yield) — even allowing for the sector-normal "negative FCF during a capex build" explanation, this is a large, multi-year funding gap that depends on the pending asset sales closing on time and on terms. 2. Neither the KKR Sempra Infrastructure stake sale nor the Ecogas México sale was confirmed closed in the primary sources reviewed as of the 2026-09-25 cutoff, despite both being "expected" to close within weeks of that date — real execution/timing risk sits directly on the critical path of the deleveraging thesis. 3. California wildfire liability is a standing, sector-specific tail risk for SDG&E explicitly named in the company's own risk-factor language, not fully offset by the AB 1054/SB 254 wildfire fund mechanisms in every loss scenario.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable) -- what would invalidate this thesis

  1. The KKR 45% Sempra Infrastructure Partners sale does not close by 2026-12-31 (three months past the company's own "Q3 2026" target).
  2. The Ecogas México sale does not close by 2026-10-31 (two months past the company's own "expected in August" target).
  3. FY2026 adjusted EPS finishes outside the affirmed $4.80–$5.30 range.
  4. Total debt (per the consolidated balance sheet) grows faster than the approved rate base at Oncor/SDG&E/SoCalGas for two consecutive quarters, without a corresponding equity or asset-sale offset.
  5. Any SDG&E wildfire-liability claim or CPUC disallowance is disclosed that is not fully covered by the AB 1054/SB 254 wildfire fund mechanism.

1. Verdict: WATCH — thesis horizon: re-assess after a multiple reset or a full-cycle guidance test (12–24 months)

Steel Dynamics is a genuinely well-run, low-cost electric-arc-furnace steelmaker with a credible new growth leg (aluminum flat-rolled) and an excellent record of beating its own quarterly guidance, but the current 12.3x NTM P/E is being earned on an EPS run-rate ($2.78 → $3.69 → guided $5.34–5.38 over the last three quarters) that is inflated by tariff-protected steel pricing and record shipments — and the company's own analyst consensus expects revenue growth of only 0.4% next fiscal year (V1 consensus_fy1_growth), i.e., the Street itself does not expect this run-rate to keep accelerating. V1's reverse-DCF shows the price implies 14.4% 10-year revenue growth against a 9.7% delivered 5-year and 10.9% delivered 10-year CAGR — the market is paying for continuation of a cyclical peak, not for what STLD has historically compounded at. This is a "great business, priced for more than its own base rate" case, not a broken one: not now, re-open on a multiple reset to a mid-cycle earnings basis or evidence the tariff-supported pricing survives a full cycle.

2. Business in plain English

Steel Dynamics operates low-cost electric-arc-furnace (EAF) steel mills (flat-rolled and long-product/structural steel), a metals-recycling (scrap) business that supplies its own mills, a steel-fabrication business (joist/deck for non-residential construction), and — as of 2025–26 — a new aluminum flat-rolled products platform (a new mill in Columbus, Mississippi, still ramping). It sells mainly to non-residential construction, automotive, energy, industrial and (for aluminum) beverage-can/industrial/automotive customers. It makes money on the spread between steel selling prices and input costs (scrap, energy), and its competitive position rests on being one of the lowest-cost EAF operators in North America, vertically integrated into its own scrap supply, with domestic-trade-policy (Section 232-style tariff) protection currently supporting US steel pricing versus imports.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Quant snapshot (b1_live_scores.csv, as of 2026-09-25): composite 0.904 (decile 10, live_rank 48/503, not in live_top30). Family scores: Q 0.436, V 0.551, M 0.854, S 0.896 (sector-relative percentiles). ROE 17.1%, gross-profit/assets 17.6%, earnings yield 4.8%, FCF/price 2.9%, 12-1 month momentum +68.2%, SUE (earnings-surprise) 1.26 (very high — consistent with the guide-beat pattern in §5). - Momentum and earnings-surprise (M, S) are real and primary-source-confirmed, not an artefact: STLD beat its own quarterly EPS guidance in every one of the last three verifiable quarters (§5), and the sequential EPS trajectory (Q1'26 $2.78 → Q2'26 $3.69 → Q3'26 guided $5.34–5.38) is a genuine, filed-and-guided acceleration, not a one-off. - Value (V, 55th percentile) is where the "cheap" read breaks down on closer inspection. The 12.3x NTM P/E triage/b1 cite as "cheap for the trajectory" is priced off an NTM EPS run-rate (V1 input: $18.96) that annualizes the current cyclically-elevated quarter, not a mid-cycle level. V1's own reverse-DCF flags this precisely: the price implies 14.4% 10-year revenue growth vs 9.7%/10.9% delivered 5y/10y CAGRs and just 0.4% consensus FY1 growth — a large gap between what the price assumes and what the business has actually compounded at, or is expected to grow at, next year. FCF yield is low (TTM 0.7% per V1; 2.6% on an SBC-adjusted basis) because the aluminum build-out is consuming heavy capex even as earnings rise — earnings quality (cash conversion) is currently weaker than the EPS headline suggests. - Quality (Q, 44th percentile) is unremarkable on the model's own metrics (leverage, accruals, asset growth) — consistent with a business mid-way through a large capex cycle (Columbus, MS aluminum mill), not with the "record shipments, record profitability" framing alone.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Cash conversion is the weak link relative to the EPS headline. TTM FCF (OCF − capex) is $955.6m against TTM net income of $1,607m (V1 inputs) — FCF/NI ≈ 59%, and TTM FCF yield on EV is just 0.7% (V1), because TTM capex ($616m) and the aluminum ramp are consuming most of operating cash flow. This is a genuine, primary-source-verified gap between "record profitability" (income-statement framing used in every release) and free cash actually available to shareholders today.
  • SBC is immaterial to dilution: ~$14m/quarter (Q2 2026) on $6.1bn quarterly revenue ≈ 0.23% of revenue.
  • Share count and capital return: weighted-average diluted shares fell from 148.96m (Q2 2025) to 144.59m (Q2 2026), a ~3.0% reduction in four quarters, funded by $200m of Q2 2026 buybacks alone (plus $901m FY2025, "over 4% of shares outstanding"). This is an orderly, long-planned internal succession (not a forced departure), but it is a leadership-continuity item worth tracking given Millett co-founded the company over 30 years ago and personally narrates every earnings release reviewed in this pass.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

V1 verdict: "excessive" (score −0.41, the worst tier), using metric NTM P/E 12.32x (41st percentile of ~14 years' own history — i.e., mid-range, not statistically cheap on a percentile basis despite looking low in absolute terms), peer median 12.47x (peer set: STLD vs NUE only, n=2 — a thin peer sample, flagged), and a reverse-DCF (FCFF, 9.19% WACC) showing the EV0 of $37.4bn implies 14.4% 10-year revenue growth, against 9.7%/10.9% delivered 5y/10y CAGR and just 0.4% consensus FY1 growth. V1's three scenario paths: bear −54.3%/yr, base −9.7%/yr, bull +52.7%/yr (3-year annualized) — a base case that is negative, and a street-flag noting "base 3y value below Street 12m low target" ($221 low vs V1's base-case $172 exit value on a 3-year view before dividends of $166, plus $6.14 cumulative dividends = $172.08). This dossier agrees with V1's "excessive" call. The mechanism (peak-cycle EPS being extrapolated into a 10-year DCF, and the multiple looking cheap only relative to itself, not to a normalized earnings level) is exactly what §3–§5 above independently document from the primary-source guidance and results: real near-term execution strength, but a price that requires the current tariff-supported pricing/margin level to persist far longer than STLD's own 5–10 year track record or the Street's own next-FY estimate would suggest. Consistent: true. Dossier view: expensive.

3-year annualised scenario returns (adopted from V1's reverse-DCF, price+dividends): bear −54.3%/yr, base −9.7%/yr, bull +52.7%/yr.

8. Bull case and bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Guidance-beat discipline: three consecutive quarters beaten by $0.10–0.25/share, and Q3 2026 guidance ($5.34–5.38) implies a further ~45% sequential EPS jump if delivered — the earnings momentum is real and filed, not promotional. 2. Aluminum diversification (Columbus, MS) is a genuine new profit pool with automotive/beverage-can qualifications already secured, reducing pure-play steel-cycle exposure over time, funded from internal cash flow without balance-sheet strain (net debt/EBITDA ~1.65x). 3. Low leverage and consistent capital return (buybacks + 6% dividend increase) give the balance sheet real flexibility to weather a steel-price downturn without cutting the dividend.

Bear (3 points): 1. Consensus itself models only 0.4% revenue growth next FY (V1) — the Street does not expect the current pricing tailwind to compound further, directly contradicting the "cheap relative to growth" framing in the triage note. 2. Tariff-dependent pricing (flagged by triage) is a trade-policy variable, not a structural moat; V1's bear scenario (−10.8% revenue growth, margin compressing to 2.3%, implying a −54%/yr 3-year return) shows how violently this business can reprice if scrap costs rise or import protection is rolled back. 3. TTM free-cash-flow yield of just 0.7–2.6% (SBC-adjusted) means the "record profitability" is not yet translating into distributable cash at a rate that supports the current EV, while the aluminum ramp still carries multi-year commissioning risk (second CASH line not expected until 2027).

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  2. Section 232/import-tariff protection on steel is materially reduced or removed (the specific trade-policy risk both triage and V1's bear case flag).
  3. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x (from ~1.65x now) as aluminum capex continues.
  4. The Columbus, MS aluminum platform fails to reach management's own stated qualification/ramp milestones (e.g., second CASH line not operating by end-2027) after $3bn+ invested.
  5. FY2027 guidance (first given under new CEO Theresa Wagler, effective 1 Jan 2027) shows a step-down in capital-return pace (buybacks or dividend growth) versus the FY2025–26 run-rate.

dossiers.STX:
STX — Seagate Technology Holdings plc

1. Verdict

WATCH — thesis horizon 12–24 months. Seagate's nearline-HDD business is genuinely sold out, guidance has beaten by wide margins for three straight quarters, and the balance sheet is being repaired fast — but the 25-Sep-2026 close of $916.83 (mkt cap $208.4bn) already prices in a level of sustained growth this business has never delivered over a full cycle, and the stock's own 5-year history (a >90% peak-to-trough round trip in 2021–2023) shows how quickly HDD sentiment can reverse. This is a "great business, priced for more than it can deliver" case, not a "don't own it" case: revisit after the next 1–2 prints if nearline pricing and hyperscaler capex commentary confirm durability.

2. Business in plain English

Seagate makes mass-capacity (nearline) hard disk drives — the spinning-magnetic-media storage that hyperscale cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Google, Meta, etc.) buy in bulk to store the exabytes of data that AI training and inference generate, plus a smaller consumer/enterprise storage tail. It is one of only two scaled global HDD makers left (with Western Digital); Toshiba is a distant third. It makes money by selling drives at a price per terabyte that scales with each new recording-technology generation (now HAMR/Mozaic platform), so revenue growth comes from a mix of unit volume and $/TB pricing. Its moat is the extreme capital and IP barriers to building a competitive HDD business from scratch (three players worldwide, unchanged in a decade) plus multi-year hyperscaler qualification cycles.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores: composite 0.824544 (decile 9, quintile 5, live_rank 87/~2,300). Family drivers: Momentum (fam_M≈0.94) and Earnings momentum/SUE (fam_S≈0.83) are very high — both real and corroborated below. Value (fam_V≈0.07) is the lowest of the four families (pct_ep 0.24, pct_fcfp 0.20, pct_bp 0.07 — i.e. cheap on almost no value metric), which the model itself is telling you: this is a momentum/earnings-revision name, not a value name. Quality (fam_Q≈0.68) is respectable (pct_ocf_a 0.93) but pct_roe is only 0.98th-percentile-adjacent — actually very high (0.98) because ROE is inflated by a small, recently-rebuilt equity base after years of losses and buybacks, which mechanically overstates ROE quality. Durability judgement: the earnings momentum is durable so far (three consecutive large beat-and-raises, corroborated by primary filings, §4–5) but its magnitude — 25%+ sequential EPS growth guided into FQ1 FY27 — is an artefact of a capacity-constrained upcycle, not a repeatable structural growth rate; HDD has a 20+ year history of exactly this kind of overshoot-then-correction cycle.

4. Last two years of results (SEC EDGAR XBRL, CIK 0001137789; fiscal year ends ~late June/early July)

Three consecutive guide-and-beat quarters, each beat by a wide margin on both lines — a genuinely strong track record of either management conservatism or a demand environment still outrunning forecasts (probably both). The FQ1 FY27 guide of $7.30 non-GAAP EPS implies another ~28% sequential increase off FQ4 FY26's $5.71 — an extraordinary ask that, if also beaten, would extend an already unusual run; if merely met, it would still represent deceleration in the beat-margin (from ~10–14% to ~0%), which is itself information the market will react to.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

FCF conversion (FY26 FCF/GAAP NI): $3.1bn / $3.184bn = 97% — excellent, no adjusted-vs-GAAP earnings-quality gap of concern. Total debt reduced $1.4bn during FY26 to $3.6bn; cash $1.7bn (net debt ≈$1.9bn). 227.4M ordinary shares outstanding. FY26 dividend $2.94/share ($649m paid); repurchases modest ($176m) — capital return is currently debt-paydown-led, not buyback-led, which is the conservative, credit-friendly choice given the export-control liability below. Capital structure includes Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2028 (dilutive impact called out in every quarter's own guidance language) — a real, disclosed dilution overhang, not hidden. Data-quality note (data conflict): the Yahoo-sourced d4 snapshot's trailing freeCashflow field ($1.94bn) and fcf_yield (0.93%) are stale relative to the FY26 10-K/press-release FCF of $3.1bn (yield ≈1.49% on 25-Sep mkt cap) — a ~60% understatement; anyone using the raw quant snapshot without cross-checking primary filings would materially misprice this name.

7. Valuation snapshot — no V1 row exists for STX; independent reverse DCF

d4 snapshot: NTM P/E ≈22.6x, TTM P/E ≈66.1x (the gap itself shows earnings catching up to a price set months ago), FCF yield ≈1.5% (corrected, see §6). Reverse DCF (own build, FCFF-style, 10-year fade to 3% terminal growth): using FY26's record $3.1bn FCF as the base, EV ≈$210.3bn (mkt cap $208.4bn + net debt $1.9bn), and a WACC of 9–10% (reasonable for a cyclical hardware name, beta materially >1), the price requires sustained FCF growth of ~21–24% per year for a full decade before decaying to a 3% terminal rate. For context: Seagate's FY22→FY24 FCF was negative-to-breakeven in multiple quarters (a real down-cycle only 2–3 years ago), and its 10-year revenue CAGR pre-AI-cycle was low-single-digit. Asking a mature, three-player, capital-intensive hardware oligopoly to compound FCF at ~22%/yr for ten years — quadrupling FCF roughly every 3.3 years — is a very high bar; it requires the current AI-driven nearline shortage to be a permanent step-change in the addressable market, not a cyclical upcycle. No V1 row exists for STX in v1_valuation_table.csv; v1_verdict is therefore null and this reverse DCF is independently built, using the same reverse-DCF logic V1 applies to other names (see ALB dossier for a worked comparison of that method's sensitivities). Own-history performance graph (10-K, Item 5): $100 invested 2 Jul 2021 → $1,093.96 by 3 Jul 2026 (+994%) vs S&P 500's $187.57 (+87.6%) over the same window — a re-rating of this magnitude, on a historically cyclical business, is itself a caution flag for the next 3 years, independent of the operating momentum being real.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): (1) AI training/inference data growth structurally raises the exabyte-per-dollar demand curve for nearline storage in a way that is not just a cyclical restock — hyperscalers have publicly signalled multi-year capacity plans; (2) HAMR/Mozaic technology transition gives Seagate a genuine areal-density/cost lead versus WDC for several more product generations, supporting continued pricing power ($25–30/TB nearline pricing per the triage screen); (3) balance sheet discipline (debt down $1.4bn in FY26) de-risks the equity story even if growth decelerates.

Bear (3 points): (1) HDD is a duopoly with a 20-year history of severe boom-bust cycles (STX went from ~$120 in 2021 to ~$35–55 in 2022–2023 on a unit-demand air-pocket) — a repeat on any hyperscaler capex pause would be brutal given today's much higher starting multiple; (2) the reverse DCF implies growth well beyond any historical precedent for this business, meaning the stock has very little margin of safety if guidance merely meets rather than beats; (3) the unresolved BIS export-control settlement (below) carries real tail risk — failure to comply could lift the suspended denial order and restrict Seagate's ability to export products at all.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Guidance beat-margin compresses to <3% (vs the ~4–14% beats of the last three quarters) for two consecutive quarters — the first sign the upcycle is normalizing.
  2. Sequential revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (vs the +7–24% sequential growth of the last four quarters).
  3. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x (FY26 exit: debt $3.6bn, cash $1.7bn, EBITDA run-rate ~$4.5–5.0bn implies currently well under 0.5x — a reversal would signal capital-allocation or demand stress).
  4. Any BIS finding of non-compliance with the April 2023 Settlement Agreement, which could lift the suspension of the denial order (see §11) — an existential, not incremental, risk if triggered.
  5. Nearline $/TB pricing (company-disclosed or via WDC's read-across) declines quarter-over-quarter — the clearest, earliest signal that the "sold out through 2027" thesis is cracking.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-10-27/28 (FQ1 FY27; guided $4.10bn revenue / $7.30 non-GAAP EPS). Quarterly dividend ($0.74/share) paid 2026-10-07 to holders of record 2026-09-24. Securities-litigation final settlement approval hearing: 2026-11-17 (see §11). No pending M&A/index events identified.

11. Red-flag scan (primary source: FY2026 10-K, Item 3/Note 12; filed 2026-08-04)

  • BIS export-control settlement (material, ongoing): on 18 Apr 2023 Seagate's subsidiaries settled with the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security over sales of HDDs to Huawei between Aug 2020–Sep 2021. Agreed to pay $300 million in quarterly $15 million installments over five years from 31 Oct 2023 (i.e. through ~2028) plus three compliance audits (two completed). A denial order is suspended, waived only after 5 years of full compliance. As of 3 Jul 2026: $120 million remains accrued ($45m current + $75m non-current); $75m was paid in FY26. Non-compliance risk is explicitly disclosed as potentially triggering loss of the suspension.
  • Securities class action (In re Seagate Technology Holdings plc Securities Litigation, N.D. Cal.): class period 14 Sep 2020–19 Apr 2023 (bookended by the BIS matter), consolidated Sep 2023. Settled in principle 3 Apr 2026 for $175 million total (~$70m insurer-funded; Seagate recorded a $105 million charge). Preliminary court approval granted 7 Jul 2026; final approval hearing 17 Nov 2026.
  • Patent litigation, both directions: (i) Lambeth Magnetic Structures v. Seagate — district court found for Seagate (2022) but the Federal Circuit vacated and remanded for a new trial on 17 Sep 2025; (ii) Godo Kaisha IP Bridge 1 v. Seagate (D. Minn., 8 patents-in-suit, filed 2024) — ongoing, company says claims are without merit; (iii) Seagate is the plaintiff in an antitrust case against HDD suspension-assembly suppliers (NHK Spring et al.) — 9th Circuit revived Seagate's claims in Jan 2026 after a prior dismissal; NHK has petitioned the Supreme Court.
  • No material weakness, no going-concern language, no restatement identified in the FY2026 10-K's Item 9A or auditor's report.

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 12–24 months. 2. Business

Stanley Black & Decker sells power tools, hand tools and outdoor equipment (DEWALT, CRAFTSMAN, STANLEY, BLACK+DECKER) mainly through big-box/home-improvement retail and professional/industrial distribution — this is the Tools & Outdoor segment (~85%+ of revenue and profit). A much smaller Industrial segment (engineered fastening for autos/aerospace, infrastructure) makes up the rest. GICS labels SWK "Industrial Machinery," but the profit driver is branded, repeat-purchase durables sold through retail/pro channels — routed to fmcg-consumer.md ("Tools & Accessories") per the stock-analysis sector router, not infra-capitalgoods.md; the small Industrial segment is a secondary capital-goods-style overlay. Competitive position: #1/#2 branded power-tools franchise (DEWALT) in North America, competing with Techtronic Industries (Milwaukee/Ryobi) and Bosch.

  1. Cost programme largely done ($2.1bn run-rate achieved) plus CAM proceeds funding debt paydown — deleveraging without further heavy lifting.
  2. DEWALT/tools brand share gains in North America retail and C&I channels; adjusted gross margin has expanded for six straight quarters even before the tariff refund.
  3. Valuation trough: 14.8x NTM P/E at the 13th percentile of 13 years of history, ~10% FCF yield — meaningful margin of safety if organic growth merely stabilises.

9. Bear case

  1. ~2.5pt of margin and $0.17 of adjusted EPS in the latest quarter is a non-repeating tariff refund; strip it out and the "raise" is far smaller.
  2. Organic volumes remain weak (Q4 FY25 volume -7%; Q1 FY26 Tools & Outdoor organic -2%) — the growth story is price/tariff-refund/divestiture-gain driven, not volume-driven.
  3. FY25 guidance was cut mid-year on one bad quarter (impairment), showing the "on track" narrative is fragile; dividend payout (~80% of GAAP EPS) leaves little room if one-offs don't recur.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Tools & Outdoor organic volume negative for two more consecutive quarters.
  2. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA fails to decline from FY25 level despite CAM proceeds.
  3. Adjusted gross margin excluding the tariff-refund benefit contracts YoY.
  4. Dividend increase paused (streak at risk) or payout > 90% of adjusted EPS.
  5. Another guidance cut.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings ~2026-11-04 (Q3 FY26, per D4 snapshot). Global Cost Reduction Program formally winds down into "continuous improvement" reporting — watch for loss of the discrete savings disclosure.

12. Red-flag scan

No auditor change, restatement, or going-concern language identified in the documents reviewed. Recurring impairment/restructuring charges across 5 of the last 8 quarters (see §6) — a rolling, multi-year restructuring is a mild governance/quality flag but is consistent with the disclosed program, not concealed. Insider Form 4 pattern and litigation docket not reviewed in this pass (time-boxed); flagged as an open item rather than asserted clean.

b1/V1 treat SWK's NTM P/E discount to peers as straightforwardly "attractive" (verdict score 0.75); this dossier confirms the discount is real but notes the peer set (diversified industrials) is an imperfect match and that recent EPS/margin momentum embeds two one-off items the quant screen cannot see (tariff refund, divestiture gain).

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — A well-funded, transparently-guided, statistically cheap private-label lender whose recent earnings growth has been disproportionately credit-cost- and buyback-driven rather than organic, with a plateauing NCO rate and a concentrated partner base; the valuation cushion justifies a position, but credit-cycle timing risk argues for sizing it small rather than at full conviction. Thesis horizon: 12–24 months, reassessed at every print against Section 9.

2. The Business

Synchrony is the largest US private-label/co-brand credit card issuer, originating card and installment receivables through exclusive retailer, healthcare (CareCredit) and platform partnerships rather than its own brand [2]. Economics run: yield on receivables → net interest income → Retailer Share Arrangements (RSA), a contractual profit/loss-share paid back to partners that scales with program performance — a partner-alignment tool that also caps how much credit-cycle upside SYF keeps [2,4]. Funding comes from Synchrony Bank, a federally chartered savings association (not a national bank, not an industrial loan company), regulated by the OCC, FDIC and CFPB [2]: direct retail deposits fund 93% of total deposits ($75.2B of $81.1B, FY2025-end), and deposits are 83–84% of total funding [2,4]. The five largest programs (Amazon, Lowe's, PayPal/Venmo, Sam's Club, TJX) generated 54% of FY2025 interest-and-fee income and 52% of receivables, three of them individually above 10% [2] — real concentration, addressed in Sections 8–9.

3. Why the Model Likes It

The pipeline's Quality (0.96) and Value (0.958) percentiles, driving the 0.80 composite [17], are real but partly cycle-flattered. ROE of ~21–25% and P/E of ~7.2–7.5x on trailing/NTM EPS [17,18] partly reflect a genuine low-cost, retail-funded franchise with expanding NIM (15.08%, Q2 2026, +30bp YoY [4]). But part is timing: provision fell from $1,491M (Q1 2025) to $1,146M (Q2 2025) as NCO dropped 68bp in one quarter [7], and allowance coverage has declined every quarter for five straight quarters (10.87%→10.09% [4,7]) — reserve releases have been a real EPS tailwind that is now shrinking ($163M release in Q2 2026 vs $265M a year earlier [4]). This is the nbfc.md pattern of a lender "looking cheapest right before the loss cycle turns," tempered by transparency: NCO has plateaued at ~5.4% for three straight quarters, just below, not deep inside, management's own 5.5–6.0% through-cycle target [4,14].
